config.doc: Directory where app logs are stored. Multiple directories can be specified as a comma-separated list to monitor event logs from multiple paths.

config.name: spark.history.fs.safemodeCheck.interval
config.doc: Interval between HDFS safemode checks for the event log directory

config.name: spark.history.fs.update.interval
config.doc: How often(in seconds) to reload log data from storage

config.name: spark.history.fs.cleaner.enabled
config.doc: Whether the History Server should periodically clean up event logs from storage

config.name: spark.history.fs.cleaner.interval
config.doc: When spark.history.fs.cleaner.enabled=true, specifies how often the filesystem job history cleaner checks for files to delete.

config.name: spark.history.fs.cleaner.maxAge
config.doc: When spark.history.fs.cleaner.enabled=true, history files older than this will be deleted when the filesystem history cleaner runs.

config.name: spark.history.fs.cleaner.maxNum
config.doc: The maximum number of log files in the event log directory.

config.name: spark.history.store.path
config.doc: Local directory where to cache application history information. By default this is not set, meaning all history information will be kept in memory.

config.name: spark.history.store.maxDiskUsage
config.doc: Maximum disk usage for the local directory where the cache application history information are stored.

config.name: spark.history.ui.port
config.doc: Web UI port to bind Spark History Server

config.name: spark.history.fs.inProgressOptimization.enabled
config.doc: Enable optimized handling of in-progress logs. This option may leave finished applications that fail to rename their event logs listed as in-progress.

config.name: spark.history.fs.endEventReparseChunkSize
config.doc: How many bytes to parse at the end of log files looking for the end event. This is used to speed up generation of application listings by skipping unnecessary parts of event log files. It can be disabled by setting this config to 0.

config.name: spark.history.fs.eventLog.rolling.maxFilesToRetain
config.doc: The maximum number of event log files which will be retained as non-compacted. By default, all event log files will be retained. Please set the configuration and ${EVENT_LOG_ROLLING_MAX_FILE_SIZE.key} accordingly if you want to control the overall size of event log files.

config.name: spark.history.fs.eventLog.rolling.compaction.score.threshold
config.doc: The threshold score to determine whether it's good to do the compaction or not. The compaction score is calculated in analyzing, and being compared to this value. Compaction will proceed only when the score is higher than the threshold value.

config.name: spark.history.fs.driverlog.cleaner.enabled
config.doc: Specifies whether the History Server should periodically clean up driver logs from storage.

config.name: spark.history.fs.driverlog.cleaner.interval
config.doc: When ${DRIVER_LOG_CLEANER_ENABLED.key}=true, specifies how often the filesystem driver log cleaner checks for files to delete. Files are only deleted if they are older than ${MAX_DRIVER_LOG_AGE_S.key}.

config.name: spark.history.fs.driverlog.cleaner.maxAge
config.doc: When ${DRIVER_LOG_CLEANER_ENABLED.key}=true, driver log files older than this will be deleted when the driver log cleaner runs.

config.name: spark.history.ui.acls.enable
config.doc: Specifies whether ACLs should be checked to authorize users viewing the applications in the history server. If enabled, access control checks are performed regardless of what the individual applications had set for spark.ui.acls.enable. The application owner will always have authorization to view their own application and any users specified via spark.ui.view.acls and groups specified via spark.ui.view.acls.groups when the application was run will also have authorization to view that application. If disabled, no access control checks are made for any application UIs available through the history server.

config.name: spark.history.ui.admin.acls
config.doc: Comma separated list of users that have view access to all the Spark applications in history server.

config.name: spark.history.ui.admin.acls.groups
config.doc: Comma separated list of groups that have view access to all the Spark applications in history server.

config.name: spark.history.fs.numReplayThreads
config.doc: Number of threads that will be used by history server to process event logs.

config.name: spark.history.retainedApplications
config.doc: The number of applications to retain UI data for in the cache. If this cap is exceeded, then the oldest applications will be removed from the cache. If an application is not in the cache, it will have to be loaded from disk if it is accessed from the UI.

config.name: spark.history.provider
config.doc: Name of the class implementing the application history backend.

config.name: spark.history.kerberos.enabled
config.doc: Indicates whether the history server should use kerberos to login. This is required if the history server is accessing HDFS files on a secure Hadoop cluster.

config.name: spark.history.kerberos.principal
config.doc: When ${KERBEROS_ENABLED.key}=true, specifies kerberos principal name for the History Server.

config.name: spark.history.kerberos.keytab
config.doc: When ${KERBEROS_ENABLED.key}=true, specifies location of the kerberos keytab file for the History Server.

config.name: spark.history.custom.executor.log.url
config.doc: Specifies custom spark executor log url for supporting external log service instead of using cluster managers' application log urls in the history server. Spark will support some path variables via patterns which can vary on cluster manager. Please check the documentation for your cluster manager to see which patterns are supported, if any. This configuration has no effect on a live application, it only affects the history server.

config.name: spark.history.custom.executor.log.url.applyIncompleteApplication
config.doc: Whether to apply custom executor log url, as specified by ${CUSTOM_EXECUTOR_LOG_URL.key}, to incomplete application as well. Even if this is true, this still only affects the behavior of the history server, not running spark applications.

config.name: spark.ui.liveUpdate.minFlushPeriod
config.doc: Minimum time elapsed before stale UI data is flushed. This avoids UI staleness when incoming task events are not fired frequently.

config.name: spark.metrics.appStatusSource.enabled
config.doc: Whether Dropwizard/Codahale metrics will be reported for the status of the running spark app.

config.name: spark.ui.showConsoleProgress
config.doc: When true, show the progress bar in the console.

config.name: spark.ui.enabled
config.doc: Whether to run the web UI for the Spark application.

config.name: spark.ui.port
config.doc: Port for your application's dashboard, which shows memory and workload data.

config.name: spark.ui.filters
config.doc: Comma separated list of filter class names to apply to the Spark Web UI.

config.name: spark.ui.reverseProxy
config.doc: Enable running Spark Master as reverse proxy for worker and application UIs. In this mode, Spark master will reverse proxy the worker and application UIs to enable access without requiring direct access to their hosts. Use it with caution, as worker and application UI will not be accessible directly, you will only be able to access themthrough spark master/proxy public URL. This setting affects all the workers and application UIs running in the cluster and must be set on all the workers, drivers and masters.

config.name: spark.ui.reverseProxyUrl
config.doc: This is the URL where your proxy is running. This URL is for proxy which is running in front of Spark Master. This is useful when running proxy for authentication e.g. OAuth proxy. Make sure this is a complete URL including scheme (http/https) and port to reach your proxy.

config.name: spark.ui.killEnabled
config.doc: Allows jobs and stages to be killed from the web UI.

config.name: spark.ui.threadDumpsEnabled
config.doc: Whether to show a link for executor thread dumps in Stages and Executor pages.

config.name: spark.ui.prometheus.enabled
config.doc: Expose executor metrics at /metrics/executors/prometheus. For master/worker/driver metrics, you need to configure `conf/metrics.properties`.

config.name: spark.ui.xXssProtection
config.doc: Value for HTTP X-XSS-Protection response header. The default is '0' which disables the browser's XSS Auditor. The XSS Auditor has been removed from Chrome and Edge, and was never implemented in Firefox. It can introduce side-channel vulnerabilities in browsers that still support it (Safari). Use Content-Security-Policy instead.

config.name: spark.ui.xContentTypeOptions.enabled
config.doc: Set to 'true' for setting X-Content-Type-Options HTTP response header to 'nosniff'

config.name: spark.ui.strictTransportSecurity
config.doc: Value for HTTP Strict Transport Security Response Header

config.name: spark.ui.requestHeaderSize
config.doc: Value for HTTP request header size in bytes.

config.name: spark.ui.proxyRedirectUri
config.doc: Proxy address to use when responding with HTTP redirects.

config.name: spark.ui.custom.executor.log.url
config.doc: Specifies custom spark executor log url for supporting external log service instead of using cluster managers' application log urls in the Spark UI. Spark will support some path variables via patterns which can vary on cluster manager. Please check the documentation for your cluster manager to see which patterns are supported, if any. This configuration replaces original log urls in event log, which will be also effective when accessing the application on history server. The new log urls must be permanent, otherwise you might have dead link for executor log urls.

config.name: spark.worker.resourcesFile
config.doc: Path to a file containing the resources allocated to the worker. The file should be formatted as a JSON array of ResourceAllocation objects. Only used internally in standalone mode.

config.name: spark.resources.discoveryPlugin
config.doc: Comma-separated list of class names implementingorg.apache.spark.api.resource.ResourceDiscoveryPlugin to load into the application.This is for advanced users to replace the resource discovery class with a custom implementation. Spark will try each class specified until one of them returns the resource information for that resource. It tries the discovery script last if none of the plugins return information for that resource.

config.name: spark.driver.resourcesFile
config.doc: Path to a file containing the resources allocated to the driver. The file should be formatted as a JSON array of ResourceAllocation objects. Only used internally in standalone mode.

config.name: spark.driver.cores
config.doc: Number of cores to use for the driver process, only in cluster mode.

config.name: spark.driver.memoryOverhead
config.doc: The amount of non-heap memory to be allocated per driver in cluster mode, in MiB unless otherwise specified.

config.name: spark.eventLog.buffer.kb
config.doc: Buffer size to use when writing to output streams, in KiB unless otherwise specified.

config.name: spark.eventLog.logStageExecutorMetrics
config.doc: Whether to write per-stage peaks of executor metrics (for each executor) to the event log.

config.name: spark.eventLog.gcMetrics.youngGenerationGarbageCollectors
config.doc: Names of supported young generation garbage collector. A name usually is the return of GarbageCollectorMXBean.getName. The built-in young generation garbage collectors are ${GarbageCollectionMetrics.YOUNG_GENERATION_BUILTIN_GARBAGE_COLLECTORS}

config.name: spark.eventLog.gcMetrics.oldGenerationGarbageCollectors
config.doc: Names of supported old generation garbage collector. A name usually is the return of GarbageCollectorMXBean.getName. The built-in old generation garbage collectors are ${GarbageCollectionMetrics.OLD_GENERATION_BUILTIN_GARBAGE_COLLECTORS}

config.name: spark.eventLog.rolling.enabled
config.doc: Whether rolling over event log files is enabled. If set to true, it cuts down each event log file to the configured size.

config.name: spark.eventLog.rolling.maxFileSize
config.doc: When ${EVENT_LOG_ENABLE_ROLLING.key}=true, specifies the max size of event log file to be rolled over.

config.name: spark.executor.processTreeMetrics.enabled
config.doc: Whether to collect process tree metrics (from the /proc filesystem) when collecting executor metrics.

config.name: spark.executor.metrics.pollingInterval
config.doc: How often to collect executor metrics (in milliseconds). If 0, the polling is done on executor heartbeats. If positive, the polling is done at this interval.

config.name: spark.executor.memoryOverhead
config.doc: The amount of non-heap memory to be allocated per executor, in MiB unless otherwise specified.

config.name: spark.cores.max
config.doc: When running on a standalone deploy cluster, the maximum amount of CPU cores to request for the application from across the cluster (not from each machine). If not set, the default will be `spark.deploy.defaultCores` on Spark's standalone cluster manager

config.name: spark.memory.offHeap.enabled
config.doc: If true, Spark will attempt to use off-heap memory for certain operations. If off-heap memory use is enabled, then spark.memory.offHeap.size must be positive.

config.name: spark.memory.offHeap.size
config.doc: The absolute amount of memory which can be used for off-heap allocation, in bytes unless otherwise specified. This setting has no impact on heap memory usage, so if your executors' total memory consumption must fit within some hard limit then be sure to shrink your JVM heap size accordingly. This must be set to a positive value when spark.memory.offHeap.enabled=true.

config.name: spark.memory.storageFraction
config.doc: Amount of storage memory immune to eviction, expressed as a fraction of the size of the region set aside by spark.memory.fraction. The higher this is, the less working memory may be available to execution and tasks may spill to disk more often. Leaving this at the default value is recommended.

config.name: spark.memory.fraction
config.doc: Fraction of (heap space - 300MB) used for execution and storage. The lower this is, the more frequently spills and cached data eviction occur. The purpose of this config is to set aside memory for internal metadata, user data structures, and imprecise size estimation in the case of sparse, unusually large records. Leaving this at the default value is recommended.

config.name: spark.storage.unrollMemoryThreshold
config.doc: Initial memory to request before unrolling any block

config.name: spark.storage.replication.proactive
config.doc: Enables proactive block replication for RDD blocks. Cached RDD block replicas lost due to executor failures are replenished if there are any existing available replicas. This tries to get the replication level of the block to the initial number

config.name: spark.storage.memoryMapThreshold
config.doc: Size in bytes of a block above which Spark memory maps when reading a block from disk. This prevents Spark from memory mapping very small blocks. In general, memory mapping has high overhead for blocks close to or below the page size of the operating system.

config.name: spark.storage.cleanupFilesAfterExecutorExit
config.doc: Whether or not cleanup the files not served by the external shuffle service on executor exits.

config.name: spark.diskStore.subDirectories
config.doc: Number of subdirectories inside each path listed in spark.local.dir for hashing Block files into.

config.name: spark.block.failures.beforeLocationRefresh
config.doc: Max number of failures before this block manager refreshes the block locations from the driver.

config.name: spark.shuffle.service.db.enabled
config.doc: Whether to use db in ExternalShuffleService. Note that this only affects standalone mode.

config.name: spark.kerberos.keytab
config.doc: Location of user's keytab.

config.name: spark.kerberos.principal
config.doc: Name of the Kerberos principal.

config.name: spark.kerberos.renewal.credentials
config.doc: Which credentials to use when renewing delegation tokens for executors. Can be either 'keytab', the default, which requires a keytab to be provided, or 'ccache', which uses the local credentials cache.

config.name: spark.kerberos.access.hadoopFileSystems
config.doc: Extra Hadoop filesystem URLs for which to request delegation tokens. The filesystem that hosts fs.defaultFS does not need to be listed here.

config.name: spark.files.fetchFailure.unRegisterOutputOnHost
config.doc: Whether to un-register all the outputs on the host in condition that we receive a FetchFailure. This is set default to false, which means, we only un-register the outputs related to the exact executor(instead of the host) on a FetchFailure.

config.name: spark.scheduler.listenerbus.eventqueue.capacity
config.doc: The default capacity for event queues. Spark will try to initialize an event queue using capacity specified by `spark.scheduler.listenerbus.eventqueue.queueName.capacity` first. If it's not configured, Spark will use the default capacity specified by this config.

config.name: spark.scheduler.listenerbus.metrics.maxListenerClassesTimed
config.doc: The number of listeners that have timers to track the elapsed time ofprocessing events. If 0 is set, disables this feature. If -1 is set,it sets no limit to the number.

config.name: spark.scheduler.listenerbus.logSlowEvent
config.doc: When enabled, log the event that takes too much time to process. This helps us discover the event types that cause performance bottlenecks. The time threshold is controlled by spark.scheduler.listenerbus.logSlowEvent.threshold.

config.name: spark.scheduler.listenerbus.logSlowEvent.threshold
config.doc: The time threshold of whether a event is considered to be taking too much time to process. Log the event if ${LISTENER_BUS_LOG_SLOW_EVENT_ENABLED.key} is true.

config.name: spark.metrics.executorMetricsSource.enabled
config.doc: Whether to register the ExecutorMetrics source with the metrics system.

config.name: spark.metrics.staticSources.enabled
config.doc: Whether to register static sources with the metrics system.

config.name: spark.history.ui.maxApplications
config.doc: The number of applications to display on the history summary page. Application UIs are still available by accessing their URLs directly even if they are not displayed on the history summary page.

config.name: spark.driver.host
config.doc: Address of driver endpoints.

config.name: spark.driver.port
config.doc: Port of driver endpoints.

config.name: spark.driver.supervise
config.doc: If true, restarts the driver automatically if it fails with a non-zero exit status. Only has effect in Spark standalone mode.

config.name: spark.driver.bindAddress
config.doc: Address where to bind network listen sockets on the driver.

config.name: spark.blockManager.port
config.doc: Port to use for the block manager when a more specific setting is not provided.

config.name: spark.driver.blockManager.port
config.doc: Port to use for the block manager on the driver.

config.name: spark.files.ignoreCorruptFiles
config.doc: Whether to ignore corrupt files. If true, the Spark jobs will continue to run when encountering corrupted or non-existing files and contents that have been read will still be returned.

config.name: spark.files.ignoreMissingFiles
config.doc: Whether to ignore missing files. If true, the Spark jobs will continue to run when encountering missing files and the contents that have been read will still be returned.

config.name: spark.files.maxPartitionBytes
config.doc: The maximum number of bytes to pack into a single partition when reading files.

config.name: spark.files.openCostInBytes
config.doc: The estimated cost to open a file, measured by the number of bytes could be scanned in the same time. This is used when putting multiple files into a partition. It's better to over estimate, then the partitions with small files will be faster than partitions with bigger files.

config.name: spark.hadoopRDD.ignoreEmptySplits
config.doc: When true, HadoopRDD/NewHadoopRDD will not create partitions for empty input splits.

config.name: spark.redaction.regex
config.doc: Regex to decide which Spark configuration properties and environment variables in driver and executor environments contain sensitive information. When this regex matches a property key or value, the value is redacted from the environment UI and various logs like YARN and event logs.

config.name: spark.redaction.string.regex
config.doc: Regex to decide which parts of strings produced by Spark contain sensitive information. When this regex matches a string part, that string part is replaced by a dummy value. This is currently used to redact the output of SQL explain commands and the exit exception annotation on Kubernetes.

config.name: spark.authenticate.secret.file
config.doc: Path to a file that contains the authentication secret to use. The secret key is loaded from this path on both the driver and the executors if overrides are not set for either entity (see below). File-based secret keys are only allowed when using Kubernetes.

config.name: spark.authenticate.secret.driver.file
config.doc: Path to a file that contains the authentication secret to use. Loaded by the driver. In Kubernetes client mode it is often useful to set a different secret path for the driver vs. the executors, since the driver may not be running in a pod unlike the executors. If this is set, an accompanying secret file must be specified for the executors. The fallback configuration allows the same path to be used for both the driver and the executors when running in cluster mode. File-based secret keys are only allowed when using Kubernetes.

config.name: spark.authenticate.secret.executor.file
config.doc: Path to a file that contains the authentication secret to use. Loaded by the executors only. In Kubernetes client mode it is often useful to set a different secret path for the driver vs. the executors, since the driver may not be running in a pod unlike the executors. If this is set, an accompanying secret file must be specified for the executors. The fallback configuration allows the same path to be used for both the driver and the executors when running in cluster mode. File-based secret keys are only allowed when using Kubernetes.

config.name: spark.buffer.write.chunkSize
config.doc: The chunk size in bytes during writing out the bytes of ChunkedByteBuffer.

config.name: spark.checkpoint.compress
config.doc: Whether to compress RDD checkpoints. Generally a good idea. Compression will use spark.io.compression.codec.

config.name: spark.rdd.checkpoint.cachePreferredLocsExpireTime
config.doc: Expire time in minutes for caching preferred locations of checkpointed RDD.Caching preferred locations can relieve query loading to DFS and save the query time. The drawback is that the cached locations can be possibly outdated and lose data locality. If this config is not specified, it will not cache.

config.name: spark.shuffle.accurateBlockThreshold
config.doc: Threshold in bytes above which the size of shuffle blocks in HighlyCompressedMapStatus is accurately recorded. This helps to prevent OOM by avoiding underestimating shuffle block size when fetch shuffle blocks.

config.name: spark.shuffle.registration.timeout
config.doc: Timeout in milliseconds for registration to the external shuffle service.

config.name: spark.shuffle.registration.maxAttempts
config.doc: When we fail to register to the external shuffle service, we will retry for maxAttempts times.

config.name: spark.reducer.maxBlocksInFlightPerAddress
config.doc: This configuration limits the number of remote blocks being fetched per reduce task from a given host port. When a large number of blocks are being requested from a given address in a single fetch or simultaneously, this could crash the serving executor or Node Manager. This is especially useful to reduce the load on the Node Manager when external shuffle is enabled. You can mitigate the issue by setting it to a lower value.

config.name: spark.network.maxRemoteBlockSizeFetchToMem
config.doc: Remote block will be fetched to disk when size of the block is above this threshold in bytes. This is to avoid a giant request takes too much memory. Note this configuration will affect both shuffle fetch and block manager remote block fetch. For users who enabled external shuffle service, this feature can only work when external shuffle service is at least 2.3.0.

config.name: spark.taskMetrics.trackUpdatedBlockStatuses
config.doc: Enable tracking of updatedBlockStatuses in the TaskMetrics. Off by default since tracking the block statuses can use a lot of memory and its not used anywhere within spark.

config.name: spark.shuffle.sort.io.plugin.class
config.doc: Name of the class to use for shuffle IO.

config.name: spark.shuffle.file.buffer
config.doc: Size of the in-memory buffer for each shuffle file output stream, in KiB unless otherwise specified. These buffers reduce the number of disk seeks and system calls made in creating intermediate shuffle files.

config.name: spark.shuffle.unsafe.file.output.buffer
config.doc: (Deprecated since Spark 4.0, please use 'spark.shuffle.localDisk.file.output.buffer'.)

config.name: spark.shuffle.spill.diskWriteBufferSize
config.doc: The buffer size, in bytes, to use when writing the sorted records to an on-disk file.

config.name: spark.storage.unrollMemoryCheckPeriod
config.doc: The memory check period is used to determine how often we should check whether there is a need to request more memory when we try to unroll the given block in memory.

config.name: spark.storage.unrollMemoryGrowthFactor
config.doc: Memory to request as a multiple of the size that used to unroll the block.

config.name: spark.yarn.dist.forceDownloadSchemes
config.doc: Comma-separated list of schemes for which resources will be downloaded to the local disk prior to being added to YARN's distributed cache. For use in cases where the YARN service does not support schemes that are supported by Spark, like http, https and ftp, or jars required to be in the local YARN client's classpath. Wildcard '*' is denoted to download resources for all the schemes.

config.name: spark.extraListeners
config.doc: Class names of listeners to add to SparkContext during initialization.

config.name: spark.shuffle.spill.numElementsForceSpillThreshold
config.doc: The maximum number of elements in memory before forcing the shuffle sorter to spill. By default it's Integer.MAX_VALUE, which means we never force the sorter to spill, until we reach some limitations, like the max page size limitation for the pointer array in the sorter.

config.name: spark.shuffle.mapOutput.parallelAggregationThreshold
config.doc: Multi-thread is used when the number of mappers * shuffle partitions is greater than or equal to this threshold. Note that the actual parallelism is calculated by number of mappers * shuffle partitions / this threshold + 1, so this threshold should be positive.

config.name: spark.driver.maxResultSize
config.doc: Size limit for results.

config.name: spark.security.credentials.renewalRatio
config.doc: Ratio of the credential's expiration time when Spark should fetch new credentials.

config.name: spark.security.credentials.retryWait
config.doc: How long to wait before retrying to fetch new credentials after a failure.

config.name: spark.shuffle.compress
config.doc: Whether to compress shuffle output. Compression will use spark.io.compression.codec.

config.name: spark.shuffle.spill.compress
config.doc: Whether to compress data spilled during shuffles. Compression will use spark.io.compression.codec.

config.name: spark.shuffle.mapStatus.compression.codec
config.doc: The codec used to compress MapStatus, which is generated by ShuffleMapTask. By default, Spark provides four codecs: lz4, lzf, snappy, and zstd. You can also use fully qualified class names to specify the codec.

config.name: spark.shuffle.spill.initialMemoryThreshold
config.doc: Initial threshold for the size of a collection before we start tracking its memory usage.

config.name: spark.shuffle.spill.batchSize
config.doc: Size of object batches when reading/writing from serializers.

config.name: spark.shuffle.sort.bypassMergeThreshold
config.doc: In the sort-based shuffle manager, avoid merge-sorting data if there is no map-side aggregation and there are at most this many reduce partitions

config.name: spark.shuffle.reduceLocality.enabled
config.doc: Whether to compute locality preferences for reduce tasks

config.name: spark.shuffle.mapOutput.minSizeForBroadcast
config.doc: The size at which we use Broadcast to send the map output statuses to the executors.

config.name: spark.shuffle.detectCorrupt
config.doc: Whether to detect any corruption in fetched blocks.

config.name: spark.shuffle.detectCorrupt.useExtraMemory
config.doc: If enabled, part of a compressed/encrypted stream will be de-compressed/de-crypted by using extra memory to detect early corruption. Any IOException thrown will cause the task to be retried once and if it fails again with same exception, then FetchFailedException will be thrown to retry previous stage

config.name: spark.shuffle.sync
config.doc: Whether to force outstanding writes to disk.

config.name: spark.shuffle.unsafe.fastMergeEnabled
config.doc: Whether to perform a fast spill merge.

config.name: spark.shuffle.sort.useRadixSort
config.doc: Whether to use radix sort for sorting in-memory partition ids. Radix sort is much faster, but requires additional memory to be reserved memory as pointers are added.

config.name: spark.shuffle.minNumPartitionsToHighlyCompress
config.doc: Number of partitions to determine if MapStatus should use HighlyCompressedMapStatus

config.name: spark.shuffle.useOldFetchProtocol
config.doc: Whether to use the old protocol while doing the shuffle block fetching. It is only enabled while we need the compatibility in the scenario of new Spark version job fetching shuffle blocks from old version external shuffle service.

config.name: spark.shuffle.readHostLocalDisk
config.doc: If enabled (and `${SHUFFLE_USE_OLD_FETCH_PROTOCOL.key}` is disabled, shuffle blocks requested from those block managers which are running on the same host are read from the disk directly instead of being fetched as remote blocks over the network.

config.name: spark.storage.localDiskByExecutors.cacheSize
config.doc: The max number of executors for which the local dirs are stored. This size is both applied for the driver and both for the executors side to avoid having an unbounded store. This cache will be used to avoid the network in case of fetching disk persisted RDD blocks or shuffle blocks (when `${SHUFFLE_HOST_LOCAL_DISK_READING_ENABLED.key}` is set) from the same host.

config.name: spark.storage.memoryMapLimitForTests
config.doc: For testing only, controls the size of chunks when memory mapping a file

config.name: spark.barrier.sync.timeout
config.doc: The timeout in seconds for each barrier() call from a barrier task. If the coordinator didn't receive all the sync messages from barrier tasks within the configured time, throw a SparkException to fail all the tasks. The default value is set to 31536000(3600 * 24 * 365) so the barrier() call shall wait for one year.

config.name: spark.scheduler.blacklist.unschedulableTaskSetTimeout
config.doc: The timeout in seconds to wait to acquire a new executor and schedule a task before aborting a TaskSet which is unschedulable because of being completely blacklisted.

config.name: spark.scheduler.barrier.maxConcurrentTasksCheck.interval
config.doc: Time in seconds to wait between a max concurrent tasks check failure and the next check. A max concurrent tasks check ensures the cluster can launch more concurrent tasks than required by a barrier stage on job submitted. The check can fail in case a cluster has just started and not enough executors have registered, so we wait for a little while and try to perform the check again. If the check fails more than a configured max failure times for a job then fail current job submission. Note this config only applies to jobs that contain one or more barrier stages, we won't perform the check on non-barrier jobs.

config.name: spark.scheduler.barrier.maxConcurrentTasksCheck.maxFailures
config.doc: Number of max concurrent tasks check failures allowed before fail a job submission. A max concurrent tasks check ensures the cluster can launch more concurrent tasks than required by a barrier stage on job submitted. The check can fail in case a cluster has just started and not enough executors have registered, so we wait for a little while and try to perform the check again. If the check fails more than a configured max failure times for a job then fail current job submission. Note this config only applies to jobs that contain one or more barrier stages, we won't perform the check on non-barrier jobs.

config.name: spark.plugins
config.doc: Comma-separated list of class names implementing org.apache.spark.api.plugin.SparkPlugin to load into the application.

config.name: spark.io.compression.snappy.blockSize
config.doc: Block size in bytes used in Snappy compression, in the case when Snappy compression codec is used. Lowering this block size will also lower shuffle memory usage when Snappy is used

config.name: spark.io.compression.lz4.blockSize
config.doc: Block size in bytes used in LZ4 compression, in the case when LZ4 compressioncodec is used. Lowering this block size will also lower shuffle memory usage when LZ4 is used.

config.name: spark.io.compression.codec
config.doc: The codec used to compress internal data such as RDD partitions, event log, broadcast variables and shuffle outputs. By default, Spark provides four codecs: lz4, lzf, snappy, and zstd. You can also use fully qualified class names to specify the codec

config.name: spark.io.compression.zstd.bufferSize
config.doc: Buffer size in bytes used in Zstd compression, in the case when Zstd compression codec is used. Lowering this size will lower the shuffle memory usage when Zstd is used, but it might increase the compression cost because of excessive JNI call overhead

config.name: spark.io.compression.zstd.level
config.doc: Compression level for Zstd compression codec. Increasing the compression level will result in better compression at the expense of more CPU and memory

config.name: spark.io.warning.largeFileThreshold
config.doc: If the size in bytes of a file loaded by Spark exceeds this threshold, a warning is logged with the possible reasons.

config.name: spark.eventLog.compression.codec
config.doc: The codec used to compress event log. By default, Spark provides four codecs: lz4, lzf, snappy, and zstd. You can also use fully qualified class names to specify the codec.

config.name: spark.reducer.maxSizeInFlight
config.doc: Maximum size of map outputs to fetch simultaneously from each reduce task, in MiB unless otherwise specified. Since each output requires us to create a buffer to receive it, this represents a fixed memory overhead per reduce task, so keep it small unless you have a large amount of memory

config.name: spark.reducer.maxReqsInFlight
config.doc: This configuration limits the number of remote requests to fetch blocks at any given point. When the number of hosts in the cluster increase, it might lead to very large number of inbound connections to one or more nodes, causing the workers to fail under load. By allowing it to limit the number of fetch requests, this scenario can be mitigated

config.name: spark.broadcast.compress
config.doc: Whether to compress broadcast variables before sending them. Generally a good idea. Compression will use spark.io.compression.codec

config.name: spark.broadcast.blockSize
config.doc: Size of each piece of a block for TorrentBroadcastFactory, in KiB unless otherwise specified. Too large a value decreases parallelism during broadcast (makes it slower); however, if it is too small, BlockManager might take a performance hit

config.name: spark.broadcast.checksum
config.doc: Whether to enable checksum for broadcast. If enabled, broadcasts will include a checksum, which can help detect corrupted blocks, at the cost of computing and sending a little more data. It's possible to disable it if the network has other mechanisms to guarantee data won't be corrupted during broadcast

config.name: spark.broadcast.UDFCompressionThreshold
config.doc: The threshold at which user-defined functions (UDFs) and Python RDD commands are compressed by broadcast in bytes unless otherwise specified

config.name: spark.rdd.compress
config.doc: Whether to compress serialized RDD partitions (e.g. for StorageLevel.MEMORY_ONLY_SER in Scala or StorageLevel.MEMORY_ONLY in Python). Can save substantial space at the cost of some extra CPU time. Compression will use spark.io.compression.codec

config.name: spark.speculation.task.duration.threshold
config.doc: Task duration after which scheduler would try to speculative run the task. If provided, tasks would be speculatively run if current stage contains less tasks than or equal to the number of slots on a single executor and the task is taking longer time than the threshold. This config helps speculate stage with very few tasks. Regular speculation configs may also apply if the executor slots are large enough. E.g. tasks might be re-launched if there are enough successful runs even though the threshold hasn't been reached. The number of slots is the maximum number of concurrent tasks per executor for the stage's resource profile, computed from the executor cores and the task cpus amount (which may be fractional), or 1 when the executor cores are not known.

config.name: spark.yarn.stagingDir
config.doc: Staging directory used while submitting applications.

config.name: spark.buffer.pageSize
config.doc: The amount of memory used per page in bytes

config.name: spark.kafka.producer.cache.timeout
config.doc: The expire time to remove the unused producers.

config.name: spark.kafka.producer.cache.evictorThreadRunInterval
config.doc: The interval of time between runs of the idle evictor thread for producer pool. When non-positive, no idle evictor thread will be run.

config.name: spark.kafka.consumer.cache.capacity
config.doc: The maximum number of consumers cached. Please note it's a soft limit (check Structured Streaming Kafka integration guide for further details).

config.name: spark.kafka.consumer.cache.jmx.enable
config.doc: Enable or disable JMX for pools created with this configuration instance.

config.name: spark.kafka.consumer.cache.timeout
config.doc: The minimum amount of time a consumer may sit idle in the pool before it is eligible for eviction by the evictor. When non-positive, no consumers will be evicted from the pool due to idle time alone.

config.name: spark.kafka.consumer.cache.evictorThreadRunInterval
config.doc: The interval of time between runs of the idle evictor thread for consumer pool. When non-positive, no idle evictor thread will be run.

config.name: spark.kafka.consumer.fetchedData.cache.timeout
config.doc: The minimum amount of time a fetched data may sit idle in the pool before it is eligible for eviction by the evictor. When non-positive, no fetched data will be evicted from the pool due to idle time alone.

config.name: spark.kafka.consumer.fetchedData.cache.evictorThreadRunInterval
config.doc: The interval of time between runs of the idle evictor thread for fetched data pool. When non-positive, no idle evictor thread will be run.

config.name: spark.kubernetes.context
config.doc: The desired context from your K8S config file used to configure the K8S client for interacting with the cluster. Useful if your config file has multiple clusters or user identities defined. The client library used locates the config file via the KUBECONFIG environment variable or by defaulting to .kube/config under your home directory. If not specified then your current context is used. You can always override specific aspects of the config file provided configuration using other Spark on K8S configuration options.

config.name: spark.kubernetes.driver.master
config.doc: The internal Kubernetes master (API server) address to be used for driver to request executors or 'local[*]' for driver-only mode.

config.name: spark.kubernetes.namespace
config.doc: The namespace that will be used for running the driver and executor pods.

config.name: spark.kubernetes.container.image
config.doc: Container image to use for Spark containers. Individual container types (e.g. driver or executor) can also be configured to use different images if desired, by setting the container type-specific image name. Note that `{{SPARK_VERSION}}` is the built-in variable that will be substituted with current Spark's version.

config.name: spark.kubernetes.driver.container.image
config.doc: Container image to use for the driver. Note that `{{SPARK_VERSION}}` is the built-in variable that will be substituted with current Spark's version.

config.name: spark.kubernetes.executor.container.image
config.doc: Container image to use for the executors. Note that `{{SPARK_VERSION}}` is the built-in variable that will be substituted with current Spark's version.

config.name: spark.kubernetes.container.image.pullPolicy
config.doc: Kubernetes image pull policy. Valid values are Always, Never, and IfNotPresent.

config.name: spark.kubernetes.container.image.pullSecrets
config.doc: Comma separated list of the Kubernetes secrets used to access private image registries.

config.name: spark.kubernetes.submission.requestTimeout
config.doc: request timeout to be used in milliseconds for starting the driver

config.name: spark.kubernetes.submission.connectionTimeout
config.doc: connection timeout to be used in milliseconds for starting the driver

config.name: spark.kubernetes.driver.requestTimeout
config.doc: request timeout to be used in milliseconds for driver to request executors

config.name: spark.kubernetes.driver.connectionTimeout
config.doc: connection timeout to be used in milliseconds for driver to request executors

config.name: spark.kubernetes.driver.limit.cores
config.doc: Specify the hard cpu limit for the driver pod

config.name: spark.kubernetes.driver.request.cores
config.doc: Specify the cpu request for the driver pod

config.name: spark.kubernetes.executor.limit.cores
config.doc: Specify the hard cpu limit for each executor pod

config.name: spark.kubernetes.executor.scheduler.name
config.doc: Specify the scheduler name for each executor pod

config.name: spark.kubernetes.executor.request.cores
config.doc: Specify the cpu request for each executor pod

config.name: spark.kubernetes.driver.pod.name
config.doc: Name of the driver pod.

config.name: spark.kubernetes.executor.podNamePrefix
config.doc: Prefix to use in front of the executor pod names. It must conform the rules defined by the Kubernetes DNS Subdomain Names. The prefix will be used to generate executor pod names in the form of $podNamePrefix-exec-$id, where the `id` is a positive int value, so the length of the `podNamePrefix` needs to be <= 237(= 253 - 10 - 6).

config.name: spark.kubernetes.allocation.batch.size
config.doc: Number of pods to launch at once in each round of executor allocation.

config.name: spark.kubernetes.allocation.batch.delay
config.doc: Time to wait between each round of executor allocation.

config.name: spark.kubernetes.executor.lostCheck.maxAttempts
config.doc: Maximum number of attempts allowed for checking the reason of an executor loss before it is assumed that the executor failed.

config.name: spark.kubernetes.submission.waitAppCompletion
config.doc: In cluster mode, whether to wait for the application to finish before exiting the launcher process.

config.name: spark.kubernetes.report.interval
config.doc: Interval between reports of the current app status in cluster mode.

config.name: spark.kubernetes.executor.apiPollingInterval
config.doc: Interval between polls against the Kubernetes API server to inspect the state of executors.

config.name: spark.kubernetes.executor.eventProcessingInterval
config.doc: Interval between successive inspection of executor events sent from the Kubernetes API.

config.name: spark.kubernetes.memoryOverheadFactor
config.doc: This sets the Memory Overhead Factor that will allocate memory to non-JVM jobs which in the case of JVM tasks will default to 0.10 and 0.40 for non-JVM jobs

config.name: spark.kubernetes.pyspark.pythonVersion
config.doc: (Deprecated since Spark 3.1, please set '${PYSPARK_PYTHON.key}' and '${PYSPARK_DRIVER_PYTHON.key}' configurations or $ENV_PYSPARK_PYTHON and $ENV_PYSPARK_DRIVER_PYTHON environment variables instead.)

config.name: spark.kubernetes.kerberos.krb5.path
config.doc: Specify the local location of the krb5.conf file to be mounted on the driver and executors for Kerberos. Note: The KDC defined needs to be visible from inside the containers

config.name: spark.kubernetes.kerberos.krb5.configMapName
config.doc: Specify the name of the ConfigMap, containing the krb5.conf file, to be mounted on the driver and executors for Kerberos. Note: The KDC definedneeds to be visible from inside the containers

config.name: spark.kubernetes.hadoop.configMapName
config.doc: Specify the name of the ConfigMap, containing the HADOOP_CONF_DIR files, to be mounted on the driver and executors for custom Hadoop configuration.

config.name: spark.kubernetes.kerberos.tokenSecret.name
config.doc: Specify the name of the secret where your existing delegation tokens are stored. This removes the need for the job user to provide any keytab for launching a job

config.name: spark.kubernetes.kerberos.tokenSecret.itemKey
config.doc: Specify the item key of the data where your existing delegation tokens are stored. This removes the need for the job user to provide any keytab for launching a job

config.name: spark.kubernetes.resource.type
config.doc: This sets the resource type internally

config.name: spark.kubernetes.local.dirs.tmpfs
config.doc: If set to true then emptyDir volumes created to back SPARK_LOCAL_DIRS will have their medium set to Memory so that they will be created as tmpfs (i.e. RAM) backed volumes. This may improve performance but scratch space usage will count towards your pods memory limit so you may wish to request more memory.

config.name: spark.kubernetes.driver.podTemplateFile
config.doc: File containing a template pod spec for the driver

config.name: spark.kubernetes.executor.podTemplateFile
config.doc: File containing a template pod spec for executors

config.name: spark.kubernetes.driver.podTemplateContainerName
config.doc: container name to be used as a basis for the driver in the given pod template

config.name: spark.kubernetes.executor.podTemplateContainerName
config.doc: container name to be used as a basis for executors in the given pod template

config.name: spark.kubernetes.executor.deleteOnTermination
config.doc: If set to false then executor pods will not be deleted in case of failure or normal termination.

config.name: spark.kubernetes.dynamicAllocation.deleteGracePeriod
config.doc: How long to wait for executors to shut down gracefully before a forceful kill.

config.name: spark.kubernetes.appKillPodDeletionGracePeriod
config.doc: Time to wait for graceful deletion of Spark pods when spark-submit is used for killing an application.

config.name: spark.kubernetes.file.upload.path
config.doc: Hadoop compatible file system path where files from the local file system will be uploaded to in cluster mode.

config.name: spark.mesos.principal
config.doc: Name of the Kerberos principal to authenticate Spark to Mesos.

config.name: spark.mesos.principal.file
config.doc: The path of file which contains the name of the Kerberos principal to authenticate Spark to Mesos.

config.name: spark.mesos.secret
config.doc: The secret value to authenticate Spark to Mesos.

config.name: spark.mesos.secret.file
config.doc: The path of file which contains the secret value to authenticate Spark to Mesos.

config.name: spark.mesos.dispatcher.webui.url
config.doc: Set the Spark Mesos dispatcher webui_url for interacting with the framework. If unset it will point to Spark's internal web UI.

config.name: spark.mesos.dispatcher.historyServer.url
config.doc: Set the URL of the history server. The dispatcher will then link each driver to its entry in the history server.

config.name: spark.mesos.driver.labels
config.doc: Mesos labels to add to the driver. Labels are free-form key-value pairs. Key-value pairs should be separated by a colon, and commas used to list more than one.Ex. key:value,key2:value2

config.name: spark.mesos.driver.webui.url
config.doc: Set the Spark Mesos driver webui_url for interacting with the framework. If unset it will point to Spark's internal web UI.

config.name: spark.mesos.driver.failoverTimeout
config.doc: Amount of time in seconds that the master will wait to hear from the driver, during a temporary disconnection, before tearing down all the executors.

config.name: spark.mesos.network.name
config.doc: Attach containers to the given named network. If this job is launched in cluster mode, also launch the driver in the given named network.

config.name: spark.mesos.network.labels
config.doc: Network labels to pass to CNI plugins. This is a comma-separated list of key-value pairs, where each key-value pair has the format key:value. Example: key1:val1,key2:val2

config.name: spark.mesos.driver.constraints
config.doc: Attribute based constraints on mesos resource offers. Applied by the dispatcher when launching drivers. Default is to accept all offers with sufficient resources.

config.name: spark.mesos.coarse
config.doc: If set to true, runs over Mesos clusters in "coarse-grained" sharing mode, where Spark acquires one long-lived Mesos task on each machine. If set to false, runs over Mesos cluster in "fine-grained" sharing mode, where one Mesos task is created per Spark task.

config.name: spark.mesos.fetcherCache.enable
config.doc: If set to true, all URIs (example: `spark.executor.uri`, `spark.mesos.uris`) will be cached by the Mesos Fetcher Cache.

config.name: spark.mesos.appJar.local.resolution.mode
config.doc: Provides support for the `local:///` scheme to reference the app jar resource in cluster mode. If user uses a local resource (`local:///path/to/jar`) and the config option is not used it defaults to `host` e.g. the mesos fetcher tries to get the resource from the host's file system. If the value is unknown it prints a warning msg in the dispatcher logs and defaults to `host`. If the value is `container` then spark submit in the container will use the jar in the container's path: `/path/to/jar`.

config.name: spark.mesos.rejectOfferDuration
config.doc: Time to consider unused resources refused, serves as a fallback of `spark.mesos.rejectOfferDurationForUnmetConstraints`, `spark.mesos.rejectOfferDurationForReachedMaxCores`.

config.name: spark.mesos.rejectOfferDurationForUnmetConstraints
config.doc: Time to consider unused resources refused with unmet constraints.

config.name: spark.mesos.rejectOfferDurationForReachedMaxCores
config.doc: Time to consider unused resources refused when maximum number of cores `spark.cores.max` is reached.

config.name: spark.mesos.uris
config.doc: A comma-separated list of URIs to be downloaded to the sandbox when driver or executor is launched by Mesos. This applies to both coarse-grained and fine-grained mode.

config.name: spark.mesos.executor.home
config.doc: Set the directory in which Spark is installed on the executors in Mesos. By default, the executors will simply use the driver's Spark home directory, which may not be visible to them. Note that this is only relevant if a Spark binary package is not specified through `spark.executor.uri`.

config.name: spark.mesos.mesosExecutor.cores
config.doc: (Fine-grained mode only) Number of cores to give each Mesos executor. This does not include the cores used to run the Spark tasks. In other words, even if no Spark task is being run, each Mesos executor will occupy the number of cores configured here. The value can be a floating point number.

config.name: spark.mesos.extra.cores
config.doc: Set the extra number of cores for an executor to advertise. This does not result in more cores allocated. It instead means that an executor will "pretend" it has more cores, so that the driver will send it more tasks. Use this to increase parallelism. This setting is only used for Mesos coarse-grained mode.

config.name: spark.mesos.executor.memoryOverhead
config.doc: The amount of additional memory, specified in MiB, to be allocated per executor. By default, the overhead will be larger of either 384 or 10% of `spark.executor.memory`. If set, the final overhead will be this value.

config.name: spark.mesos.executor.docker.image
config.doc: Set the name of the docker image that the Spark executors will run in. The selected image must have Spark installed, as well as a compatible version of the Mesos library. The installed path of Spark in the image can be specified with `spark.mesos.executor.home`; the installed path of the Mesos library can be specified with `spark.executorEnv.MESOS_NATIVE_JAVA_LIBRARY`.

config.name: spark.mesos.executor.docker.forcePullImage
config.doc: Force Mesos agents to pull the image specified in `spark.mesos.executor.docker.image`. By default Mesos agents will not pull images they already have cached.

config.name: spark.mesos.executor.docker.parameters
config.doc: Set the list of custom parameters which will be passed into the `docker run` command when launching the Spark executor on Mesos using the docker containerizer. The format of this property is a list of key/value pairs which pair looks key1=value1.

config.name: spark.mesos.executor.docker.volumes
config.doc: Set the list of volumes which will be mounted into the Docker image, which was set using `spark.mesos.executor.docker.image`. The format of this property is a list of mappings following the form passed to `docker run -v`. That is they take the form: `[host_path:]container_path[:ro|:rw]`

config.name: spark.mesos.gpus.max
config.doc: Set the maximum number GPU resources to acquire for this job. Note that executors will still launch when no GPU resources are found since this configuration is just an upper limit and not a guaranteed amount.

config.name: spark.mesos.task.labels
config.doc: Set the Mesos labels to add to each task. Labels are free-form key-value pairs. Key-value pairs should be separated by a colon, and commas used to list more than one. If your label includes a colon or comma, you can escape it with a backslash. Ex. key:value,key2:a\\:b.

config.name: spark.mesos.constraints
config.doc: Attribute-based constraints on mesos resource offers. By default, all resource offers will be accepted. This setting applies only to executors. Refer to Mesos Attributes & Resources doc for more information on attributes.

config.name: spark.mesos.containerizer
config.doc: This only affects docker containers, and must be one of "docker" or "mesos". Mesos supports two types of containerizers for docker: the "docker" containerizer, and the preferred "mesos" containerizer. Read more here: http://mesos.apache.org/documentation/latest/container-image/

config.name: spark.mesos.role
config.doc: Set the role of this Spark framework for Mesos. Roles are used in Mesos for reservations and resource weight sharing.

config.name: spark.yarn.tags
config.doc: Comma-separated list of strings to pass through as YARN application tags appearing in YARN Application Reports, which can be used for filtering when querying YARN.

config.name: spark.yarn.priority
config.doc: Application priority for YARN to define pending applications ordering policy, those with higher value have a better opportunity to be activated. Currently, YARN only supports application priority when using FIFO ordering policy.

config.name: spark.yarn.am.attemptFailuresValidityInterval
config.doc: Interval after which AM failures will be considered independent and not accumulate towards the attempt count.

config.name: spark.yarn.executor.failuresValidityInterval
config.doc: Interval after which Executor failures will be considered independent and not accumulate towards the attempt count.

config.name: spark.yarn.maxAppAttempts
config.doc: Maximum number of AM attempts before failing the app.

config.name: spark.yarn.user.classpath.first
config.doc: Whether to place user jars in front of Spark's classpath.

config.name: spark.yarn.populateHadoopClasspath
config.doc: Whether to populate Hadoop classpath from `yarn.application.classpath` and `mapreduce.application.classpath` Note that if this is set to `false`, it requires a `with-Hadoop` Spark distribution that bundles Hadoop runtime or user has to provide a Hadoop installation separately. By default, for `with-hadoop` Spark distribution, this is set to `false`; for `no-hadoop` distribution, this is set to `true`.

config.name: spark.yarn.config.gatewayPath
config.doc: Root of configuration paths that is present on gateway nodes, and will be replaced with the corresponding path in cluster machines.

config.name: spark.yarn.config.replacementPath
config.doc: Path to use as a replacement for ${GATEWAY_ROOT_PATH.key} when launching processes in the YARN cluster.

config.name: spark.yarn.historyServer.allowTracking
config.doc: Allow using the History Server URL for the application as the tracking URL for the application when the Web UI is not enabled.

config.name: spark.yarn.archive
config.doc: Location of archive containing jars files with Spark classes.

config.name: spark.yarn.jars
config.doc: Location of jars containing Spark classes.

config.name: spark.yarn.preserve.staging.files
config.doc: Whether to preserve temporary files created by the job in HDFS.

config.name: spark.yarn.submit.file.replication
config.doc: Replication factor for files uploaded by Spark to HDFS.

config.name: spark.yarn.submit.waitAppCompletion
config.doc: In cluster mode, whether to wait for the application to finish before exiting the launcher process.

config.name: spark.yarn.report.interval
config.doc: Interval between reports of the current app status.

config.name: spark.yarn.clientLaunchMonitorInterval
config.doc: Interval between requests for status the client mode AM when starting the app.

config.name: spark.yarn.metrics.namespace
config.doc: The root namespace for AM metrics reporting.

config.name: spark.yarn.am.nodeLabelExpression
config.doc: Node label expression for the AM.

config.name: spark.yarn.am.finalMessageLimit
config.doc: The limit size of final diagnostic message for our ApplicationMaster to unregister from the ResourceManager.

config.name: spark.yarn.am.extraJavaOptions
config.doc: Extra Java options for the client-mode AM. `${AM_DEFAULT_JAVA_OPTIONS.key}` will be prepended to this configuration.

config.name: spark.yarn.am.extraLibraryPath
config.doc: Extra native library path for the client-mode AM.

config.name: spark.yarn.executor.nodeLabelExpression
config.doc: Node label expression for executors.

config.name: spark.yarn.unmanagedAM.enabled
config.doc: In client mode, whether to launch the Application Master service as part of the client using unmanaged am.

config.name: spark.yarn.rolledLog.includePattern
config.doc: Java Regex to filter the log files which match the defined include pattern and those log files will be aggregated in a rolling fashion.

config.name: spark.yarn.rolledLog.excludePattern
config.doc: Java Regex to filter the log files which match the defined exclude pattern and those log files will not be aggregated in a rolling fashion.

config.name: spark.sql.analyzer.maxIterations
config.doc: The max number of iterations the analyzer runs.

config.name: spark.sql.optimizer.excludedRules
config.doc: Configures a list of rules to be disabled in the optimizer, in which the rules are specified by their rule names and separated by comma. It is not guaranteed that all the rules in this configuration will eventually be excluded, as some rules are necessary for correctness. The optimizer will log the rules that have indeed been excluded.

config.name: spark.sql.optimizer.maxIterations
config.doc: The max number of iterations the optimizer runs.

config.name: spark.sql.optimizer.inSetConversionThreshold
config.doc: The threshold of set size for InSet conversion.

config.name: spark.sql.optimizer.inSetSwitchThreshold
config.doc: Configures the max set size in InSet for which Spark will generate code with switch statements. This is applicable only to bytes, shorts, ints, dates.

config.name: spark.sql.optimizer.planChangeLog.level
config.doc: Configures the log level for logging the change from the original plan to the new plan after a rule or batch is applied. The value can be 'trace', 'debug', 'info', 'warn', or 'error'. The default log level is 'trace'.

config.name: spark.sql.optimizer.planChangeLog.rules
config.doc: Configures a list of rules to be logged in the optimizer, in which the rules are specified by their rule names and separated by comma.

config.name: spark.sql.optimizer.planChangeLog.batches
config.doc: Configures a list of batches to be logged in the optimizer, in which the batches are specified by their batch names and separated by comma.

config.name: spark.sql.optimizer.dynamicPartitionPruning.enabled
config.doc: When true, we will generate predicate for partition column when it's used as join key

config.name: spark.sql.optimizer.dynamicPartitionPruning.useStats
config.doc: When true, distinct count statistics will be used for computing the data size of the partitioned table after dynamic partition pruning, in order to evaluate if it is worth adding an extra subquery as the pruning filter if broadcast reuse is not applicable.

config.name: spark.sql.optimizer.dynamicPartitionPruning.fallbackFilterRatio
config.doc: When statistics are not available or configured not to be used, this config will be used as the fallback filter ratio for computing the data size of the partitioned table after dynamic partition pruning, in order to evaluate if it is worth adding an extra subquery as the pruning filter if broadcast reuse is not applicable. This fallback ratio only applies when the filtering side has a selective predicate; a materialized filtering side without one obtains dynamic partition pruning through broadcast reuse only.

config.name: spark.sql.optimizer.dynamicPartitionPruning.reuseBroadcastOnly
config.doc: When true, dynamic partition pruning will only apply when the broadcast exchange of a broadcast hash join operation can be reused as the dynamic pruning filter.

config.name: spark.sql.inMemoryColumnarStorage.compressed
config.doc: When set to true Spark SQL will automatically select a compression codec for each column based on statistics of the data.

config.name: spark.sql.inMemoryColumnarStorage.batchSize
config.doc: Controls the size of batches for columnar caching. Larger batch sizes can improve memory utilization and compression, but risk OOMs when caching data.

config.name: spark.sql.inMemoryColumnarStorage.partitionPruning
config.doc: When true, enable partition pruning for in-memory columnar tables.

config.name: spark.sql.inMemoryTableScanStatistics.enable
config.doc: When true, enable in-memory table scan accumulators.

config.name: spark.sql.inMemoryColumnarStorage.enableVectorizedReader
config.doc: Enables vectorized reader for columnar caching.

config.name: spark.sql.columnVector.offheap.enabled
config.doc: When true, use OffHeapColumnVector in ColumnarBatch.

config.name: spark.sql.join.preferSortMergeJoin
config.doc: When true, prefer sort merge join over shuffled hash join. Sort merge join consumes less memory than shuffled hash join and it works efficiently when both join tables are large. On the other hand, shuffled hash join can improve performance (e.g., of full outer joins) when one of join tables is much smaller.

config.name: spark.sql.sort.enableRadixSort
config.doc: When true, enable use of radix sort when possible. Radix sort is much faster but requires additional memory to be reserved up-front. The memory overhead may be significant when sorting very small rows (up to 50% more in this case).

config.name: spark.sql.autoBroadcastJoinThreshold
config.doc: Configures the maximum size in bytes for a table that will be broadcast to all worker nodes when performing a join. By setting this value to -1 broadcasting can be disabled.

config.name: spark.sql.limit.scaleUpFactor
config.doc: Minimal increase rate in number of partitions between attempts when executing a take on a query. Higher values lead to more partitions read. Lower values might lead to longer execution times as more jobs will be run

config.name: spark.sql.hive.advancedPartitionPredicatePushdown.enabled
config.doc: When true, advanced partition predicate pushdown into Hive metastore is enabled.

config.name: spark.sql.shuffle.partitions
config.doc: The default number of partitions to use when shuffling data for joins or aggregations.

config.name: spark.sql.adaptive.shuffle.targetPostShuffleInputSize
config.doc: (Deprecated since Spark 3.0)

config.name: spark.sql.adaptive.enabled
config.doc: When true, enable adaptive query execution, which re-optimizes the query plan in the middle of query execution, based on accurate runtime statistics.

config.name: spark.sql.adaptive.forceApply
config.doc: Adaptive query execution is skipped when the query does not have exchanges or sub-queries. By setting this config to true (together with '${ADAPTIVE_EXECUTION_ENABLED.key}' set to true), Spark will force apply adaptive query execution for all supported queries.

config.name: spark.sql.adaptive.logLevel
config.doc: Configures the log level for adaptive execution logging of plan changes. The value can be ${VALID_LOG_LEVELS.mkString()}.

config.name: spark.sql.adaptive.advisoryPartitionSizeInBytes
config.doc: The advisory size in bytes of the shuffle partition during adaptive optimization (when ${ADAPTIVE_EXECUTION_ENABLED.key} is true). It takes effect when Spark coalesces small shuffle partitions or splits skewed shuffle partition.

config.name: spark.sql.adaptive.coalescePartitions.enabled
config.doc: When true and '${ADAPTIVE_EXECUTION_ENABLED.key}' is true, Spark will coalesce contiguous shuffle partitions according to the target size (specified by '${ADVISORY_PARTITION_SIZE_IN_BYTES.key}'), to avoid too many small tasks.

config.name: spark.sql.adaptive.coalescePartitions.minPartitionNum
config.doc: (deprecated) The suggested (not guaranteed) minimum number of shuffle partitions after coalescing. If not set, the default value is the default parallelism of the Spark cluster. This configuration only has an effect when '${ADAPTIVE_EXECUTION_ENABLED.key}' and '${COALESCE_PARTITIONS_ENABLED.key}' are both true.

config.name: spark.sql.adaptive.coalescePartitions.initialPartitionNum
config.doc: The initial number of shuffle partitions before coalescing. If not set, it equals to ${SHUFFLE_PARTITIONS.key}. This configuration only has an effect when '${ADAPTIVE_EXECUTION_ENABLED.key}' and '${COALESCE_PARTITIONS_ENABLED.key}' are both true.

config.name: spark.sql.adaptive.fetchShuffleBlocksInBatch
config.doc: Whether to fetch the contiguous shuffle blocks in batch. Instead of fetching blocks one by one, fetching contiguous shuffle blocks for the same map task in batch can reduce IO and improve performance. Note, multiple contiguous blocks exist in single fetch request only happen when '${ADAPTIVE_EXECUTION_ENABLED.key}' and '${COALESCE_PARTITIONS_ENABLED.key}' are both true. This feature also depends on a relocatable serializer, the concatenation support codec in use, the new version shuffle fetch protocol and io encryption is disabled.

config.name: spark.sql.adaptive.localShuffleReader.enabled
config.doc: When true and '${ADAPTIVE_EXECUTION_ENABLED.key}' is true, Spark tries to use local shuffle reader to read the shuffle data when the shuffle partitioning is not needed, for example, after converting sort-merge join to broadcast-hash join.

config.name: spark.sql.adaptive.skewJoin.enabled
config.doc: When true and '${ADAPTIVE_EXECUTION_ENABLED.key}' is true, Spark dynamically handles skew in shuffled join (sort-merge and shuffled hash) by splitting (and replicating if needed) skewed partitions.

config.name: spark.sql.adaptive.skewJoin.skewedPartitionFactor
config.doc: A partition is considered as skewed if its size is larger than this factor multiplying the median partition size and also larger than 'spark.sql.adaptive.skewJoin.skewedPartitionThresholdInBytes'

config.name: spark.sql.adaptive.skewJoin.skewedPartitionThresholdInBytes
config.doc: A partition is considered as skewed if its size in bytes is larger than this threshold and also larger than '${SKEW_JOIN_SKEWED_PARTITION_FACTOR.key}' multiplying the median partition size. Ideally this config should be set larger than '${ADVISORY_PARTITION_SIZE_IN_BYTES.key}'.

config.name: spark.sql.adaptive.nonEmptyPartitionRatioForBroadcastJoin
config.doc: The relation with a non-empty partition ratio lower than this config will not be considered as the build side of a broadcast-hash join in adaptive execution regardless of its size.This configuration only has an effect when '${ADAPTIVE_EXECUTION_ENABLED.key}' is true.

config.name: spark.sql.subexpressionElimination.enabled
config.doc: When true, common subexpressions will be eliminated.

config.name: spark.sql.caseSensitive
config.doc: Whether the query analyzer should be case sensitive or not. Default to case insensitive. It is highly discouraged to turn on case sensitive mode.

config.name: spark.sql.constraintPropagation.enabled
config.doc: When true, the query optimizer will infer and propagate data constraints in the query plan to optimize them. Constraint propagation can sometimes be computationally expensive for certain kinds of query plans (such as those with a large number of predicates and aliases) which might negatively impact overall runtime.

config.name: spark.sql.parser.escapedStringLiterals
config.doc: When true, string literals (including regex patterns) remain escaped in our SQL parser. The default is false since Spark 2.0. Setting it to true can restore the behavior prior to Spark 2.0.

config.name: spark.sql.sources.fileCompressionFactor
config.doc: When estimating the output data size of a table scan, multiply the file size with this factor as the estimated data size, in case the data is compressed in the file and lead to a heavily underestimated result.

config.name: spark.sql.parquet.mergeSchema
config.doc: When true, the Parquet data source merges schemas collected from all data files, otherwise the schema is picked from the summary file or a random data file if no summary file is available.

config.name: spark.sql.parquet.respectSummaryFiles
config.doc: When true, we make assumption that all part-files of Parquet are consistent with summary files and we will ignore them when merging schema. Otherwise, if this is false, which is the default, we will merge all part-files. This should be considered as expert-only option, and shouldn't be enabled before knowing what it means exactly.

config.name: spark.sql.parquet.binaryAsString
config.doc: Some other Parquet-producing systems, in particular Impala and older versions of Spark SQL, do not differentiate between binary data and strings when writing out the Parquet schema. This flag tells Spark SQL to interpret binary data as a string to provide compatibility with these systems.

config.name: spark.sql.parquet.int96AsTimestamp
config.doc: Some Parquet-producing systems, in particular Impala, store Timestamp into INT96. Spark would also store Timestamp as INT96 because we need to avoid precision lost of the nanoseconds field. This flag tells Spark SQL to interpret INT96 data as a timestamp to provide compatibility with these systems.

config.name: spark.sql.parquet.int96TimestampConversion
config.doc: This controls whether timestamp adjustments should be applied to INT96 data when converting to timestamps, for data written by Impala. This is necessary because Impala stores INT96 data with a different timezone offset than Hive & Spark.

config.name: spark.sql.parquet.outputTimestampType
config.doc: Sets which Parquet timestamp type to use when Spark writes data to Parquet files. INT96 is a non-standard but commonly used timestamp type in Parquet. TIMESTAMP_MICROS is a standard timestamp type in Parquet, which stores number of microseconds from the Unix epoch. TIMESTAMP_MILLIS is also standard, but with millisecond precision, which means Spark has to truncate the microsecond portion of its timestamp value.

config.name: spark.sql.parquet.compression.codec
config.doc: Sets the compression codec used when writing Parquet files. If either `compression` or `parquet.compression` is specified in the table-specific options/properties, the precedence would be `compression`, `parquet.compression`, `spark.sql.parquet.compression.codec`. Acceptable values include: none, uncompressed, snappy, gzip, lzo, brotli, lz4, lz4_raw, zstd.

config.name: spark.sql.parquet.filterPushdown
config.doc: Enables Parquet filter push-down optimization when set to true.

config.name: spark.sql.parquet.filterPushdown.date
config.doc: If true, enables Parquet filter push-down optimization for Date. This configuration only has an effect when '${PARQUET_FILTER_PUSHDOWN_ENABLED.key}' is enabled.

config.name: spark.sql.parquet.filterPushdown.timestamp
config.doc: If true, enables Parquet filter push-down optimization for Timestamp. This configuration only has an effect when '${PARQUET_FILTER_PUSHDOWN_ENABLED.key}' is enabled and Timestamp stored as TIMESTAMP_MICROS or TIMESTAMP_MILLIS type.

config.name: spark.sql.parquet.filterPushdown.decimal
config.doc: If true, enables Parquet filter push-down optimization for Decimal. This configuration only has an effect when '${PARQUET_FILTER_PUSHDOWN_ENABLED.key}' is enabled.

config.name: spark.sql.parquet.filterPushdown.string.startsWith
config.doc: If true, enables Parquet filter push-down optimization for string startsWith function. This configuration only has an effect when '${PARQUET_FILTER_PUSHDOWN_ENABLED.key}' is enabled.

config.name: spark.sql.parquet.pushdown.inFilterThreshold
config.doc: For IN predicate, Parquet filter will push-down a set of OR clauses if its number of values not exceeds this threshold. Otherwise, Parquet filter will push-down a value greater than or equal to its minimum value and less than or equal to its maximum value. By setting this value to 0 this feature can be disabled. This configuration only has an effect when '${PARQUET_FILTER_PUSHDOWN_ENABLED.key}' is enabled.

config.name: spark.sql.parquet.writeLegacyFormat
config.doc: If true, data will be written in a way of Spark 1.4 and earlier. For example, decimal values will be written in Apache Parquet's fixed-length byte array format, which other systems such as Apache Hive and Apache Impala use. If false, the newer format in Parquet will be used. For example, decimals will be written in int-based format. If Parquet output is intended for use with systems that do not support this newer format, set to true.

config.name: spark.sql.parquet.output.committer.class
config.doc: The output committer class used by Parquet. The specified class needs to be a subclass of org.apache.hadoop.mapreduce.OutputCommitter. Typically, it's also a subclass of org.apache.parquet.hadoop.ParquetOutputCommitter. If it is not, then metadata summaries will never be created, irrespective of the value of parquet.summary.metadata.level

config.name: spark.sql.parquet.enableVectorizedReader
config.doc: Enables vectorized parquet decoding.

config.name: spark.sql.parquet.recordLevelFilter.enabled
config.doc: If true, enables Parquet's native record-level filtering using the pushed down filters. This configuration only has an effect when '${PARQUET_FILTER_PUSHDOWN_ENABLED.key}' is enabled and the vectorized reader is not used. You can ensure the vectorized reader is not used by setting '${PARQUET_VECTORIZED_READER_ENABLED.key}' to false.

config.name: spark.sql.parquet.columnarReaderBatchSize
config.doc: The number of rows to include in a parquet vectorized reader batch. The number should be carefully chosen to minimize overhead and avoid OOMs in reading data.

config.name: spark.sql.orc.compression.codec
config.doc: Sets the compression codec used when writing ORC files. If either `compression` or `orc.compress` is specified in the table-specific options/properties, the precedence would be `compression`, `orc.compress`, `spark.sql.orc.compression.codec`. Acceptable values include: none, uncompressed, snappy, zlib, lzo, zstd, lz4, brotli.

config.name: spark.sql.orc.impl
config.doc: When native, use the native version of ORC support instead of the ORC library in Hive. It is 'hive' by default prior to Spark 2.4.

config.name: spark.sql.orc.enableVectorizedReader
config.doc: Enables vectorized orc decoding.

config.name: spark.sql.orc.columnarReaderBatchSize
config.doc: The number of rows to include in a orc vectorized reader batch. The number should be carefully chosen to minimize overhead and avoid OOMs in reading data.

config.name: spark.sql.orc.filterPushdown
config.doc: When true, enable filter pushdown for ORC files.

config.name: spark.sql.orc.mergeSchema
config.doc: When true, the Orc data source merges schemas collected from all data files, otherwise the schema is picked from a random data file.

config.name: spark.sql.hive.verifyPartitionPath
config.doc: When true, check all the partition paths under the table\'s root directory when reading data stored in HDFS. This configuration will be deprecated in the future releases and replaced by ${SPARK_IGNORE_MISSING_FILES.key}.

config.name: spark.sql.hive.metastorePartitionPruning
config.doc: When true, some predicates will be pushed down into the Hive metastore so that unmatching partitions can be eliminated earlier.

config.name: spark.sql.hive.manageFilesourcePartitions
config.doc: When true, enable metastore partition management for file source tables as well. This includes both datasource and converted Hive tables. When partition management is enabled, datasource tables store partition in the Hive metastore, and use the metastore to prune partitions during query planning when ${HIVE_METASTORE_PARTITION_PRUNING.key} is set to true.

config.name: spark.sql.hive.filesourcePartitionFileCacheSize
config.doc: When nonzero, enable caching of partition file metadata in memory. All tables share a cache that can use up to specified num bytes for file metadata. This conf only has an effect when hive filesource partition management is enabled.

config.name: spark.sql.hive.caseSensitiveInferenceMode
config.doc: Sets the action to take when a case-sensitive schema cannot be read from a Hive Serde table's properties when reading the table with Spark native data sources. Valid options include INFER_AND_SAVE (infer the case-sensitive schema from the underlying data files and write it back to the table properties), INFER_ONLY (infer the schema but don't attempt to write it to the table properties) and NEVER_INFER (the default mode-- fallback to using the case-insensitive metastore schema instead of inferring).

config.name: spark.sql.optimizer.metadataOnly
config.doc: When true, enable the metadata-only query optimization that use the table's metadata to produce the partition columns instead of table scans. It applies when all the columns scanned are partition columns and the query has an aggregate operator that satisfies distinct semantics.
