By default the optimization is disabled, and deprecated as of Spark 3.0 since it may return incorrect results when the files are empty, see also SPARK-26709. It will be removed in the future releases. If you must use, use 'SparkSessionExtensions' instead to inject it as a custom rule.

config.name: spark.sql.columnNameOfCorruptRecord
config.doc: The name of internal column for storing raw/un-parsed JSON and CSV records that fail to parse.

config.name: spark.sql.broadcastTimeout
config.doc: Timeout in seconds for the broadcast wait time in broadcast joins.

config.name: spark.sql.thriftserver.scheduler.pool
config.doc: Set a Fair Scheduler pool for a JDBC client session.

config.name: spark.sql.thriftServer.incrementalCollect
config.doc: When true, enable incremental collection for execution in Thrift Server.

config.name: spark.sql.thriftserver.ui.retainedStatements
config.doc: The number of SQL statements kept in the JDBC/ODBC web UI history.

config.name: spark.sql.thriftserver.ui.retainedSessions
config.doc: The number of SQL client sessions kept in the JDBC/ODBC web UI history.

config.name: spark.sql.sources.default
config.doc: The default data source to use in input/output.

config.name: spark.sql.hive.convertCTAS
config.doc: When true, a table created by a Hive CTAS statement (no USING clause) without specifying any storage property will be converted to a data source table, using the data source set by ${DEFAULT_DATA_SOURCE_NAME.key}.

config.name: spark.sql.hive.gatherFastStats
config.doc: When true, fast stats (number of files and total size of all files) will be gathered in parallel while repairing table partitions to avoid the sequential listing in Hive metastore.

config.name: spark.sql.sources.partitionColumnTypeInference.enabled
config.doc: When true, automatically infer the data types for partitioned columns.

config.name: spark.sql.sources.bucketing.enabled
config.doc: When false, we will treat bucketed table as normal table

config.name: spark.sql.sources.bucketing.maxBuckets
config.doc: The maximum number of buckets allowed.

config.name: spark.sql.crossJoin.enabled
config.doc: When false, we will throw an error if a query contains a cartesian product without explicit CROSS JOIN syntax.

config.name: spark.sql.orderByOrdinal
config.doc: When true, the ordinal numbers are treated as the position in the select list. When false, the ordinal numbers in order/sort by clause are ignored.

config.name: spark.sql.groupByOrdinal
config.doc: When true, the ordinal numbers in group by clauses are treated as the position in the select list. When false, the ordinal numbers are ignored.

config.name: spark.sql.groupByAliases
config.doc: When true, aliases in a select list can be used in group by clauses. When false, an analysis exception is thrown in the case.

config.name: spark.sql.sources.parallelPartitionDiscovery.threshold
config.doc: The maximum number of paths allowed for listing files at driver side. If the number of detected paths exceeds this value during partition discovery, it tries to list the files with another Spark distributed job. This configuration is effective only when using file-based sources such as Parquet, JSON and ORC.

config.name: spark.sql.sources.parallelPartitionDiscovery.parallelism
config.doc: The number of parallelism to list a collection of path recursively, Set the number to prevent file listing from generating too many tasks.

config.name: spark.sql.sources.ignoreDataLocality
config.doc: If true, Spark will not fetch the block locations for each file on listing files. This speeds up file listing, but the scheduler cannot schedule tasks to take advantage of data locality. It can be particularly useful if data is read from a remote cluster so the scheduler could never take advantage of locality anyway.

config.name: spark.sql.analyzer.failAmbiguousSelfJoin
config.doc: When true, fail the Dataset query if it contains ambiguous self-join.

config.name: spark.sql.pivotMaxValues
config.doc: When doing a pivot without specifying values for the pivot column this is the maximum number of (distinct) values that will be collected without error.

config.name: spark.sql.runSQLOnFiles
config.doc: When true, we could use `datasource`.`path` as table in SQL query.

config.name: spark.sql.codegen.wholeStage
config.doc: When true, the whole stage (of multiple operators) will be compiled into single java method.

config.name: spark.sql.codegen.useIdInClassName
config.doc: When true, embed the (whole-stage) codegen stage ID into the class name of the generated class as a suffix

config.name: spark.sql.codegen.maxFields
config.doc: The maximum number of fields (including nested fields) that will be supported before deactivating whole-stage codegen.

config.name: spark.sql.codegen.factoryMode
config.doc: This config determines the fallback behavior of several codegen generators during tests. `FALLBACK` means trying codegen first and then falling back to interpreted if any compile error happens. Disabling fallback if `CODEGEN_ONLY`. `NO_CODEGEN` skips codegen and goes interpreted path always. Note that this configuration is only for the internal usage, and NOT supposed to be set by end users.

config.name: spark.sql.codegen.fallback
config.doc: When true, (whole stage) codegen could be temporary disabled for the part of query that fail to compile generated code

config.name: spark.sql.codegen.logging.maxLines
config.doc: The maximum number of codegen lines to log when errors occur. Use -1 for unlimited.

config.name: spark.sql.codegen.hugeMethodLimit
config.doc: The maximum bytecode size of a single compiled Java function generated by whole-stage codegen. When the compiled function exceeds this threshold, the whole-stage codegen is deactivated for this subtree of the current query plan. The default value is 65535, which is the largest bytecode size possible for a valid Java method. When running on HotSpot, it may be preferable to set the value to ${CodeGenerator.DEFAULT_JVM_HUGE_METHOD_LIMIT} to match HotSpot's implementation.

config.name: spark.sql.codegen.methodSplitThreshold
config.doc: The threshold of source-code splitting in the codegen. When the number of characters in a single Java function (without comment) exceeds the threshold, the function will be automatically split to multiple smaller ones. We cannot know how many bytecode will be generated, so use the code length as metric. When running on HotSpot, a function's bytecode should not go beyond 8KB, otherwise it will not be JITted; it also should not be too small, otherwise there will be many function calls.

config.name: spark.sql.codegen.splitConsumeFuncByOperator
config.doc: When true, whole stage codegen would put the logic of consuming rows of each physical operator into individual methods, instead of a single big method. This can be used to avoid oversized function that can miss the opportunity of JIT optimization.

config.name: spark.sql.files.maxPartitionBytes
config.doc: The maximum number of bytes to pack into a single partition when reading files. This configuration is effective only when using file-based sources such as Parquet, JSON and ORC.

config.name: spark.sql.files.openCostInBytes
config.doc: The estimated cost to open a file, measured by the number of bytes could be scanned in the same time. This is used when putting multiple files into a partition. It's better to over estimated, then the partitions with small files will be faster than partitions with bigger files (which is scheduled first). This configuration is effective only when using file-based sources such as Parquet, JSON and ORC.

config.name: spark.sql.files.ignoreCorruptFiles
config.doc: Whether to ignore corrupt files. If true, the Spark jobs will continue to run when encountering corrupted files and the contents that have been read will still be returned. This configuration is effective only when using file-based sources such as Parquet, JSON and ORC.

config.name: spark.sql.files.ignoreMissingFiles
config.doc: Whether to ignore missing files. If true, the Spark jobs will continue to run when encountering missing files and the contents that have been read will still be returned. This configuration is effective only when using file-based sources such as Parquet, JSON and ORC.

config.name: spark.sql.files.maxRecordsPerFile
config.doc: Maximum number of records to write out to a single file. If this value is zero or negative, there is no limit.

config.name: spark.sql.exchange.reuse
config.doc: When true, the planner will try to find out duplicated exchanges and re-use them.

config.name: spark.sql.execution.reuseSubquery
config.doc: When true, the planner will try to find out duplicated subqueries and re-use them.

config.name: spark.sql.streaming.stateStore.providerClass
config.doc: The class used to manage state data in stateful streaming queries. This class must be a subclass of StateStoreProvider, and must have a zero-arg constructor. Note: For structured streaming, this configuration cannot be changed between query restarts from the same checkpoint location.

config.name: spark.sql.streaming.stateStore.minDeltasForSnapshot
config.doc: Minimum number of state store delta files that needs to be generated before they consolidated into snapshots.

config.name: spark.sql.streaming.flatMapGroupsWithState.stateFormatVersion
config.doc: State format version used by flatMapGroupsWithState operation in a streaming query

config.name: spark.sql.streaming.checkpointLocation
config.doc: The default location for storing checkpoint data for streaming queries.

config.name: spark.sql.streaming.forceDeleteTempCheckpointLocation
config.doc: When true, enable temporary checkpoint locations force delete.

config.name: spark.sql.streaming.minBatchesToRetain
config.doc: The minimum number of batches that must be retained and made recoverable. This also controls the lifecycle of checkpoint files: state, offset and commit log files older than this many batches are eligible for cleanup. Must be positive.

config.name: spark.sql.streaming.maxBatchesToRetainInMemory
config.doc: The maximum number of batches which will be retained in memory to avoid loading from files. The value adjusts a trade-off between memory usage vs cache miss: '2' covers both success and direct failure cases, '1' covers only success case, and '0' covers extreme case - disable cache to maximize memory size of executors.

config.name: spark.sql.streaming.aggregation.stateFormatVersion
config.doc: State format version used by streaming aggregation operations in a streaming query. State between versions are tend to be incompatible, so state format version shouldn't be modified after running.

config.name: spark.sql.streaming.stopActiveRunOnRestart
config.doc: Running multiple runs of the same streaming query concurrently is not supported. If we find a concurrent active run for a streaming query (in the same or different SparkSessions on the same cluster) and this flag is true, we will stop the old streaming query run to start the new one.

config.name: spark.sql.streaming.join.stateFormatVersion
config.doc: State format version used by streaming join operations in a streaming query. State between versions are tend to be incompatible, so state format version shouldn't be modified after running. Version 3 uses a single state store with virtual column families instead of four stores and is only supported with RocksDB. Version 4 optimizes watermark-based eviction, also using a single state store with virtual column families and only supported with RocksDB. NOTE: version 1 is DEPRECATED and should not be explicitly set by users.

config.name: spark.sql.streaming.unsupportedOperationCheck
config.doc: When true, the logical plan for streaming query will be checked for unsupported operations.

config.name: spark.sql.variable.substitute
config.doc: This enables substitution using syntax like `${var}`, `${system:var}`, and `${env:var}`.

config.name: spark.sql.codegen.aggregate.map.twolevel.enabled
config.doc: Enable two-level aggregate hash map. When enabled, records will first be inserted/looked-up at a 1st-level, small, fast map, and then fallback to a 2nd-level, larger, slower map when 1st level is full or keys cannot be found. When disabled, records go directly to the 2nd level.

config.name: spark.sql.codegen.aggregate.map.vectorized.enable
config.doc: Enable vectorized aggregate hash map. This is for testing/benchmarking only.

config.name: spark.sql.codegen.aggregate.splitAggregateFunc.enabled
config.doc: When true, the code generator would split aggregate code into individual methods instead of a single big method. This can be used to avoid oversized function that can miss the opportunity of JIT optimization.

config.name: spark.sql.view.maxNestedViewDepth
config.doc: The maximum depth of a view reference in a nested view. A nested view may reference other nested views, the dependencies are organized in a directed acyclic graph (DAG). However the DAG depth may become too large and cause unexpected behavior. This configuration puts a limit on this: when the depth of a view exceeds this value during analysis, we terminate the resolution to avoid potential errors.

config.name: spark.sql.streaming.multipleWatermarkPolicy
config.doc: Policy to calculate the global watermark value when there are multiple watermark operators in a streaming query. The default value is 'min' which chooses the minimum watermark reported across multiple operators. Other alternative value is 'max' which chooses the maximum across multiple operators. Note: This configuration cannot be changed between query restarts from the same checkpoint location.

config.name: spark.sql.objectHashAggregate.sortBased.fallbackThreshold
config.doc: In the case of ObjectHashAggregateExec, when the size of the in-memory hash map grows too large, we will fall back to sort-based aggregation. This option sets a row count threshold for the size of the hash map.

config.name: spark.sql.execution.useObjectHashAggregateExec
config.doc: Decides if we use ObjectHashAggregateExec when possible.

config.name: spark.sql.jsonGenerator.ignoreNullFields
config.doc: Whether to ignore null fields when generating JSON objects in JSON data source and JSON functions such as to_json. If false, it generates null for null fields in JSON objects.

config.name: spark.sql.streaming.fileSink.log.deletion
config.doc: Whether to delete the expired log files in file stream sink.

config.name: spark.sql.streaming.fileSink.log.compactInterval
config.doc: Number of log files after which all the previous files are compacted into the next log file.

config.name: spark.sql.streaming.fileSink.log.cleanupDelay
config.doc: How long that a file is guaranteed to be visible for all readers.

config.name: spark.sql.streaming.fileSource.log.deletion
config.doc: Whether to delete the expired log files in file stream source.

config.name: spark.sql.streaming.fileSource.log.compactInterval
config.doc: Number of log files after which all the previous files are compacted into the next log file.

config.name: spark.sql.streaming.fileSource.log.cleanupDelay
config.doc: How long in milliseconds a file is guaranteed to be visible for all readers.

config.name: spark.sql.streaming.fileSource.schema.forceNullable
config.doc: When true, force the schema of streaming file source to be nullable (including all the fields). Otherwise, the schema might not be compatible with actual data, which leads to corruptions.

config.name: spark.sql.streaming.fileSource.cleaner.numThreads
config.doc: Number of threads used in the file source completed file cleaner.

config.name: spark.sql.streaming.schemaInference
config.doc: Whether file-based streaming sources will infer its own schema

config.name: spark.sql.streaming.pollingDelay
config.doc: How long to delay polling new data when no data is available

config.name: spark.sql.streaming.stopTimeout
config.doc: How long to wait in milliseconds for the streaming execution thread to stop when calling the streaming query's stop() method. 0 or negative values wait indefinitely.

config.name: spark.sql.streaming.noDataProgressEventInterval
config.doc: How long to wait before providing query idle event when there is no data

config.name: spark.sql.streaming.noDataMicroBatches.enabled
config.doc: Whether streaming micro-batch engine will execute batches without data for eager state management for stateful streaming queries.

config.name: spark.sql.streaming.metricsEnabled
config.doc: Whether Dropwizard/Codahale metrics will be reported for active streaming queries.

config.name: spark.sql.streaming.numRecentProgressUpdates
config.doc: The number of progress updates to retain for a streaming query

config.name: spark.sql.streaming.checkpointFileManagerClass
config.doc: The class used to write checkpoint files atomically. This class must be a subclass of the interface CheckpointFileManager.

config.name: spark.sql.streaming.checkpoint.escapedPathCheck.enabled
config.doc: Whether to detect a streaming query may pick up an incorrect checkpoint path due to SPARK-26824.

config.name: spark.sql.statistics.parallelFileListingInStatsComputation.enabled
config.doc: When true, SQL commands use parallel file listing, as opposed to single thread listing. This usually speeds up commands that need to list many directories.

config.name: spark.sql.defaultSizeInBytes
config.doc: The default table size used in query planning. By default, it is set to Long.MaxValue which is larger than `${AUTO_BROADCASTJOIN_THRESHOLD.key}` to be more conservative. That is to say by default the optimizer will not choose to broadcast a table unless it knows for sure its size is small enough.

config.name: spark.sql.statistics.fallBackToHdfs
config.doc: When true, it will fall back to HDFS if the table statistics are not available from table metadata. This is useful in determining if a table is small enough to use broadcast joins. This flag is effective only for non-partitioned Hive tables. For non-partitioned data source tables, it will be automatically recalculated if table statistics are not available. For partitioned data source and partitioned Hive tables, It is '${DEFAULT_SIZE_IN_BYTES.key}' if table statistics are not available.

config.name: spark.sql.statistics.ndv.maxError
config.doc: The maximum relative standard deviation allowed in HyperLogLog++ algorithm when generating column level statistics.

config.name: spark.sql.statistics.histogram.enabled
config.doc: Generates histograms when computing column statistics if enabled. Histograms can provide better estimation accuracy. Currently, Spark only supports equi-height histogram. Note that collecting histograms takes extra cost. For example, collecting column statistics usually takes only one table scan, but generating equi-height histogram will cause an extra table scan.

config.name: spark.sql.statistics.histogram.numBins
config.doc: The number of bins when generating histograms.

config.name: spark.sql.statistics.percentile.accuracy
config.doc: Accuracy of percentile approximation when generating equi-height histograms. Larger value means better accuracy. The relative error can be deduced by 1.0 / PERCENTILE_ACCURACY.

config.name: spark.sql.statistics.size.autoUpdate.enabled
config.doc: Enables automatic update for table size once table's data is changed. Note that if the total number of files of the table is very large, this can be expensive and slow down data change commands.

config.name: spark.sql.cbo.enabled
config.doc: Enables CBO for estimation of plan statistics when set true.

config.name: spark.sql.cbo.planStats.enabled
config.doc: When true, the logical plan will fetch row counts and column statistics from catalog.

config.name: spark.sql.cbo.joinReorder.enabled
config.doc: Enables join reorder in CBO.

config.name: spark.sql.cbo.joinReorder.dp.threshold
config.doc: The maximum number of joined nodes allowed in the dynamic programming algorithm.

config.name: spark.sql.cbo.joinReorder.card.weight
config.doc: The weight of the ratio of cardinalities (number of rows) in the cost comparison function. The ratio of sizes in bytes has weight 1 - this value. The weighted geometric mean of these ratios is used to decide which of the candidate plans will be chosen by the CBO.

config.name: spark.sql.cbo.joinReorder.dp.star.filter
config.doc: Applies star-join filter heuristics to cost based join enumeration.

config.name: spark.sql.cbo.starSchemaDetection
config.doc: When true, it enables join reordering based on star schema detection.

config.name: spark.sql.cbo.starJoinFTRatio
config.doc: Specifies the upper limit of the ratio between the largest fact tables for a star join to be considered.

config.name: spark.sql.session.timeZone
config.doc: The ID of session local timezone in the format of either region-based zone IDs or zone offsets. Region IDs must have the form 'area/city', such as 'America/Los_Angeles'. Zone offsets must be in the format '(+|-)HH', '(+|-)HH:mm' or '(+|-)HH:mm:ss', e.g '-08', '+01:00' or '-13:33:33'. Also 'UTC' and 'Z' are supported as aliases of '+00:00'. Other short names are not recommended to use because they can be ambiguous.

config.name: spark.sql.windowExec.buffer.in.memory.threshold
config.doc: Threshold for number of rows guaranteed to be held in memory by the window operator

config.name: spark.sql.windowExec.buffer.spill.threshold
config.doc: Threshold for number of rows to be spilled by window operator

config.name: spark.sql.sortMergeJoinExec.buffer.in.memory.threshold
config.doc: Threshold for number of rows guaranteed to be held in memory by the sort merge join operator

config.name: spark.sql.sortMergeJoinExec.buffer.spill.threshold
config.doc: Threshold for number of rows to be spilled by sort merge join operator

config.name: spark.sql.cartesianProductExec.buffer.in.memory.threshold
config.doc: Threshold for number of rows guaranteed to be held in memory by the cartesian product operator

config.name: spark.sql.cartesianProductExec.buffer.spill.threshold
config.doc: Threshold for number of rows to be spilled by cartesian product operator

config.name: spark.sql.parser.quotedRegexColumnNames
config.doc: When true, quoted Identifiers (using backticks) in SELECT statement are interpreted as regular expressions.

config.name: spark.sql.execution.rangeExchange.sampleSizePerPartition
config.doc: Number of points to sample per partition in order to determine the range boundaries for range partitioning, typically used in global sorting (without limit).

config.name: spark.sql.execution.arrow.enabled
config.doc: (Deprecated since Spark 3.0, please set 'spark.sql.execution.arrow.pyspark.enabled'.)

config.name: spark.sql.execution.arrow.pyspark.enabled
config.doc: When true, make use of Apache Arrow for columnar data transfers in PySpark. This optimization applies to: 1. pyspark.sql.DataFrame.toPandas. 2. pyspark.sql.SparkSession.createDataFrame when its input is a Pandas DataFrame or a NumPy ndarray. The following data type is unsupported: ArrayType of TimestampType.

config.name: spark.sql.pyspark.jvmStacktrace.enabled
config.doc: When true, it shows the JVM stacktrace in the user-facing PySpark exception together with Python stacktrace. By default, it is disabled to hide JVM stacktrace and shows a Python-friendly exception only. Note that this is independent from log level settings.

config.name: spark.sql.execution.arrow.sparkr.enabled
config.doc: When true, make use of Apache Arrow for columnar data transfers in SparkR. This optimization applies to: 1. createDataFrame when its input is an R DataFrame 2. collect 3. dapply 4. gapply The following data types are unsupported: FloatType, BinaryType, ArrayType, StructType and MapType.

config.name: spark.sql.execution.arrow.fallback.enabled
config.doc: (Deprecated since Spark 3.0, please set 'spark.sql.execution.arrow.pyspark.fallback.enabled'.)

config.name: spark.sql.execution.arrow.pyspark.fallback.enabled
config.doc: When true, optimizations enabled by '${ARROW_PYSPARK_EXECUTION_ENABLED.key}' will fallback automatically to non-optimized implementations if an error occurs.

config.name: spark.sql.execution.arrow.maxRecordsPerBatch
config.doc: When using Apache Arrow, limit the maximum number of records that can be written to a single ArrowRecordBatch in memory. If set to zero or negative there is no limit. See also spark.sql.execution.arrow.maxBytesPerBatch. If both are set, each batch is created when any condition of both is met.

config.name: spark.sql.execution.pandas.udf.buffer.size
config.doc: Same as `${BUFFER_SIZE.key}` but only applies to Pandas UDF executions. If it is not set, the fallback is `${BUFFER_SIZE.key}`. Note that Pandas execution requires more than 4 bytes. Lowering this value could make small Pandas UDF batch iterated and pipelined; however, it might degrade performance. See SPARK-27870.

config.name: spark.sql.legacy.execution.pandas.groupedMap.assignColumnsByName
config.doc: When true, columns will be looked up by name if labeled with a string and fallback to use position if not. When false, a grouped map Pandas UDF will assign columns from the returned Pandas DataFrame based on position, regardless of column label type. This configuration will be deprecated in future releases.

config.name: spark.sql.execution.pandas.convertToArrowArraySafely
config.doc: When true, Arrow will perform safe type conversion when converting Pandas.Series to Arrow array during serialization. Arrow will raise errors when detecting unsafe type conversion like overflow. When false, disabling Arrow's type check and do type conversions anyway. This config only works for Arrow 0.11.0+.

config.name: spark.sql.optimizer.replaceExceptWithFilter
config.doc: When true, the apply function of the rule verifies whether the right node of the except operation is of type Filter or Project followed by Filter. If yes, the rule further verifies 1) Excluding the filter operations from the right (as well as the left node, if any) on the top, whether both the nodes evaluates to a same result. 2) The left and right nodes don't contain any SubqueryExpressions. 3) The output column names of the left node are distinct. If all the conditions are met, the rule will replace the except operation with a Filter by flipping the filter condition(s) of the right node.

config.name: spark.sql.decimalOperations.allowPrecisionLoss
config.doc: When true (default), establishing the result type of an arithmetic operation happens according to Hive behavior and SQL ANSI 2011 specification, i.e. rounding the decimal part of the result if an exact representation is not possible. Otherwise, NULL is returned in those cases, as previously.

config.name: spark.sql.legacy.literal.pickMinimumPrecision
config.doc: When integral literal is used in decimal operations, pick a minimum precision required by the literal if this config is true, to make the resulting precision and/or scale smaller. This can reduce the possibility of precision lose and/or overflow.

config.name: spark.sql.redaction.options.regex
config.doc: Regex to decide which keys in a Spark SQL command's options map contain sensitive information. The values of options whose names that match this regex will be redacted in the explain output. This redaction is applied on top of the global redaction configuration defined by ${SECRET_REDACTION_PATTERN.key}.

config.name: spark.sql.redaction.string.regex
config.doc: Regex to decide which parts of strings produced by Spark contain sensitive information. When this regex matches a string part, that string part is replaced by a dummy value. This is currently used to redact the output of SQL explain commands. When this conf is not set, the value from `spark.redaction.string.regex` is used.

config.name: spark.sql.function.concatBinaryAsString
config.doc: When this option is set to false and all inputs are binary, `functions.concat` returns an output as binary. Otherwise, it returns as a string.

config.name: spark.sql.function.eltOutputAsString
config.doc: When this option is set to false and all inputs are binary, `elt` returns an output as binary. Otherwise, it returns as a string.

config.name: spark.sql.sources.validatePartitionColumns
config.doc: When this option is set to true, partition column values will be validated with user-specified schema. If the validation fails, a runtime exception is thrown. When this option is set to false, the partition column value will be converted to null if it can not be casted to corresponding user-specified schema.

config.name: spark.sql.streaming.continuous.epochBacklogQueueSize
config.doc: The max number of entries to be stored in queue to wait for late epochs. If this parameter is exceeded by the size of the queue, stream will stop with an error.

config.name: spark.sql.streaming.continuous.executorQueueSize
config.doc: The size (measured in number of rows) of the queue used in continuous execution to buffer the results of a ContinuousDataReader.

config.name: spark.sql.streaming.continuous.executorPollIntervalMs
config.doc: The interval at which continuous execution readers will poll to check whether the epoch has advanced on the driver.

config.name: spark.sql.sources.useV1SourceList
config.doc: A comma-separated list of data source short names or fully qualified data source implementation class names for which Data Source V2 code path is disabled. These data sources will fallback to Data Source V1 code path.

config.name: spark.sql.streaming.disabledV2Writers
config.doc: A comma-separated list of fully qualified data source register class names for which StreamWriteSupport is disabled. Writes to these sources will fall back to the V1 Sinks.

config.name: spark.sql.streaming.disabledV2MicroBatchReaders
config.doc: A comma-separated list of fully qualified data source register class names for which MicroBatchReadSupport is disabled. Reads from these sources will fall back to the V1 Sources.

config.name: spark.sql.sources.partitionOverwriteMode
config.doc: When INSERT OVERWRITE a partitioned data source table, we currently support 2 modes: static and dynamic. In static mode, Spark deletes all the partitions that match the partition specification(e.g. PARTITION(a=1,b)) in the INSERT statement, before overwriting. In dynamic mode, Spark doesn't delete partitions ahead, and only overwrite those partitions that have data written into it at runtime. By default we use static mode to keep the same behavior of Spark prior to 2.3. Note that this config doesn't affect Hive serde tables, as they are always overwritten with dynamic mode. This can also be set as an output option for a data source using key partitionOverwriteMode (which takes precedence over this setting), e.g. dataframe.write.option("partitionOverwriteMode", "dynamic").save(path).

config.name: spark.sql.storeAssignmentPolicy
config.doc: When inserting a value into a column with different data type, Spark will perform type coercion. Currently, we support 3 policies for the type coercion rules: ANSI, legacy and strict. With ANSI policy, Spark performs the type coercion as per ANSI SQL. In practice, the behavior is mostly the same as PostgreSQL. It disallows certain unreasonable type conversions such as converting `string` to `int` or `double` to `boolean`. With legacy policy, Spark allows the type coercion as long as it is a valid `Cast`, which is very loose. e.g. converting `string` to `int` or `double` to `boolean` is allowed. It is also the only behavior in Spark 2.x and it is compatible with Hive. With strict policy, Spark doesn't allow any possible precision loss or data truncation in type coercion, e.g. converting `double` to `int` or `decimal` to `double` is not allowed.

config.name: spark.sql.ansi.enabled
config.doc: When true, Spark SQL uses an ANSI compliant dialect instead of being Hive compliant. For example, Spark will throw an exception at runtime instead of returning null results when the inputs to a SQL operator/function are invalid. For full details of this dialect, you can find them in the section "ANSI Compliance" of Spark's documentation. Some ANSI dialect features may be not from the ANSI SQL standard directly, but their behaviors align with ANSI SQL's style

config.name: spark.sql.execution.sortBeforeRepartition
config.doc: When perform a repartition following a shuffle, the output row ordering would be nondeterministic. If some downstream stages fail and some tasks of the repartition stage retry, these tasks may generate different data, and that can lead to correctness issues. Turn on this config to insert a local sort before actually doing repartition to generate consistent repartition results. The performance of repartition() may go down since we insert extra local sort before it.

config.name: spark.sql.optimizer.nestedSchemaPruning.enabled
config.doc: Prune nested fields from a logical relation's output which are unnecessary in satisfying a query. This optimization allows columnar file format readers to avoid reading unnecessary nested column data. Currently Parquet and ORC are the data sources that implement this optimization.

config.name: spark.sql.optimizer.nestedPredicatePushdown.supportedFileSources
config.doc: A comma-separated list of data source short names or fully qualified data source implementation class names for which Spark tries to push down predicates for nested columns and/or names containing `dots` to data sources. This configuration is only effective with file-based data sources in DSv1. Currently, Parquet and ORC implement both optimizations. The other data sources don't support this feature yet. So the default value is 'parquet,orc'.

config.name: spark.sql.optimizer.serializer.nestedSchemaPruning.enabled
config.doc: Prune nested fields from object serialization operator which are unnecessary in satisfying a query. This optimization allows object serializers to avoid executing unnecessary nested expressions.

config.name: spark.sql.optimizer.expression.nestedPruning.enabled
config.doc: Prune nested fields from expressions in an operator which are unnecessary in satisfying a query. Note that this optimization doesn't prune nested fields from physical data source scanning. For pruning nested fields from scanning, please use `spark.sql.optimizer.nestedSchemaPruning.enabled` config.

config.name: spark.sql.execution.topKSortFallbackThreshold
config.doc: In SQL queries with a SORT followed by a LIMIT like 'SELECT x FROM t ORDER BY y LIMIT m', if m is under this threshold, do a top-K sort in memory, otherwise do a global sort which spills to disk if necessary.

config.name: spark.sql.csv.parser.columnPruning.enabled
config.doc: If it is set to true, column names of the requested schema are passed to CSV parser. Other column values can be ignored during parsing even if they are malformed.

config.name: spark.sql.repl.eagerEval.enabled
config.doc: Enables eager evaluation or not. When true, the top K rows of Dataset will be displayed if and only if the REPL supports the eager evaluation. Currently, the eager evaluation is supported in PySpark and SparkR. In PySpark, for the notebooks like Jupyter, the HTML table (generated by _repr_html_) will be returned. For plain Python REPL, the returned outputs are formatted like dataframe.show(). In SparkR, the returned outputs are showed similar to R data.frame would.

config.name: spark.sql.repl.eagerEval.maxNumRows
config.doc: The max number of rows that are returned by eager evaluation. This only takes effect when ${REPL_EAGER_EVAL_ENABLED.key} is set to true. The valid range of this config is from 0 to (Int.MaxValue - 1), so the invalid config like negative and greater than (Int.MaxValue - 1) will be normalized to 0 and (Int.MaxValue - 1).

config.name: spark.sql.repl.eagerEval.truncate
config.doc: The max number of characters for each cell that is returned by eager evaluation. This only takes effect when ${REPL_EAGER_EVAL_ENABLED.key} is set to true.

config.name: spark.sql.codegen.aggregate.fastHashMap.capacityBit
config.doc: Capacity for the max number of rows to be held in memory by the fast hash aggregate product operator. The bit is not for actual value, but the actual numBuckets is determined by loadFactor (e.g: default bit value 16 , the actual numBuckets is ((1 << 16) / 0.5).

config.name: spark.sql.avro.compression.codec
config.doc: Compression codec used in writing of AVRO files. Supported codecs: uncompressed, deflate, snappy, bzip2, xz and zstandard. Default codec is snappy.

config.name: spark.sql.avro.deflate.level
config.doc: Compression level for the deflate codec used in writing of AVRO files. Valid value must be in the range of from 1 to 9 inclusive or -1. The default value is -1 which corresponds to 6 level in the current implementation.

config.name: spark.sql.legacy.sizeOfNull
config.doc: If it is set to false, or ${ANSI_ENABLED.key} is true, then size of null returns null. Otherwise, it returns -1, which was inherited from Hive.

config.name: spark.sql.legacy.replaceDatabricksSparkAvro.enabled
config.doc: If it is set to true, the data source provider com.databricks.spark.avro is mapped to the built-in but external Avro data source module for backward compatibility.

config.name: spark.sql.legacy.setopsPrecedence.enabled
config.doc: When set to true and the order of evaluation is not specified by parentheses, the set operations are performed from left to right as they appear in the query. When set to false and order of evaluation is not specified by parentheses, INTERSECT operations are performed before any UNION, EXCEPT and MINUS operations.

config.name: spark.sql.legacy.exponentLiteralAsDecimal.enabled
config.doc: When set to true, a literal with an exponent (e.g. 1E-30) would be parsed as Decimal rather than Double.

config.name: spark.sql.legacy.allowNegativeScaleOfDecimal
config.doc: When set to true, negative scale of Decimal type is allowed. For example, the type of number 1E10BD under legacy mode is DecimalType(2, -9), but is Decimal(11, 0) in non legacy mode.

config.name: spark.sql.legacy.bucketedTableScan.outputOrdering
config.doc: When true, the bucketed table scan will list files during planning to figure out the output ordering, which is expensive and may make the planning quite slow.

config.name: spark.sql.legacy.parser.havingWithoutGroupByAsWhere
config.doc: If it is set to true, the parser will treat HAVING without GROUP BY as a normal WHERE, which does not follow SQL standard.

config.name: spark.sql.legacy.json.allowEmptyString.enabled
config.doc: When set to true, the parser of JSON data source treats empty strings as null for some data types such as `IntegerType`.

config.name: spark.sql.legacy.createEmptyCollectionUsingStringType
config.doc: When set to true, Spark returns an empty collection with `StringType` as element type if the `array`/`map` function is called without any parameters. Otherwise, Spark returns an empty collection with `NullType` as element type.

config.name: spark.sql.legacy.allowUntypedScalaUDF
config.doc: When set to true, user is allowed to use org.apache.spark.sql.functions. udf(f: AnyRef, dataType: DataType). Otherwise, an exception will be thrown at runtime.

config.name: spark.sql.truncateTable.ignorePermissionAcl.enabled
config.doc: When set to true, TRUNCATE TABLE command will not try to set back original permission and ACLs when re-creating the table/partition paths.

config.name: spark.sql.legacy.dataset.nameNonStructGroupingKeyAsValue
config.doc: When set to true, the key attribute resulted from running `Dataset.groupByKey` for non-struct key type, will be named as `value`, following the behavior of Spark version 2.4 and earlier.

config.name: spark.sql.debug.maxToStringFields
config.doc: Maximum number of fields of sequence-like entries can be converted to strings in debug output. Any elements beyond the limit will be dropped and replaced by a "... N more fields" placeholder.

config.name: spark.sql.maxPlanStringLength
config.doc: Maximum number of characters to output for a plan string. If the plan is longer, further output will be truncated. The default setting always generates a full plan. Set this to a lower value such as 8k if plan strings are taking up too much memory or are causing OutOfMemory errors in the driver or UI processes.

config.name: spark.sql.legacy.setCommandRejectsSparkCoreConfs
config.doc: If it is set to true, SET command will fail when the key is registered as a SparkConf entry.

config.name: spark.sql.datetime.java8API.enabled
config.doc: If the configuration property is set to true, java.time.Instant and java.time.LocalDate classes of Java 8 API are used as external types for Catalyst's TimestampType and DateType. If it is set to false, java.sql.Timestamp and java.sql.Date are used for the same purpose.

config.name: spark.sql.sources.binaryFile.maxLength
config.doc: The max length of a file that can be read by the binary file data source. Spark will fail fast and not attempt to read the file if its length exceeds this value. The theoretical max is Int.MaxValue, though VMs might implement a smaller max.

config.name: spark.sql.legacy.typeCoercion.datetimeToString.enabled
config.doc: If it is set to true, date/timestamp will cast to string in binary comparisons with String when ${ANSI_ENABLED.key} is false.

config.name: spark.sql.defaultCatalog
config.doc: Name of the default catalog. This will be the current catalog if users have not explicitly set the current catalog yet.

config.name: spark.sql.mapKeyDedupPolicy
config.doc: The policy to deduplicate map keys in builtin function: CreateMap, MapFromArrays, MapFromEntries, StringToMap, MapConcat and TransformKeys. When EXCEPTION, the query fails if duplicated map keys are detected. When LAST_WIN, the map key that is inserted at last takes precedence.

config.name: spark.sql.legacy.doLooseUpcast
config.doc: When true, the upcast will be loose and allows string to atomic types.

config.name: spark.sql.legacy.ctePrecedencePolicy
config.doc: When LEGACY, outer CTE definitions takes precedence over inner definitions. If set to EXCEPTION, AnalysisException is thrown while name conflict is detected in nested CTE. The default is CORRECTED, inner CTE definitions take precedence. This config will be removed in future versions and CORRECTED will be the only behavior.

config.name: spark.sql.legacy.timeParserPolicy
config.doc: When LEGACY, java.text.SimpleDateFormat is used for formatting and parsing dates/timestamps in a locale-sensitive manner, which is the approach before Spark 3.0. When set to CORRECTED, classes from java.time.* packages are used for the same purpose. When set to EXCEPTION, RuntimeException is thrown when we will get different results. The default is CORRECTED.

config.name: spark.sql.legacy.followThreeValuedLogicInArrayExists
config.doc: When true, the ArrayExists will follow the three-valued boolean logic.

config.name: spark.sql.maven.additionalRemoteRepositories
config.doc: A comma-delimited string config of the optional additional remote Maven mirror repositories. This is only used for downloading Hive jars in IsolatedClientLoader if the default Maven Central repo is unreachable.

config.name: spark.sql.legacy.fromDayTimeString.enabled
config.doc: When true, the `from` bound is not taken into account in conversion of a day-time string to an interval, and the `to` bound is used to skip all interval units out of the specified range. If it is set to `false`, `ParseException` is thrown if the input does not match to the pattern defined by `from` and `to`.

config.name: spark.sql.legacy.notReserveProperties
config.doc: When true, all database and table properties are not reserved and available for create/alter syntaxes. But please be aware that the reserved properties will be silently removed.

config.name: spark.sql.legacy.addSingleFileInAddFile
config.doc: When true, only a single file can be added using ADD FILE. If false, then users can add directory by passing directory path to ADD FILE.

config.name: spark.sql.legacy.mssqlserver.numericMapping.enabled
config.doc: When true, use legacy MsSqlServer TINYINT, SMALLINT and REAL type mapping.

config.name: spark.sql.csv.filterPushdown.enabled
config.doc: When true, enable filter pushdown to CSV datasource.

config.name: spark.sql.addPartitionInBatch.size
config.doc: The number of partitions to be handled in one turn when use `AlterTableAddPartitionCommand` or `RepairTableCommand` to add partitions into table. The smaller batch size is, the less memory is required for the real handler, e.g. Hive Metastore.

config.name: spark.sql.legacy.allowHashOnMapType
config.doc: When set to true, hash expressions can be applied on elements of MapType. Otherwise, an analysis exception will be thrown.

config.name: spark.sql.legacy.parquet.datetimeRebaseModeInWrite
config.doc: When LEGACY, Spark will rebase dates/timestamps from Proleptic Gregorian calendar to the legacy hybrid (Julian + Gregorian) calendar when writing Parquet files. When CORRECTED, Spark will not do rebase and write the dates/timestamps as it is. When EXCEPTION, which is the default, Spark will fail the writing if it sees ancient dates/timestamps that are ambiguous between the two calendars. This config influences on writes of the following parquet logical types: DATE, TIMESTAMP_MILLIS, TIMESTAMP_MICROS. The INT96 type has the separate config: ${LEGACY_PARQUET_INT96_REBASE_MODE_IN_WRITE.key}.

config.name: spark.sql.legacy.parquet.datetimeRebaseModeInRead
config.doc: When LEGACY, Spark will rebase dates/timestamps from the legacy hybrid (Julian + Gregorian) calendar to Proleptic Gregorian calendar when reading Parquet files. When CORRECTED, Spark will not do rebase and read the dates/timestamps as it is. When EXCEPTION, which is the default, Spark will fail the reading if it sees ancient dates/timestamps that are ambiguous between the two calendars. This config is only effective if the writer info (like Spark, Hive) of the Parquet files is unknown. This config influences on reads of the following parquet logical types: DATE, TIMESTAMP_MILLIS, TIMESTAMP_MICROS. The INT96 type has the separate config: ${LEGACY_PARQUET_INT96_REBASE_MODE_IN_READ.key}.

config.name: spark.sql.legacy.avro.datetimeRebaseModeInWrite
config.doc: When LEGACY, Spark will rebase dates/timestamps from Proleptic Gregorian calendar to the legacy hybrid (Julian + Gregorian) calendar when writing Avro files. When CORRECTED, Spark will not do rebase and write the dates/timestamps as it is. When EXCEPTION, which is the default, Spark will fail the writing if it sees ancient dates/timestamps that are ambiguous between the two calendars.

config.name: spark.sql.legacy.avro.datetimeRebaseModeInRead
config.doc: When LEGACY, Spark will rebase dates/timestamps from the legacy hybrid (Julian + Gregorian) calendar to Proleptic Gregorian calendar when reading Avro files. When CORRECTED, Spark will not do rebase and read the dates/timestamps as it is. When EXCEPTION, which is the default, Spark will fail the reading if it sees ancient dates/timestamps that are ambiguous between the two calendars. This config is only effective if the writer info (like Spark, Hive) of the Avro files is unknown.

config.name: spark.sql.scriptTransformation.exitTimeoutInSeconds
config.doc: Timeout for executor to wait for the termination of transformation script when EOF.

config.name: spark.sql.warehouse.dir
config.doc: The default location for managed databases and tables.

config.name: spark.sql.sources.schemaStringLengthThreshold
config.doc: The maximum length allowed in a single cell when storing additional schema information in Hive's metastore.

config.name: spark.sql.filesourceTableRelationCacheSize
config.doc: The maximum size of the cache that maps qualified table names to table relation plans.

config.name: spark.sql.codegen.cache.maxEntries
config.doc: When nonzero, enable caching of generated classes for operators and expressions. All jobs share the cache that can use up to the specified number for generated classes.

config.name: spark.sql.codegen.comments
config.doc: When true, put comment in the generated code. Since computing huge comments can be extremely expensive in certain cases, such as deeply-nested expressions which operate over inputs with wide schemas, default is false.

config.name: spark.sql.debug
config.doc: Only used for internal debugging. Not all functions are supported when it is enabled.

config.name: spark.sql.hive.thriftServer.singleSession
config.doc: When set to true, Hive Thrift server is running in a single session mode. All the JDBC/ODBC connections share the temporary views, function registries, SQL configuration and the current database.

config.name: spark.sql.extensions
config.doc: A comma-separated list of classes that implement Function1[SparkSessionExtensions, Unit] used to configure Spark Session extensions. The classes must have a no-args constructor. If multiple extensions are specified, they are applied in the specified order. For the case of rules and planner strategies, they are applied in the specified order. For the case of parsers, the last parser is used and each parser can delegate to its predecessor. For the case of function name conflicts, the last registered function name is used.

config.name: spark.sql.queryExecutionListeners
config.doc: List of class names implementing QueryExecutionListener that will be automatically added to newly created sessions. The classes should have either a no-arg constructor, or a constructor that expects a SparkConf argument.

config.name: spark.sql.streaming.streamingQueryListeners
config.doc: List of class names implementing StreamingQueryListener that will be automatically added to newly created sessions. The classes should have either a no-arg constructor, or a constructor that expects a SparkConf argument.

config.name: spark.sql.ui.retainedExecutions
config.doc: Number of executions to retain in the Spark UI.

config.name: spark.sql.broadcastExchange.maxThreadThreshold
config.doc: The maximum degree of parallelism to fetch and broadcast the table. If we encounter memory issue like frequently full GC or OOM when broadcast table we can decrease this number in order to reduce memory usage. Notice the number should be carefully chosen since decreasing parallelism might cause longer waiting for other broadcasting. Also, increasing parallelism may cause memory problem.

config.name: spark.sql.subquery.maxThreadThreshold
config.doc: The maximum degree of parallelism to execute the subquery.

config.name: spark.sql.event.truncate.length
config.doc: Threshold of SQL length beyond which it will be truncated before adding to event. Defaults to no truncation. If set to 0, callsite will be logged instead.

config.name: spark.sql.legacy.sessionInitWithConfigDefaults
config.doc: Flag to revert to legacy behavior where a cloned SparkSession receives SparkConf defaults, dropping any overrides in its parent SparkSession.

config.name: spark.sql.defaultUrlStreamHandlerFactory.enabled
config.doc: When true, register Hadoop's FsUrlStreamHandlerFactory to support ADD JAR against HDFS locations. It should be disabled when a different stream protocol handler should be registered to support a particular protocol type, or if Hadoop's FsUrlStreamHandlerFactory conflicts with other protocol types such as `http` or `https`. See also SPARK-25694 and HADOOP-14598.

config.name: spark.sql.streaming.ui.enabled
config.doc: Whether to run the Structured Streaming Web UI for the Spark application when the Spark Web UI is enabled.

config.name: spark.sql.streaming.ui.retainedProgressUpdates
config.doc: The number of progress updates to retain for a streaming query for Structured Streaming UI.

config.name: spark.sql.streaming.ui.retainedQueries
config.doc: The number of inactive queries to retain for Structured Streaming UI.

config.name: spark.sql.hive.metastore.version
config.doc: Version of the Hive metastore. Available options are 2.0.0 through 2.3.10, 3.0.0 through 3.1.3 and 4.0.0 through 4.1.0.

config.name: spark.sql.hive.version
config.doc: The compiled, a.k.a, builtin Hive version of the Spark distribution bundled with. Note that, this a read-only conf and only used to report the built-in hive version. If you want a different metastore client for Spark to call, please refer to spark.sql.hive.metastore.version.

config.name: spark.sql.hive.metastore.jars
config.doc: | Location of the jars that should be used to instantiate the HiveMetastoreClient. | This property can be one of four options: | 1. "builtin" | Use Hive ${builtinHiveVersion}, which is bundled with the Spark assembly when | -Phive is enabled. When this option is chosen, | spark.sql.hive.metastore.version must be either | ${builtinHiveVersion} or not defined. | 2. "maven" | Use Hive jars of specified version downloaded from Maven repositories. | 3. "path" | Use Hive jars configured by `spark.sql.hive.metastore.jars.path` | in comma separated format. Support both local or remote paths.The provided jars | should be the same version as `${HIVE_METASTORE_VERSION.key}`. | 4. A classpath in the standard format for both Hive and Hadoop. The provided jars | should be the same version as `${HIVE_METASTORE_VERSION.key}`.

config.name: spark.sql.hive.convertMetastoreParquet
config.doc: When set to true, the built-in Parquet reader and writer are used to process parquet tables created by using the HiveQL syntax, instead of Hive serde.

config.name: spark.sql.hive.convertMetastoreParquet.mergeSchema
config.doc: When true, also tries to merge possibly different but compatible Parquet schemas in different Parquet data files. This configuration is only effective when "spark.sql.hive.convertMetastoreParquet" is true.

config.name: spark.sql.hive.convertMetastoreOrc
config.doc: When set to true, the built-in ORC reader and writer are used to process ORC tables created by using the HiveQL syntax, instead of Hive serde.

config.name: spark.sql.hive.convertInsertingPartitionedTable
config.doc: When set to true, and `spark.sql.hive.convertMetastoreParquet` or `spark.sql.hive.convertMetastoreOrc` is true, the built-in ORC/Parquet writer is usedto process inserting into partitioned ORC/Parquet tables created by using the HiveSQL syntax.

config.name: spark.sql.hive.convertMetastoreCtas
config.doc: When set to true, Spark will try to use built-in data source writer instead of Hive serde in CTAS. This flag is effective only if `spark.sql.hive.convertMetastoreParquet` or `spark.sql.hive.convertMetastoreOrc` is enabled respectively for Parquet and ORC formats

config.name: spark.sql.hive.metastore.sharedPrefixes
config.doc: A comma separated list of class prefixes that should be loaded using the classloader that is shared between Spark SQL and a specific version of Hive. An example of classes that should be shared is JDBC drivers that are needed to talk to the metastore. Other classes that need to be shared are those that interact with classes that are already shared. For example, custom appenders that are used by log4j.

config.name: spark.sql.hive.metastore.barrierPrefixes
config.doc: A comma separated list of class prefixes that should explicitly be reloaded for each version of Hive that Spark SQL is communicating with. For example, Hive UDFs that are declared in a prefix that typically would be shared (i.e. org.apache.spark.*).

config.name: spark.sql.hive.thriftServer.async
config.doc: When set to true, Hive Thrift server executes SQL queries in an asynchronous way.

config.name: spark.history.store.hybridStore.enabled
config.doc: Whether to use HybridStore as the store when parsing event logs. HybridStore will first write data to an in-memory store and having a background thread that dumps data to a disk store after the writing to in-memory store is completed.

config.name: spark.history.store.hybridStore.maxMemoryUsage
config.doc: Maximum memory space that can be used to create HybridStore. The HybridStore co-uses the heap memory, so the heap memory should be increased through the memory option for SHS if the HybridStore is enabled.

config.name: spark.master.ui.decommission.allow.mode
config.doc: Specifies the behavior of the Master Web UI's /workers/kill endpoint. Possible choices are: `LOCAL` means allow this endpoint from IP's that are local to the machine running the Master, `DENY` means to completely disable this endpoint, `ALLOW` means to allow calling this endpoint from any IP.

config.name: spark.executor.metrics.fileSystemSchemes
config.doc: The file system schemes to report in executor metrics.

config.name: spark.storage.decommission.enabled
config.doc: Whether to decommission the block manager when decommissioning executor

config.name: spark.storage.decommission.shuffleBlocks.enabled
config.doc: Whether to transfer shuffle blocks during block manager decommissioning. Requires a migratable shuffle resolver (like sort based shuffle)

config.name: spark.storage.decommission.shuffleBlocks.maxThreads
config.doc: Maximum number of threads to use in migrating shuffle files.

config.name: spark.storage.decommission.rddBlocks.enabled
config.doc: Whether to transfer RDD blocks during block manager decommissioning.

config.name: spark.storage.decommission.maxReplicationFailuresPerBlock
config.doc: Maximum number of failures which can be handled for the replication of one RDD block when block manager is decommissioning and trying to move its existing blocks.

config.name: spark.storage.decommission.replicationReattemptInterval
config.doc: The interval of time between consecutive cache block replication reattempts happening on each decommissioning executor (due to storage decommissioning).

config.name: spark.storage.decommission.fallbackStorage.path
config.doc: The location for fallback storage during block manager decommissioning. For example, `s3a://spark-storage/`. In case of empty, fallback storage is disabled. The storage will not be cleaned up by Spark unless ${STORAGE_DECOMMISSION_FALLBACK_STORAGE_CLEANUP.key} is true. Use an external clean up mechanism when false, for instance a TTL.

config.name: spark.locality.wait.legacyResetOnTaskLaunch
config.doc: Whether to use the legacy behavior of locality wait, which resets the delay timer anytime a task is scheduled. See Delay Scheduling section of TaskSchedulerImpl's class documentation for more details.

config.name: spark.scheduler.excludeOnFailure.unschedulableTaskSetTimeout
config.doc: The timeout in seconds to wait to acquire a new executor and schedule a task before aborting a TaskSet which is unschedulable because all executors are excluded due to failures.

config.name: spark.archives
config.doc: Comma-separated list of archives to be extracted into the working directory of each executor. .jar, .tar.gz, .tgz and .zip are supported. You can specify the directory name to unpack via adding '#' after the file name to unpack, for example, 'file.zip#directory'. This configuration is experimental.

config.name: spark.decommission.enabled
config.doc: When decommission enabled, Spark will try its best to shutdown the executor gracefully. Spark will try to migrate all the RDD blocks (controlled by ${STORAGE_DECOMMISSION_RDD_BLOCKS_ENABLED.key}) and shuffle blocks (controlled by ${STORAGE_DECOMMISSION_SHUFFLE_BLOCKS_ENABLED.key}) from the decommissioning executor to a remote executor when ${STORAGE_DECOMMISSION_ENABLED.key} is enabled. With decommission enabled, Spark will also decommission an executor instead of killing when ${DYN_ALLOCATION_ENABLED.key} enabled.

config.name: spark.executor.decommission.killInterval
config.doc: Duration after which a decommissioned executor will be killed forcefully *by an outside* (e.g. non-spark) service. This config is useful for cloud environments where we know in advance when an executor is going to go down after decommissioning signal i.e. around 2 mins in aws spot nodes, 1/2 hrs in spot block nodes etc. This config is currently used to decide what tasks running on decommission executors to speculate.

config.name: spark.scheduler.resource.profileMergeConflicts
config.doc: If set to true, Spark will merge ResourceProfiles when different profiles are specified in RDDs that get combined into a single stage. When they are merged, Spark chooses the maximum of each resource and creates a new ResourceProfile. The default of false results in Spark throwing an exception if multiple different ResourceProfiles are found in RDDs going into the same stage.

config.name: spark.standalone.submit.waitAppCompletion
config.doc: In standalone cluster mode, controls whether the client waits to exit until the application completes. If set to true, the client process will stay alive polling the driver's status. Otherwise, the client process will exit after submission.

config.name: spark.executor.allowSparkContext
config.doc: If set to true, SparkContext can be created in executors.

config.name: spark.executor.killOnFatalError.depth
config.doc: The max depth of the exception chain in a failed task Spark will search for a fatal error to check whether it should kill the JVM process. 0 means not checking any fatal error, 1 means checking only the exception but not the cause, and so on.

config.name: spark.shuffle.push.enabled
config.doc: Set to true to enable push-based shuffle on the client side and this works in conjunction with the server side flag spark.shuffle.push.server.mergedShuffleFileManagerImpl which needs to be set with the appropriate org.apache.spark.network.shuffle.MergedShuffleFileManager implementation for push-based shuffle to be enabled

config.name: spark.shuffle.push.maxRetainedMergerLocations
config.doc: Maximum number of merger locations cached for push-based shuffle. Currently, merger locations are hosts of external shuffle services responsible for handling pushed blocks, merging them and serving merged blocks for later shuffle fetch.

config.name: spark.shuffle.push.mergersMinThresholdRatio
config.doc: Ratio used to compute the minimum number of shuffle merger locations required for a stage based on the number of partitions for the reducer stage. For example, a reduce stage which has 100 partitions and uses the default value 0.05 requires at least 5 unique merger locations to enable push-based shuffle. Merger locations are currently defined as external shuffle services.

config.name: spark.shuffle.push.mergersMinStaticThreshold
config.doc: The static threshold for number of shuffle push merger locations should be available in order to enable push-based shuffle for a stage. Note this config works in conjunction with ${SHUFFLE_MERGER_LOCATIONS_MIN_THRESHOLD_RATIO.key}. Maximum of spark.shuffle.push.mergersMinStaticThreshold and ${SHUFFLE_MERGER_LOCATIONS_MIN_THRESHOLD_RATIO.key} ratio number of mergers needed to enable push-based shuffle for a stage. For eg: with 1000 partitions for the child stage with spark.shuffle.push.mergersMinStaticThreshold as 5 and ${SHUFFLE_MERGER_LOCATIONS_MIN_THRESHOLD_RATIO.key} set to 0.05, we would need at least 50 mergers to enable push-based shuffle for that stage.

config.name: spark.kubernetes.configMap.maxSize
config.doc: Max size limit for a config map. This is configurable as per https://etcd.io/docs/v3.4.0/dev-guide/limit/ on k8s server end.

config.name: spark.kubernetes.allocation.executor.timeout
config.doc: Time to wait before a newly created executor POD request, which does not reached the POD pending state yet, considered timedout and will be deleted.

config.name: spark.kubernetes.executor.checkAllContainers
config.doc: If set to true, all containers in the executor pod will be checked when reportingexecutor status.

config.name: spark.kubernetes.executor.missingPodDetectDelta
config.doc: When a registered executor's POD is missing from the Kubernetes API server's polled list of PODs then this delta time is taken as the accepted time difference between the registration time and the time of the polling. After this time the POD is considered missing from the cluster and the executor will be removed.

config.name: spark.mesos.dispatcher.queue
config.doc: Set the name of the dispatcher queue to which the application is submitted. The specified queue must be added to the dispatcher with "spark.mesos.dispatcher.queue.[QueueName]". If no queue is specified, then the application is submitted to the "default" queue with 0.0 priority.

config.name: spark.yarn.applicationType
config.doc: Type of this application,it allows user to specify a more specific type for the application, such as SPARK,SPARK-SQL, SPARK-STREAMING, SPARK-MLLIB and SPARK-GRAPH

config.name: spark.yarn.includeDriverLogsLink
config.doc: In cluster mode, whether the client application report includes links to the driver container's logs. This requires polling the ResourceManager's REST API, so it places some additional load on the RM.

config.name: spark.sql.planChangeLog.level
config.doc: Configures the log level for logging the change from the original plan to the new plan after a rule or batch is applied. The value can be ${VALID_LOG_LEVELS.mkString()}.

config.name: spark.sql.planChangeLog.rules
config.doc: Configures a list of rules for logging plan changes, in which the rules are specified by their rule names and separated by comma.

config.name: spark.sql.planChangeLog.batches
config.doc: Configures a list of batches for logging plan changes, in which the batches are specified by their batch names and separated by comma.

config.name: spark.sql.adaptive.optimizer.excludedRules
config.doc: Configures a list of rules to be disabled in the adaptive optimizer, in which the rules are specified by their rule names and separated by comma. The optimizer will log the rules that have indeed been excluded.

config.name: spark.sql.subexpressionElimination.cache.maxEntries
config.doc: The maximum entries of the cache used for interpreted subexpression elimination.

config.name: spark.sql.hive.metastorePartitionPruningInSetThreshold
config.doc: The threshold of set size for InSet predicate when pruning partitions through Hive Metastore. When the set size exceeds the threshold, we rewrite the InSet predicate to be greater than or equal to the minimum value in set and less than or equal to the maximum value in set. Larger values may cause Hive Metastore stack overflow. But for InSet inside Not with values exceeding the threshold, we won't push it to Hive Metastore.

config.name: spark.sql.thriftServer.queryTimeout
config.doc: Set a query duration timeout in seconds in Thrift Server. If the timeout is set to a positive value, a running query will be cancelled automatically when the timeout is exceeded, otherwise the query continues to run till completion. If timeout values are set for each statement via `java.sql.Statement.setQueryTimeout` and they are smaller than this configuration value, they take precedence. If you set this timeout and prefer to cancel the queries right away without waiting task to finish, consider enabling ${THRIFTSERVER_FORCE_CANCEL.key} together.

config.name: spark.sql.sources.bucketing.autoBucketedScan.enabled
config.doc: When true, decide whether to do bucketed scan on input tables based on query plan automatically. Do not use bucketed scan if 1. query does not have operators to utilize bucketing (e.g. join, group-by, etc), or 2. there's an exchange operator between these operators and table scan. Note when '${BUCKETING_ENABLED.key}' is set to false, this configuration does not take any effect.

config.name: spark.sql.files.minPartitionNum
config.doc: The suggested (not guaranteed) minimum number of split file partitions. If not set, the default value is `${LEAF_NODE_DEFAULT_PARALLELISM.key}`. This configuration is effective only when using file-based sources such as Parquet, JSON and ORC.

config.name: spark.sql.execution.removeRedundantProjects
config.doc: Whether to remove redundant project exec node based on children's output and ordering requirement.

config.name: spark.sql.execution.removeRedundantSorts
config.doc: Whether to remove redundant physical sort node

config.name: spark.sql.streaming.stateStore.stateSchemaCheck
config.doc: When true, Spark will validate the state schema against schema on existing state and fail query if it's incompatible.

config.name: spark.sql.streaming.stateStore.formatValidation.enabled
config.doc: When true, check if the data from state store is valid or not when running streaming queries. This can happen if the state store format has been changed. Note, the feature is only effective in the build-in HDFS state store provider now.

config.name: spark.sql.streaming.stateStore.maintenanceInterval
config.doc: The interval in milliseconds between triggering maintenance tasks in StateStore. The maintenance task executes background maintenance task in all the loaded store providers if they are still the active instances according to the coordinator. If not, inactive instances of store providers will be closed.

config.name: spark.sql.streaming.stateStore.compression.codec
config.doc: The codec used to compress delta and snapshot files generated by StateStore. By default, Spark provides four codecs: lz4, lzf, snappy, and zstd. You can also use fully qualified class names to specify the codec. Default codec is lz4.

config.name: spark.sql.streaming.kafka.useDeprecatedOffsetFetching
config.doc: When true, the deprecated Consumer based offset fetching used which could cause infinite wait in Spark queries. Such cases query restart is the only workaround. For further details please see Offset Fetching chapter of Structured Streaming Kafka Integration Guide.

config.name: spark.sql.streaming.statefulOperator.checkCorrectness.enabled
config.doc: When true, the stateful operators for streaming query will be checked for possible correctness issue due to global watermark. The correctness issue comes from queries containing stateful operation which can emit rows older than the current watermark plus allowed late record delay, which are "late rows" in downstream stateful operations and these rows can be discarded. Please refer the programming guide doc for more details. Once the issue is detected, Spark will throw analysis exception. When this config is disabled, Spark will just print warning message for users. Prior to Spark 3.1.0, the behavior is disabling this config.

config.name: spark.sql.legacy.allowParameterlessCount
config.doc: When true, the SQL function 'count' is allowed to take no parameters.

config.name: spark.sql.legacy.useCurrentConfigsForView
config.doc: When true, SQL Configs of the current active SparkSession instead of the captured ones will be applied during the parsing and analysis phases of the view resolution.

config.name: spark.sql.legacy.storeAnalyzedPlanForView
config.doc: When true, analyzed plan instead of SQL text will be stored when creating temporary view

config.name: spark.sql.optimizer.enableJsonExpressionOptimization
config.doc: Whether to optimize JSON expressions in SQL optimizer. It includes pruning unnecessary columns from from_json, simplifying from_json + to_json, to_json + named_struct(from_json.col1, from_json.col2, ....).

config.name: spark.sql.execution.pyspark.udf.simplifiedTraceback.enabled
config.doc: When true, the traceback from Python UDFs is simplified. It hides the Python worker, (de)serialization, etc from PySpark in tracebacks, and only shows the exception messages from UDFs. Note that this works only with CPython 3.7+.

config.name: spark.sql.execution.fastFailOnFileFormatOutput
config.doc: Whether to fast fail task execution when writing output to FileFormat datasource. If this is enabled, in `FileFormatWriter` we will catch `FileAlreadyExistsException` and fast fail output task without further task retry. Only enabling this if you know the `FileAlreadyExistsException` of the output task is unrecoverable, i.e., further task attempts won't be able to success. If the `FileAlreadyExistsException` might be recoverable, you should keep this as disabled and let Spark to retry output tasks. This is disabled by default.

config.name: spark.sql.optimizer.disableHints
config.doc: When true, the optimizer will disable user-specified hints that are additional directives for better planning of a query.

config.name: spark.sql.legacy.parseNullPartitionSpecAsStringLiteral
config.doc: If it is set to true, `PARTITION(col=null)` is parsed as a string literal of its text representation, e.g., string 'null', when the partition column is string type. Otherwise, it is always parsed as a null literal in the partition spec.

config.name: spark.sql.legacy.statisticalAggregate
config.doc: When set to true, statistical aggregate function returns Double.NaN if divide by zero occurred during expression evaluation, otherwise, it returns null. Before version 3.1.0, it returns NaN in divideByZero case by default.

config.name: spark.sql.maxMetadataStringLength
config.doc: Maximum number of characters to output for a metadata string. e.g. file location in `DataSourceScanExec`, every value will be abbreviated if exceed length.

config.name: spark.sql.ui.explainMode
config.doc: Configures the query explain mode used in the Spark SQL UI. The value can be 'simple', 'extended', 'codegen', 'cost', or 'formatted'. The default value is 'formatted'.

config.name: spark.sql.json.filterPushdown.enabled
config.doc: When true, enable filter pushdown to JSON datasource.

config.name: spark.sql.avro.filterPushdown.enabled
config.doc: When true, enable filter pushdown to Avro datasource.

config.name: spark.sql.legacy.integerGroupingId
config.doc: When true, grouping_id() returns int values instead of long values.

config.name: spark.sql.legacy.parquet.int96RebaseModeInWrite
config.doc: When LEGACY, Spark will rebase INT96 timestamps from Proleptic Gregorian calendar to the legacy hybrid (Julian + Gregorian) calendar when writing Parquet files. When CORRECTED, Spark will not do rebase and write the timestamps as it is. When EXCEPTION, which is the default, Spark will fail the writing if it sees ancient timestamps that are ambiguous between the two calendars.

config.name: spark.sql.legacy.parquet.int96RebaseModeInRead
config.doc: When LEGACY, Spark will rebase INT96 timestamps from the legacy hybrid (Julian + Gregorian) calendar to Proleptic Gregorian calendar when reading Parquet files. When CORRECTED, Spark will not do rebase and read the timestamps as it is. When EXCEPTION, which is the default, Spark will fail the reading if it sees ancient timestamps that are ambiguous between the two calendars. This config is only effective if the writer info (like Spark, Hive) of the Parquet files is unknown.

config.name: spark.sql.bucketing.coalesceBucketsInJoin.enabled
config.doc: When true, if two bucketed tables with the different number of buckets are joined, the side with a bigger number of buckets will be coalesced to have the same number of buckets as the other side. Bigger number of buckets is divisible by the smaller number of buckets. Bucket coalescing is applied to sort-merge joins and shuffled hash join. Note: Coalescing bucketed table can avoid unnecessary shuffling in join, but it also reduces parallelism and could possibly cause OOM for shuffled hash join.

config.name: spark.sql.bucketing.coalesceBucketsInJoin.maxBucketRatio
config.doc: The ratio of the number of two buckets being coalesced should be less than or equal to this value for bucket coalescing to be applied. This configuration only has an effect when '${COALESCE_BUCKETS_IN_JOIN_ENABLED.key}' is set to true.

config.name: spark.sql.execution.broadcastHashJoin.outputPartitioningExpandLimit
config.doc: The maximum number of partitionings that a HashPartitioning can be expanded to. This configuration is applicable only for BroadcastHashJoin inner joins and can be set to '0' to disable this feature.

config.name: spark.sql.optimizeNullAwareAntiJoin
config.doc: When true, NULL-aware anti join execution can be planned as BroadcastHashJoinExec with flag isNullAwareAntiJoin enabled, optimized from O(M*N) calculation into O(M) calculation using Hash lookup instead of Looping lookup. Only support for singleColumn NAAJ for now. The optimization is also controlled by spark.sql.optimizeNullAwareAntiJoin.broadcastThreshold.

config.name: spark.sql.legacy.castComplexTypesToString.enabled
config.doc: When true, maps and structs are wrapped by [] in casting to strings, and NULL elements of structs/maps/arrays will be omitted while converting to strings. Otherwise, if this is false, which is the default, maps and structs are wrapped by {}, and NULL elements will be converted to "null".

config.name: spark.sql.legacy.pathOptionBehavior.enabled
config.doc: When true, "path" option is overwritten if one path parameter is passed to DataFrameReader.load(), DataFrameWriter.save(), DataStreamReader.load(), or DataStreamWriter.start(). Also, "path" option is added to the overall paths if multiple path parameters are passed to DataFrameReader.load()

config.name: spark.sql.legacy.extraOptionsBehavior.enabled
config.doc: When true, the extra options will be ignored for DataFrameReader.table(). If set it to false, which is the default, Spark will check if the extra options have the same key, but the value is different with the table serde properties. If the check passes, the extra options will be merged with the serde properties as the scan options. Otherwise, an exception will be thrown.

config.name: spark.sql.sources.disabledJdbcConnProviderList
config.doc: Configures a list of JDBC connection providers, which are disabled. The list contains the name of the JDBC connection providers separated by comma.

config.name: spark.sql.legacy.createHiveTableByDefault
config.doc: When set to true, CREATE TABLE syntax without USING or STORED AS will use Hive instead of the value of ${DEFAULT_DATA_SOURCE_NAME.key} as the table provider.

config.name: spark.sql.legacy.charVarcharAsString
config.doc: When true, Spark treats CHAR/VARCHAR type the same as STRING type, which is the behavior of Spark 3.0 and earlier. This means no length check for CHAR/VARCHAR type and no padding for CHAR type when writing data to the table.

config.name: spark.sql.legacy.keepCommandOutputSchema
config.doc: When true, Spark will keep the output schema of commands such as SHOW DATABASES unchanged.

config.name: spark.sql.cache.serializer
config.doc: The name of a class that implements org.apache.spark.sql.columnar.CachedBatchSerializer. It will be used to translate SQL data into a format that can more efficiently be cached. The underlying API is subject to change so use with caution. Multiple classes cannot be specified. The class must have a no-arg constructor. Available implementations include: org.apache.spark.sql.execution.columnar.DefaultCachedBatchSerializer (default) and org.apache.spark.sql.execution.columnar.ArrowCachedBatchSerializer (Arrow format with zero-copy columnar reads and better Arrow ecosystem interoperability).

config.name: spark.sql.metadataCacheTTLSeconds
config.doc: Time-to-live (TTL) value for the metadata caches: partition file metadata cache and session catalog cache. This configuration only has an effect when this value having a positive value (> 0). It also requires setting '${StaticSQLConf.CATALOG_IMPLEMENTATION.key}' to `hive`, setting '${SQLConf.HIVE_FILESOURCE_PARTITION_FILE_CACHE_SIZE.key}' > 0 and setting '${SQLConf.HIVE_MANAGE_FILESOURCE_PARTITIONS.key}' to `true` to be applied to the partition file metadata cache.

config.name: spark.sql.streaming.ui.enabledCustomMetricList
config.doc: Configures a list of custom metrics on Structured Streaming UI, which are enabled. The list contains the name of the custom metrics separated by comma. In aggregation only sum used.
