config.doc: The max number of retries to reconnect. After spark.worker.initialRegistrationRetries attempts, the interval is between 30 and 90 seconds.

config.name: spark.worker.idPattern
config.doc: The pattern for worker ID generation based on Java `String.format` method. The default value is `worker-%s-%s-%d` which represents the existing worker id string, e.g., `worker-20231109183042-[fe80::1%lo0]-39729`. Please be careful to generate unique IDs

config.name: spark.default.parallelism
config.doc: Default number of partitions in RDDs returned by transformations like join, reduceByKey, and parallelize when not set by user. For distributed shuffle operations like reduceByKey and join, the largest number of partitions in a parent RDD. For operations like parallelize with no parent RDDs, it depends on the cluster manager. For example in Local mode, it defaults to the number of cores on the local machine

config.name: spark.driver.minMemoryOverhead
config.doc: The minimum amount of non-heap memory to be allocated per driver in cluster mode, in MiB unless otherwise specified. This value is ignored if spark.driver.memoryOverhead is set directly.

config.name: spark.log.structuredLogging.enabled
config.doc: When true, Spark logs are output as structured JSON lines with added Spark Mapped Diagnostic Context (MDC), facilitating easier integration with log aggregation and analysis tools. When false, logs are plain text without MDC. This configuration does not apply to interactive environments such as spark-shell, spark-sql, and PySpark shell.

config.name: spark.log.legacyTaskNameMdc.enabled
config.doc: When true, the MDC (Mapped Diagnostic Context) key `mdc.taskName` will be set in the log output, which is the behavior of Spark version 3.1 through Spark 3.5 releases. When false, the logging framework will use `task_name` as the MDC key, aligning it with the naming convention of newer MDC keys introduced in Spark 4.0 release.

config.name: spark.driver.log.localDir
config.doc: Specifies a local directory to write driver logs and enable Driver Log UI Tab.

config.name: spark.eventLog.includeTaskMetricsAccumulators
config.doc: Whether to include TaskMetrics' underlying accumulator values in the event log (as part of the Task/Stage/Job metrics' 'Accumulables' fields. The TaskMetrics values are already logged in the 'Task Metrics' fields (so the accumulator updates are redundant). This flag defaults to true for behavioral backwards compatibility for applications that might rely on the redundant logging. See SPARK-42204 for details.

config.name: spark.executor.minMemoryOverhead
config.doc: The minimum amount of non-heap memory to be allocated per executor in MiB unless otherwise specified. This value is ignored if spark.executor.memoryOverhead is set directly.

config.name: spark.scheduler.listenerbus.exitTimeout
config.doc: The time that event queue waits until the dispatch thread exits when stop is invoked. This is set to 0 by default for graceful shutdown of the event queue, but allow the user to configure the waiting time.

config.name: spark.driver.timeout
config.doc: A timeout for Spark driver in minutes. 0 means infinite. For the positive time value, terminate the driver with the exit code 124 if it runs after timeout duration. To use, it's required to set `spark.plugins=org.apache.spark.deploy.DriverTimeoutPlugin`.

config.name: spark.checkpoint.dir
config.doc: Set the default directory for checkpointing. It can be overwritten by SparkContext.setCheckpointDir.

config.name: spark.shuffle.file.merge.buffer
config.doc: Size of the in-memory buffer for each shuffle file input stream, in KiB unless otherwise specified. These buffers use off-heap buffers and are related to the number of files in the shuffle file. Too large buffers should be avoided.

config.name: spark.shuffle.localDisk.file.output.buffer
config.doc: The file system for this buffer size after each partition is written in all local disk shuffle writers. In KiB unless otherwise specified.

config.name: spark.kubernetes.jars.avoidDownloadSchemes
config.doc: Comma-separated list of schemes for which jars will NOT be downloaded to the driver local disk prior to be distributed to executors, only for kubernetes deployment. For use in cases when the jars are big and executor counts are high, concurrent download causes network saturation and timeouts. Wildcard '*' is denoted to not downloading jars for any the schemes.

config.name: spark.scheduler.numCancelledJobGroupsToTrack
config.doc: The maximum number of tracked job groups that are cancelled with `cancelJobGroupAndFutureJobs`. If this maximum number is hit, the oldest job group will no longer be tracked that future jobs belonging to this job group will not be cancelled.

config.name: spark.master.rest.host
config.doc: Specifies the host of the Master REST API endpoint

config.name: spark.master.rest.maxThreads
config.doc: Maximum number of threads to use in the Spark Master REST API Server.

config.name: spark.master.rest.filters
config.doc: Comma separated list of filter class names to apply to the Spark Master REST API.

config.name: spark.master.rest.virtualThread.enabled
config.doc: If true, Spark master tries to use Java 21 virtual thread for REST API.

config.name: spark.master.ui.historyServerUrl
config.doc: The URL where Spark history server is running. Please note that this assumes that all Spark jobs share the same event log location where the history server accesses.

config.name: spark.master.useAppNameAsAppId.enabled
config.doc: (Experimental) If true, Spark master uses the user-provided appName for appId.

config.name: spark.master.useDriverIdAsAppName.enabled
config.doc: (Experimental) If true, Spark master tries to set driver ID as appName.

config.name: spark.io.compression.zstd.workers
config.doc: Thread size spawned to compress in parallel when using Zstd. When the value is 0, no worker is spawned, it works in single-threaded mode. When value > 0, it triggers asynchronous mode, corresponding number of threads are spawned. More workers improve performance, but also increase memory cost.

config.name: spark.io.compression.lzf.parallel.enabled
config.doc: When true, LZF compression will use multiple threads to compress data in parallel.

config.name: spark.executor.syncLogLevel.enabled
config.doc: If set to true, log level applied through SparkContext.setLogLevel() method will be propagated to all executors.

config.name: spark.stage.maxConsecutiveAttempts
config.doc: Number of consecutive stage attempts allowed before a stage is aborted.

config.name: spark.scheduler.stage.legacyAbortAfterKillTasks
config.doc: Whether to abort a stage after TaskScheduler.killAllTaskAttempts(). This is used to restore the original behavior in case there are any regressions after abort stage is removed

config.name: spark.scheduler.dropTaskInfoAccumulablesOnTaskCompletion.enabled
config.doc: If true, the task info accumulables will be cleared upon task completion in TaskSetManager. This reduces the heap usage of the driver by only referencing the task info accumulables for the active tasks and not for completed tasks.

config.name: spark.shutdown.timeout
config.doc: Defines the timeout period to wait for all shutdown hooks to be executed. This must be passed as a system property argument in the Java options, for example spark.driver.extraJavaOptions="-Dspark.shutdown.timeout=60s".

config.name: spark.api.mode
config.doc: For Spark Classic applications, specify whether to automatically use Spark Connect by running a local Spark Connect server dedicated to the application. The server is terminated when the application is terminated. The value can be `classic` or `connect`.

config.name: spark.kubernetes.legacy.useReadWriteOnceAccessMode
config.doc: If true, use ReadWriteOnce instead of ReadWriteOncePod as persistence volume access mode.

config.name: spark.yarn.client.statCache.preload.enabled
config.doc: Enables statCache to be preloaded at YARN client side. This feature analyzes the pattern of resources paths, and if multiple resources shared the same parent directory, a single listStatus will be invoked on the parent directory instead of multiple getFileStatus on individual resources. If most resources are from a small set of directories, this can improve job submission time. Enabling this feature may potentially increase client memory overhead.

config.name: spark.yarn.client.statCache.preload.perDirectoryThreshold
config.doc: Minimum resource count in a directory to trigger statCache preloading when submitting an application. If the number of resources in a directory, without any wildcards, equals or exceeds this threshold, the statCache for that directory will be preloaded. This configuration will only take effect when spark.yarn.client.statCache.preloaded.enabled option is enabled.

config.name: spark.sql.analyzer.singlePassResolver.enabled
config.doc: When true, use the single-pass Resolver instead of the fixed-point Analyzer. This is an alternative Analyzer framework, which resolves the parsed logical plan in a single post-order traversal. It uses ExpressionResolver to resolve expressions and NameScope to control the visibility of names. In contrast to the current fixed-point framework, subsequent in-tree traversals are disallowed. Most of the fixed-point Analyzer code is reused in the form of specific node transformation functions (AliasResolution.resolve, FunctionResolution.resolveFunction, etc). This feature is currently under development.

config.name: spark.sql.analyzer.singlePassResolver.dualRunWithLegacy
config.doc: When true, run both analyzers to check if single-pass Analyzer correctly produces the same analyzed plan as the fixed-point Analyzer for the existing set of features defined in the ResolverGuard

config.name: spark.sql.analyzer.singlePassResolver.returnSinglePassResultInDualRun
config.doc: When true, return the result of the single-pass resolver as the result of the dual run analysis (which is used if the ANALYZER_DUAL_RUN_LEGACY_AND_SINGLE_PASS_RESOLVER flag value is true). Otherwise, return the result of the fixed-point analyzer.

config.name: spark.sql.analyzer.singlePassResolver.validationEnabled
config.doc: When true, validate the Resolver output with ResolutionValidator. The ResolutionValidator validates the resolved logical plan tree in one pass and asserts the internal contracts. It uses the ExpressionResolutionValidator internally to validate resolved expression trees in the same manner.

config.name: spark.sql.analyzer.singlePassResolver.relationBridging.enabled
config.doc: When set to true, the single-pass Resolver will reuse the relation metadata that was previously resolved in fixed-point run. This makes sense only in ANALYZER_DUAL_RUN_LEGACY_AND_SINGLE_PASS_RESOLVER mode. In that case HybridAnalyzer enables the AnalyzerBridgeState and passes it to the single-pass Analyzer after the fixed-point run is complete. Single-pass Resolver uses this AnalyzerBridgeState to construct a special RelationMetadataProvider implementation - BridgedRelationMetadataProvider. This component simply reuses cached relation metadata and avoids any blocking calls (catalog RPCs or table metadata reads).

config.name: spark.sql.expressionTreeChangeLog.level
config.doc: Configures the log level for logging the change from the unresolved expression tree to the resolved expression tree in the single-pass bottom-up Resolver. The value can be ${VALID_LOG_LEVELS.mkString()}.

config.name: spark.sql.lightweightPlanChangeValidation
config.doc: Similar to ${PLAN_CHANGE_VALIDATION.key}, this validates plan changes and runs after every rule, however it is enabled by default and so it should be lightweight.

config.name: spark.sql.extendedExplainProviders
config.doc: A comma-separated list of classes that implement the org.apache.spark.sql.ExtendedExplainGenerator trait. If provided, Spark will print extended plan information from the providers in explain plan and in the UI

config.name: spark.sql.inMemoryColumnarStorage.hugeVectorReserveRatio
config.doc: When spark.sql.inMemoryColumnarStorage.hugeVectorThreshold <= 0 or the required memory is smaller than spark.sql.inMemoryColumnarStorage.hugeVectorThreshold, spark reserves required memory * 2 memory; otherwise, spark reserves required memory * this ratio memory, and will release this column vector memory before reading the next batch rows.

config.name: spark.sql.inMemoryColumnarStorage.hugeVectorThreshold
config.doc: When the required memory is larger than this, spark reserves required memory * ${VECTORIZED_HUGE_VECTOR_RESERVE_RATIO.key} memory next time and release this column vector memory before reading the next batch rows. -1 means disabling the optimization.

config.name: spark.sql.adaptive.applyFinalStageShuffleOptimizations
config.doc: Configures whether adaptive query execution (if enabled) should apply shuffle coalescing and local shuffle read optimization for the final query stage.

config.name: spark.sql.collation.allowInMapKeys
config.doc: Allow for non-UTF8_BINARY collated strings inside of map's keys

config.name: spark.sql.collation.objectLevel.enabled
config.doc: Object level collations feature is under development and its use should be done under this feature flag. The feature allows setting default collation for all underlying columns within that object, except the ones that were previously created.

config.name: spark.sql.collation.trim.enabled
config.doc: When enabled allows the use of trim collations which trim trailing whitespaces from strings.

config.name: spark.sql.icu.caseMappings.enabled
config.doc: When enabled we use the ICU library (instead of the JVM) to implement case mappings for strings under UTF8_BINARY collation.

config.name: spark.sql.parser.eagerEvalOfUnresolvedInlineTable
config.doc: Controls whether we optimize the ASTree that gets generated when parsing VALUES lists (UnresolvedInlineTable) by eagerly evaluating it in the AST Builder.

config.name: spark.sql.execution.interruptOnCancel
config.doc: When true, all running tasks will be interrupted if one cancels a query.

config.name: spark.sql.dataSource.skipAssertOnPredicatePushdown
config.doc: Enable skipping assert when expression in not translated to predicate.

config.name: spark.sql.binaryOutputStyle
config.doc: The output style used display binary data. Valid values are 'UTF-8', 'BASIC', 'BASE64', 'HEX', and 'HEX_DISCRETE'.

config.name: spark.sql.sources.v2.bucketing.shuffle.enabled
config.doc: During a storage-partitioned join, whether to allow to shuffle only one side. When only one side is KeyedPartitioning, if the conditions are met, spark will only shuffle the other side. This optimization will reduce the amount of data that needs to be shuffle. This config requires ${V2_BUCKETING_ENABLED.key} to be enabled

config.name: spark.sql.sources.v2.bucketing.allowJoinKeysSubsetOfPartitionKeys.enabled
config.doc: Whether to allow storage-partition join in the case where join keys are a subset of the partition keys of the source tables. At planning time, Spark will group the partitions by only those keys that are in the join keys. This is currently enabled only if ${REQUIRE_ALL_CLUSTER_KEYS_FOR_DISTRIBUTION.key} is false.

config.name: spark.sql.sources.v2.bucketing.allowCompatibleTransforms.enabled
config.doc: Whether to allow storage-partition join in the case where the partition transforms are compatible but not identical. This config requires both ${V2_BUCKETING_ENABLED.key} and ${V2_BUCKETING_PUSH_PART_VALUES_ENABLED.key} to be enabled and ${V2_BUCKETING_PARTIALLY_CLUSTERED_DISTRIBUTION_ENABLED.key} to be disabled.

config.name: spark.sql.sources.v2.bucketing.partition.filter.enabled
config.doc: Whether to filter partitions when running storage-partition join. When enabled, partitions without matches on the other side can be omitted for scanning, if allowed by the join type. This config requires both ${V2_BUCKETING_ENABLED.key} and ${V2_BUCKETING_PUSH_PART_VALUES_ENABLED.key} to be enabled.

config.name: spark.sql.sources.v2.bucketing.sorting.enabled
config.doc: When turned on, Spark will recognize the specific distribution reported by a V2 data source through SupportsReportPartitioning, and will try to avoid a shuffle if possible when sorting by those columns. This config requires ${V2_BUCKETING_ENABLED.key} to be enabled.

config.name: spark.sql.defaultCacheStorageLevel
config.doc: The default storage level of `dataset.cache()`, `catalog.cacheTable()` and sql query `CACHE TABLE t`.

config.name: spark.sql.dataframeCache.logLevel
config.doc: Configures the log level of Dataframe cache operations, including adding and removing entries from Dataframe cache, hit and miss on cache application. This log should only be used for debugging purposes and not in the production environment, since it generates a large amount of logs.

config.name: spark.sql.legacy.viewSchemaBindingMode
config.doc: Set to false to disable the WITH SCHEMA clause for view DDL and suppress the line in DESCRIBE EXTENDED and SHOW CREATE TABLE.

config.name: spark.sql.legacy.viewSchemaCompensation
config.doc: Set to false to revert default view schema binding mode from WITH SCHEMA COMPENSATION to WITH SCHEMA BINDING.

config.name: spark.sql.sources.useListFilesFileSystemList
config.doc: A comma-separated list of file system schemes to use FileSystem.listFiles API for a single root path listing

config.name: spark.sql.transposeMaxValues
config.doc: When doing a transpose without specifying values for the index column this is the maximum number of values that will be transposed without error.

config.name: spark.sql.codegen.broadcastCleanedSourceThreshold
config.doc: A threshold (in string length) to determine if we should make the generated code a broadcast variable in whole stage codegen. To disable this, set the threshold to < 0; otherwise if the size is above the threshold, it'll use broadcast variable. Note that maximum string length allowed in Java is Integer.MAX_VALUE, so anything above it would be meaningless. The default value is set to -1 (disabled by default).

config.name: spark.sql.files.ignoreInvalidPartitionPaths
config.doc: Whether to ignore invalid partition paths that do not match <column>=<value>. When the option is enabled, table with two partition directories 'table/invalid' and 'table/col=1' will only load the latter directory and ignore the invalid partition

config.name: spark.sql.streaming.stateStore.numStateStoreMaintenanceThreads
config.doc: Total number of threads split between the snapshot and cleanup maintenance pools for stateful streaming queries. Each pool needs at least 1 thread, so the minimum is 2. The default value is the number of cores * 0.25 so that the pools don't take too many resources away from the query and affect performance. Use snapshotToCleanupThreadRatio to configure the split between snapshot and cleanup pools.

config.name: spark.sql.streaming.flatMapGroupsWithState.skipEmittingInitialStateKeys
config.doc: When true, the flatMapGroupsWithState operation in a streaming query will not emit results for the initial state keys of each group.

config.name: spark.sql.streaming.ratioExtraSpaceAllowedInCheckpoint
config.doc: The ratio of extra space allowed for batch deletion of files when maintenance isinvoked. When value > 0, it optimizes the cost of discovering and deleting old checkpoint versions. The minimum number of stale versions we retain in checkpoint location for batch deletion is calculated by minBatchesToRetain * ratioExtraSpaceAllowedInCheckpoint.

config.name: spark.sql.streaming.transformWithState.stateSchemaVersion
config.doc: The version of the state schema used by the transformWithState operator

config.name: spark.sql.streaming.stateStore.checkpointFormatVersion
config.doc: The version of the approach of doing state store checkpoint

config.name: spark.sql.streaming.stateStore.maxNumStateSchemaFiles
config.doc: The maximum number of StateSchemaV3 files allowed per operator

config.name: spark.sql.streaming.stateStore.encodingFormat
config.doc: The encoding format used for stateful operators to store information in the state store

config.name: spark.sql.streaming.stateStore.valueStateSchemaEvolutionThreshold
config.doc: The maximum number of value state schema evolutions allowed per column family

config.name: spark.sql.streaming.triggerAvailableNowWrapper.enabled
config.doc: Whether to use the wrapper implementation of Trigger.AvailableNow if the source does not support Trigger.AvailableNow. Enabling this allows the benefits of Trigger.AvailableNow with sources which don't support it, but some sources may show unexpected behavior including duplication, data loss, etc. So use with extreme care! The ideal direction is to persuade developers of source(s) to support Trigger.AvailableNow.

config.name: spark.sql.streaming.optimizeOneRowPlan.enabled
config.doc: When true, enable OptimizeOneRowPlan rule for the case where the child is a streaming Dataset. This is a fallback flag to revert the 'incorrect' behavior, hence this configuration must not be used without understanding in depth. Use this only to quickly recover failure in existing query!

config.name: spark.sql.optimizer.avoidCollapseUDFWithExpensiveExpr
config.doc: Whether to avoid collapsing projections that would duplicate expensive expressions in UDFs.

config.name: spark.sql.statistics.updatePartitionStatsInAnalyzeTable.enabled
config.doc: When this config is enabled, Spark will also update partition statistics in analyze table command (i.e., ANALYZE TABLE .. COMPUTE STATISTICS [NOSCAN]). Note the command will also become more expensive. When this config is disabled, Spark will only update table level statistics.

config.name: spark.sql.shuffleDependency.skipMigration.enabled
config.doc: When enabled, shuffle dependencies for a Spark Connect SQL execution are marked at the end of the execution, and they will not be migrated during decommissions.

config.name: spark.sql.shuffleDependency.fileCleanup.enabled
config.doc: (Deprecated since Spark 4.1, please set 'spark.sql.connect.shuffleDependency.fileCleanup.enabled'.)

config.name: spark.sql.pyspark.udf.profiler
config.doc: Configure the Python/Pandas UDF profiler by enabling or disabling it with the option to choose between "perf" and "memory" types, or unsetting the config disables the profiler. This is disabled by default.

config.name: spark.sql.execution.pyspark.udf.faulthandler.enabled
config.doc: Same as ${Python.PYTHON_WORKER_FAULTHANLDER_ENABLED.key} for Python execution with DataFrame and SQL. It can change during runtime.

config.name: spark.sql.execution.pyspark.udf.idleTimeoutSeconds
config.doc: Same as ${Python.PYTHON_WORKER_IDLE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS.key} for Python execution with DataFrame and SQL. It can change during runtime.

config.name: spark.sql.pyspark.plotting.max_rows
config.doc: The visual limit on plots. If set to 1000 for top-n-based plots (pie, bar, barh), the first 1000 data points will be used for plotting. For sampled-based plots (scatter, area, line), 1000 data points will be randomly sampled.

config.name: spark.sql.execution.arrow.maxBytesPerBatch
config.doc: When using Apache Arrow, limit the maximum bytes in each batch that can be written to a single ArrowRecordBatch in memory. Unlike 'spark.sql.execution.arrow.maxRecordsPerBatch', this configuration does not work for createDataFrame/toPandas with Arrow/pandas instances. See also spark.sql.execution.arrow.maxRecordsPerBatch. If both are set, each batch is created when any condition of both is met.

config.name: spark.sql.execution.arrow.transformWithStateInPandas.maxRecordsPerBatch
config.doc: When using TransformWithStateInPandas, limit the maximum number of state records that can be written to a single ArrowRecordBatch in memory.

config.name: spark.sql.execution.python.udf.maxRecordsPerBatch
config.doc: When using Python UDFs, limit the maximum number of records that can be batched for serialization/deserialization.

config.name: spark.sql.execution.python.udf.buffer.size
config.doc: Same as `${BUFFER_SIZE.key}` but only applies to Python UDF executions. If it is not set, the fallback is `${BUFFER_SIZE.key}`.

config.name: spark.sql.execution.pyspark.udf.hideTraceback.enabled
config.doc: When true, only show the message of the exception from Python UDFs, hiding the stack trace. If this is enabled, simplifiedTraceback has no effect.

config.name: spark.sql.execution.pythonUDF.arrow.concurrency.level
config.doc: The level of concurrency to execute Arrow-optimized Python UDF. This can be useful if Python UDFs use I/O intensively.

config.name: spark.sql.planner.pythonExecution.memory
config.doc: Specifies the memory allocation for executing Python code in Spark driver, in MiB. When set, it caps the memory for Python execution to the specified amount. If not set, Spark will not limit Python's memory usage and it is up to the application to avoid exceeding the overhead memory space shared with other non-JVM processes. Note: Windows does not support resource limiting and actual resource is not limited on MacOS.

config.name: spark.sql.scripting.enabled
config.doc: SQL Scripting feature is under development and its use should be done under this feature flag. SQL Scripting enables users to write procedural SQL including control flow and error handling.

config.name: spark.sql.legacy.disableMapKeyNormalization
config.doc: Disables key normalization when creating a map with `ArrayBasedMapBuilder`. When set to `true` it will prevent key normalization when building a map, which will allow for values such as `-0.0` and `0.0` to be present as distinct keys.

config.name: spark.sql.chunkBase64String.enabled
config.doc: Whether to truncate string generated by the `Base64` function. When true, base64 strings generated by the base64 function are chunked into lines of at most 76 characters. When false, the base64 strings are not chunked.

config.name: spark.sql.alwaysInlineCommonExpr
config.doc: When true, always inline common expressions instead of using the WITH expression. This may lead to duplicated expressions and the config should only be enabled if you hit bugs caused by the WITH expression.

config.name: spark.sql.useCommonExprIdForAlias
config.doc: When true, use the common expression ID for the alias when rewriting With expressions. Otherwise, use the index of the common expression definition. When true this avoids duplicate alias names, but is helpful to set to false for testing to ensure that alias names are consistent.

config.name: spark.sql.optimizer.decorrelateLimit.enabled
config.doc: Decorrelate subqueries with correlation under LIMIT.

config.name: spark.sql.optimizer.decorrelateOffset.enabled
config.doc: Decorrelate subqueries with correlation under LIMIT with OFFSET.

config.name: spark.sql.optimizer.decorrelateUnionOrSetOpUnderLimit.enabled
config.doc: Decorrelate UNION or SET operation under LIMIT operator. If not enabled,revert to legacy incorrect behavior for certain subqueries with correlation underUNION/SET operator with a LIMIT operator above it.

config.name: spark.sql.optimizer.decorrelateExistsSubqueryLegacyIncorrectCountHandling.enabled
config.doc: If enabled, revert to legacy incorrect behavior for certain EXISTS/IN subqueries with COUNT or similar aggregates.

config.name: spark.sql.optimizer.decorrelateSubqueryPreventConstantHoldingForCountBug.enabled
config.doc: If enabled, prevents constant folding in subqueries that contain a COUNT-bug-susceptible Aggregate.

config.name: spark.sql.optimizer.pullOutNestedDataOuterRefExpressions.enabled
config.doc: Handle correlation over nested data extract expressions by pulling out the expression into the outer plan. This enables correlation on map attributes for example.

config.name: spark.sql.optimizer.wrapExistsInAggregateFunction
config.doc: When true, the optimizer will wrap newly introduced `exists` attributes in an aggregate function to ensure that Aggregate nodes preserve semantic invariant that each variable among agg expressions appears either in grouping expressions or belongs to and aggregate function.

config.name: spark.sql.optimizer.pruneFiltersCanPruneStreamingSubplan
config.doc: Allow PruneFilters to remove streaming subplans when we encounter a false filter. This flag is to restore prior buggy behavior for broken pipelines.

config.name: spark.sql.artifact.isolation.enabled
config.doc: When enabled for a Spark Session, artifacts (such as JARs, files, archives) added to this session are isolated from other sessions within the same Spark instance. When disabled for a session, artifacts added to this session are visible to other sessions that have this config disabled. This config can only be set during the creation of a Spark Session and will have no effect when changed in the middle of session usage.

config.name: spark.sql.artifact.isolation.alwaysApplyClassloader
config.doc: When enabled, the classloader holding per-session artifacts will always be applied during SQL executions (useful for Spark Connect). When disabled, the classloader will be applied only when any artifact is added to the session.

config.name: spark.sql.avro.xz.level
config.doc: Compression level for the xz codec used in writing of AVRO files. Valid value must be in the range of from 1 to 9 inclusive The default value is 6.

config.name: spark.sql.avro.zstandard.level
config.doc: Compression level for the zstandard codec used in writing of AVRO files.

config.name: spark.sql.avro.zstandard.bufferPool.enabled
config.doc: If true, enable buffer pool of ZSTD JNI library when writing of AVRO files

config.name: spark.sql.legacy.inlineCTEInCommands
config.doc: If true, always inline the CTE relations for the queries in commands. This is the legacy behavior which may produce incorrect results because Spark may evaluate a CTE relation more than once, even if it's nondeterministic.

config.name: spark.sql.legacy.mssqlserver.datetimeoffsetMapping.enabled
config.doc: When true, DATETIMEOFFSET is mapped to StringType; otherwise, it is mapped to TimestampType.

config.name: spark.sql.legacy.mysql.bitArrayMapping.enabled
config.doc: When true, use LongType to represent MySQL BIT(n>1); otherwise, use BinaryType.

config.name: spark.sql.legacy.mysql.timestampNTZMapping.enabled
config.doc: When true, TimestampNTZType and MySQL TIMESTAMP can be converted bidirectionally. For reading, MySQL TIMESTAMP is converted to TimestampNTZType when JDBC read option preferTimestampNTZ is true. For writing, TimestampNTZType is converted to MySQL TIMESTAMP; otherwise, DATETIME

config.name: spark.sql.legacy.oracle.timestampMapping.enabled
config.doc: When true, TimestampType maps to TIMESTAMP in Oracle; otherwise, TIMESTAMP WITH LOCAL TIME ZONE.

config.name: spark.sql.legacy.db2.numericMapping.enabled
config.doc: When true, SMALLINT maps to IntegerType in DB2; otherwise, ShortType

config.name: spark.sql.legacy.db2.booleanMapping.enabled
config.doc: When true, BooleanType maps to CHAR(1) in DB2; otherwise, BOOLEAN

config.name: spark.sql.legacy.postgres.datetimeMapping.enabled
config.doc: When true, TimestampType maps to TIMESTAMP WITHOUT TIME ZONE in PostgreSQL for writing; otherwise, TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE. When true, TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE can be converted to TimestampNTZType when JDBC read option preferTimestampNTZ is true; otherwise, converted to TimestampType regardless of preferTimestampNTZ.

config.name: spark.sql.json.enableExactStringParsing
config.doc: When set to true, string columns extracted from JSON objects will be extracted exactly as they appear in the input string, with no changes

config.name: spark.sql.json.useUnsafeRow
config.doc: When set to true, use UnsafeRow to represent struct result in the JSON parser. It can be overwritten by the JSON option `useUnsafeRow`.

config.name: spark.sql.variant.allowDuplicateKeys
config.doc: When set to false, parsing variant from JSON will throw an error if there are duplicate keys in the input JSON object. When set to true, the parser will keep the last occurrence of all fields with the same key.

config.name: spark.sql.variant.allowReadingShredded
config.doc: When true, the Parquet reader is allowed to read shredded or unshredded variant. When false, it only reads unshredded variant.

config.name: spark.sql.variant.pushVariantIntoScan
config.doc: When true, replace variant type in the scan schema with a struct containing requested fields.

config.name: spark.sql.variant.writeShredding.enabled
config.doc: When true, the Parquet writer is allowed to write shredded variant.

config.name: spark.sql.variant.forceShreddingSchemaForTest
config.doc: FOR INTERNAL TESTING ONLY. Sets shredding schema for Variant.

config.name: spark.sql.legacy.duplicateBetweenInput
config.doc: When true, we use legacy between implementation. This is a flag that fixes a problem introduced by a between optimization, see ticket SPARK-49063.

config.name: spark.sql.preserveCharVarcharTypeInfo
config.doc: When true, Spark does not replace CHAR/VARCHAR types the STRING type, which is the default behavior of Spark 3.0 and earlier versions. This means the length checks for CHAR/VARCHAR types is enforced and CHAR type is also properly padded.

config.name: spark.sql.legacy.readFileSourceTableCacheIgnoreOptions
config.doc: When set to true, reading from file source table caches the first query plan and ignores subsequent changes in query options. Otherwise, query options will be applied to the cached plan and may produce different results.

config.name: spark.sql.legacy.noCharPaddingInPredicate
config.doc: When true, Spark will not apply char type padding for CHAR type columns in string comparison predicates, when '${READ_SIDE_CHAR_PADDING.key}' is false.

config.name: spark.sql.execution.pandas.inferPandasDictAsMap
config.doc: When true, spark.createDataFrame will infer dict from Pandas DataFrame as a MapType. When false, spark.createDataFrame infers dict from Pandas DataFrame as a StructType which is default inferring from PyArrow.

config.name: spark.sql.pyspark.legacy.inferMapTypeFromFirstPair.enabled
config.doc: PySpark's SparkSession.createDataFrame infers the key/value types of a map from all pairs in the map by default. If this config is set to true, it restores the legacy behavior of only inferring the type from the first non-null pair.

config.name: spark.sql.legacy.avro.allowIncompatibleSchema
config.doc: When set to false, if types in Avro are encoded in the same format, but the type in the Avro schema explicitly says that the data types are different, reject reading the data type in the format to avoid returning incorrect results. When set to true, it restores the legacy behavior of allow reading the data in the format, which may return incorrect results.

config.name: spark.sql.optimizer.decorrelateJoinPredicate.enabled
config.doc: Decorrelate scalar and lateral subqueries with correlated references in join predicates. This configuration is only effective when '${DECORRELATE_INNER_QUERY_ENABLED.key}' is true.

config.name: spark.sql.optimizer.decorrelatePredicateSubqueriesInJoinPredicate.enabled
config.doc: Decorrelate predicate (in and exists) subqueries with correlated references in join predicates.

config.name: spark.sql.optimizer.optimizeUncorrelatedInSubqueriesInJoinCondition.enabled
config.doc: When true, optimize uncorrelated IN subqueries in join predicates by rewriting them to joins. This interacts with ${LEGACY_NULL_IN_EMPTY_LIST_BEHAVIOR.key} because it can rewrite IN predicates.

config.name: spark.sql.optimizer.excludeSubqueryRefsFromRemoveRedundantAliases.enabled
config.doc: When true, exclude the references from the subquery expressions (in, exists, etc.) while removing redundant aliases.

config.name: spark.sql.timeTravelTimestampKey
config.doc: The option name to specify the time travel timestamp when reading a table.

config.name: spark.sql.timeTravelVersionKey
config.doc: The option name to specify the time travel table version when reading a table.

config.name: spark.sql.operatorPipeSyntaxEnabled
config.doc: If true, enable operator pipe syntax for Apache Spark SQL. This uses the operator pipe marker |> to indicate separation between clauses of SQL in a manner that describes the sequence of steps that the query performs in a composable fashion.

config.name: spark.sql.legacy.raiseErrorWithoutErrorClass
config.doc: When set to true, restores the legacy behavior of `raise_error` and `assert_true` to not return the `[USER_RAISED_EXCEPTION]` prefix. For example, `raise_error('error!')` returns `error!` instead of `[USER_RAISED_EXCEPTION] Error!`.

config.name: spark.sql.legacy.scalarSubqueryCountBugBehavior
config.doc: When set to true, restores legacy behavior of potential incorrect count bug handling for scalar subqueries.

config.name: spark.sql.legacy.scalarSubqueryAllowGroupByNonEqualityCorrelatedPredicate
config.doc: When set to true, use incorrect legacy behavior for checking whether a scalar subquery with a group-by on correlated columns is allowed. See SPARK-48503

config.name: spark.sql.analyzer.scalarSubqueryAllowGroupByColumnEqualToConstant
config.doc: When set to true, allow scalar subqueries with group-by on a column that also has an equality filter with a constant (SPARK-48557).

config.name: spark.sql.optimizer.scalarSubqueryUseSingleJoin
config.doc: When set to true, use LEFT_SINGLE join for correlated scalar subqueries where optimizer can't prove that only 1 row will be returned

config.name: spark.sql.analyzer.allowSubqueryExpressionsInLambdasOrHigherOrderFunctions
config.doc: When set to false, the analyzer will throw an error if a subquery expression appears in a lambda function or higher-order function. When set to true, it restores the legacy behavior of allowing subquery eexpressions in lambda functions or higher-order functions.

config.name: spark.sql.files.supportSecondOffsetFormat
config.doc: When set to true, datetime formatter used for csv, json and xml will support zone offsets that have seconds in it. e.g. LA timezone offset prior to 1883 was -07:52:58. When this flag is not set we lose seconds information.

config.name: spark.sql.artifact.copyFromLocalToFs.allowDestLocal
config.doc: Allow the `copyFromLocalToFs` destination to be a local file system path on the driver node. This lets the caller overwrite arbitrary files on the driver node, so it should only be enabled for testing purposes. This is a static conf: it can only be set when starting the driver, and not from a session.

config.name: spark.sql.legacy.decimal.retainFractionDigitsOnTruncate
config.doc: When set to true, we will try to retain the fraction digits first rather than integral digits as prior Spark 4.0, when getting a least common type between decimal types, and the result decimal precision exceeds the max precision.

config.name: spark.sql.stackTracesInDataFrameContext
config.doc: The number of non-Spark stack traces in the captured DataFrame query context.

config.name: spark.sql.dataFrameQueryContext.enabled
config.doc: Enable the DataFrame query context. This feature is enabled by default, but has a non-trivial performance overhead because of the stack trace collection.

config.name: spark.sql.legacy.javaCharsets
config.doc: When set to true, the functions like `encode()` can use charsets from JDK while encoding or decoding string values. If it is false, such functions support only one of the charsets: 'US-ASCII', 'ISO-8859-1', 'UTF-8', 'UTF-16BE', 'UTF-16LE', 'UTF-16', 'UTF-32'.

config.name: spark.sql.legacy.codingErrorAction
config.doc: When set to true, encode/decode functions replace unmappable characters with mojibake instead of reporting coding errors.

config.name: spark.sql.legacy.earlyEvalCurrentTime
config.doc: When set to true, evaluation and constant folding will happen for now() and current_timestamp() expressions before finish analysis phase. This flag will allow a bit more liberal syntax but it will sacrifice correctness - Results of now() and current_timestamp() can be different for different operations in a single query.

config.name: spark.sql.legacy.bangEqualsNot
config.doc: When set to true, '!' is a lexical equivalent for 'NOT'. That is '!' can be used outside of the documented prefix usage in a logical expression. Examples are: `expr ! IN (1, 2)` and `expr ! BETWEEN 1 AND 2`, but also `IF ! EXISTS`.

config.name: spark.sql.orderingAwareLimitOffset
config.doc: When set to true, a local sort will be inserted between GlobalLimitExec and single-partition ShuffleExchangeExec, if the underlying plan produces sorted data. This is because shuffle reader in Spark fetches shuffle blocks in a random order and can not preserve the data ordering, while LIMIT/OFFSET must preserve ordering.

config.name: spark.sql.lazySetOperatorOutput.enabled
config.doc: When set to true, Except/Intersect/Union operator's output will be a lazy val. It is a performance optimization for querires with a large number of stacked set operators. This is because of rules like WidenSetOperationTypes that traverse the logical plan tree and call output on each Except/Intersect/Union node. Such traversal has quadratic complexity: O(number_of_nodes * (1 + 2 + 3 + ... + number_of_nodes)).

config.name: spark.sql.legacy.parseQueryWithoutEof
config.doc: When set to true, ParserInterface#parseQuery(...) is going to use base `query` grammar term without EOF resulting in some queries (like `SELECT 1 UNION SELECT 2`) to be parsed incorrectly - `UNION` will be treated as an alias, and the rest of SQL input will be thrown away.

config.name: spark.sql.legacy.dataFrameWriterV2IgnorePathOption
config.doc: When set to true, DataFrameWriterV2 ignores the 'path' option and always write data to the default table location.

config.name: spark.sql.runCollationTypeCastsBeforeAliasAssignment.enabled
config.doc: When set to true, rules like ResolveAliases or ResolveAggregateFunctions will run CollationTypeCasts before alias assignment. This is necessary for correct alias generation.

config.name: spark.sql.extensions.test.loadFromCp
config.doc: Flag that determines if we should load extensions from the classpath using the SparkSessionExtensionsProvider mechanism. This is a test only flag.

config.name: spark.sql.shuffleExchange.maxThreadThreshold
config.doc: The maximum degree of parallelism for doing preparation of shuffle exchange, which includes subquery execution, file listing, etc.

config.name: spark.sql.resultQueryStage.maxThreadThreshold
config.doc: The maximum degree of parallelism to execute ResultQueryStageExec in AQE

config.name: spark.python.sql.dataFrameDebugging.enabled
config.doc: Enable the DataFrame debugging. This feature is enabled by default, but has a non-trivial performance overhead because of the stack trace collection.

config.name: spark.connect.grpc.binding.address
config.doc: The address for Spark Connect server to bind.

config.name: spark.connect.grpc.port.maxRetries
config.doc: The max port retry attempts for the gRPC server binding.By default, it's set to 0, and the server will fail fast in case of port conflicts.

config.name: spark.connect.session.manager.defaultSessionTimeout
config.doc: Timeout after which sessions without any new incoming RPC will be removed. Setting it to -1 indicates that sessions should be kept forever.

config.name: spark.connect.session.manager.closedSessionsTombstonesSize
config.doc: Maximum size of the cache of sessions after which sessions that did not receive any requests will be removed.

config.name: spark.connect.session.manager.maintenanceInterval
config.doc: Interval at which session manager will search for expired sessions to remove.

config.name: spark.connect.ml.backend.classes
config.doc: |Comma separated list of classes that implement the trait |org.apache.spark.sql.connect.plugin.MLBackendPlugin to replace the |specified Spark ML operators with a backend-specific implementation. |

config.name: spark.sql.connect.enrichError.enabled
config.doc: |When true, it enriches errors with full exception messages and optionally server-side |stacktrace on the client side via an additional RPC. |

config.name: spark.sql.connect.serverStacktrace.enabled
config.doc: When true, it sets the server-side stacktrace in the user-facing Spark exception.

config.name: spark.connect.grpc.maxMetadataSize
config.doc: Sets the maximum size of metadata fields. For instance, it restricts metadata fields in `ErrorInfo`.

config.name: spark.connect.progress.reportInterval
config.doc: The interval at which the progress of a query is reported to the client. If the value is set to a negative value the progress reports will be disabled.

config.name: spark.connect.session.planCache.maxSize
config.doc: Sets the maximum number of cached resolved logical plans in Spark Connect Session. If set to a value less or equal than zero will disable the plan cache.

config.name: spark.connect.session.planCache.enabled
config.doc: When true, the cache of resolved logical plans is enabled if '${CONNECT_SESSION_PLAN_CACHE_SIZE.key}' is greater than zero. When false, the cache is disabled even if '${CONNECT_SESSION_PLAN_CACHE_SIZE.key}' is greater than zero. The caching is best-effort and not guaranteed.

config.name: spark.connect.authenticate.token
config.doc: A pre-shared token that will be used to authenticate clients. This secret must be passed as a bearer token by for clients to connect.

config.name: spark.sql.hive.convertInsertingUnpartitionedTable
config.doc: When set to true, and `spark.sql.hive.convertMetastoreParquet` or `spark.sql.hive.convertMetastoreOrc` is true, the built-in ORC/Parquet writer is usedto process inserting into unpartitioned ORC/Parquet tables created by using the HiveSQL syntax.

config.name: spark.history.fs.eventLog.rolling.onDemandLoadEnabled
config.doc: Whether to look up rolling event log locations on demand manner before listing files.

config.name: spark.history.fs.numCompactThreads
config.doc: Number of threads that will be used by history server to compact event logs.

config.name: spark.python.unix.domain.socket.enabled
config.doc: When set to true, the Python driver uses a Unix domain socket for operations like creating or collecting a DataFrame from local data, using accumulators, and executing Python functions with PySpark such as Python UDFs. This configuration only applies to Spark Classic and Spark Connect server.

config.name: spark.python.unix.domain.socket.dir
config.doc: When specified, it uses the directory to create Unix domain socket files. Otherwise, it uses the default location of the temporary directory set in 'java.io.tmpdir' property. This is used when ${PYTHON_UNIX_DOMAIN_SOCKET_ENABLED.key} is enabled.

config.name: spark.python.worker.killOnIdleTimeout
config.doc: Whether Spark should terminate the Python worker process when the idle timeout (as defined by $PYTHON_WORKER_IDLE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS_KEY) is reached. If enabled, Spark will terminate the Python worker process in addition to logging the status.

config.name: spark.python.worker.tracebackDumpIntervalSeconds
config.doc: The interval (in seconds) for Python workers to dump their tracebacks. If it's positive, the Python worker will periodically dump the traceback into its `stderr`. The default is `0` that means it is disabled.

config.name: spark.python.factory.idleWorkerMaxPoolSize
config.doc: Maximum number of idle Python workers to keep. If unset, the number is unbounded. If set to a positive integer N, at most N idle workers are retained; least-recently used workers are evicted first.

config.name: spark.python.daemon.killWorkerOnFlushFailure
config.doc: When enabled, exceptions raised during output flush operations in the Python worker managed under Python daemon are not caught, causing the worker to terminate with the exception. This allows Spark to detect the failure and launch a new worker and retry the task. When disabled, flush exceptions are caught and logged but the worker continues, which could cause the worker to get stuck due to protocol mismatch.

config.name: spark.eventLog.excludedPatterns
config.doc: Specifies comma-separated event names to be excluded from the event logs.

config.name: spark.executor.isolatedSessionCache.size
config.doc: Maximum number of isolated sessions to cache in the executor. Each cached session maintains its own classloader for artifact isolation.

config.name: spark.memory.unmanagedMemoryPollingInterval
config.doc: Interval for polling unmanaged memory users to track their memory usage. Unmanaged memory users are components that manage their own memory outside of Spark's core memory management, such as RocksDB for Streaming State Store. Setting this to 0 disables unmanaged memory polling.

config.name: spark.driver.metrics.pollingInterval
config.doc: How often to collect driver metrics (in milliseconds). If unset, the polling is done at the executor heartbeat interval. If set, the polling is done at this interval.

config.name: spark.shuffle.spill.maxSizeInBytesForSpillThreshold
config.doc: The maximum in memory size in bytes before forcing the shuffle sorter to spill. By default it is Long.MAX_VALUE, which means we never force the sorter to spill, until we reach some limitations, like the max page size limitation for the pointer array in the sorter.

config.name: spark.io.compression.zstd.strategy
config.doc: Compression strategy for Zstd compression codec. The higher the value is, the more complex it becomes, usually resulting stronger but slower compression or higher CPU cost.

config.name: spark.submit.callSystemExitOnMainExit
config.doc: If true, SparkSubmit will call System.exit() to initiate JVM shutdown once the user's main method has exited. This can be useful in cases where non-daemon JVM threads might otherwise prevent the JVM from shutting down on its own.

config.name: spark.driver.log.redirectConsoleOutputs
config.doc: Comma-separated list of the console output kind for driver that needs to redirect to logging system. Supported values are `stdout`, `stderr`. It only takes affect when `${PLUGINS.key}` is configured with `org.apache.spark.deploy.RedirectConsolePlugin`.

config.name: spark.executor.logs.redirectConsoleOutputs
config.doc: Comma-separated list of the console output kind for executor that needs to redirect to logging system. Supported values are `stdout`, `stderr`. It only takes affect when `${PLUGINS.key}` is configured with `org.apache.spark.deploy.RedirectConsolePlugin`.

config.name: spark.kubernetes.executor.useDriverPodIP
config.doc: If true, executor pods use Driver pod IP directly instead of Driver Service.

config.name: spark.kubernetes.driver.pod.excludedFeatureSteps
config.doc: Class names to exclude from driver pod feature steps. Comma separated.

config.name: spark.kubernetes.executor.pod.excludedFeatureSteps
config.doc: Class name to exclude from executor pod feature steps. Comma separated.

config.name: spark.kubernetes.allocation.maximum
config.doc: The maximum number of executor pods to try to create during the whole job lifecycle.

config.name: spark.kubernetes.executor.deletedExecutorsCacheTimeout
config.doc: Time-to-live (TTL) value for the cache for deleted executors

config.name: spark.kubernetes.executor.terminationGracePeriodSeconds
config.doc: Time to wait for graceful termination of executor pods.

config.name: spark.kubernetes.allocation.maxPendingPodsPerRp
config.doc: Maximum number of pending PODs allowed per resource profile ID during executor allocation. This provides finer-grained control over pending pods by limiting them per resource profile rather than globally. When set, this limit is enforced independently for each resource profile ID.

config.name: spark.kubernetes.driver.annotateExitException
config.doc: If set to true, Spark will store the exit exception failed applications in the Kubernetes API server using the $EXIT_EXCEPTION_ANNOTATION annotation. Note that the annotation is visible to anyone who can get the driver pod. The parts of the exit exception matching `spark.redaction.string.regex` are redacted.

config.name: spark.sql.analyzer.preferColumnOverLcaInArrayIndex
config.doc: When true, prefer the column from the underlying relation over the lateral column alias reference with the same name (see SPARK-53734).

config.name: spark.sql.analyzer.dontDeduplicateExpressionIfExprIdInOutput
config.doc: DeduplicateRelations shouldn't remap expressions to new ExprIds if old ExprId still exists in output.

config.name: spark.sql.analyzer.unionIsResolvedWhenDuplicatesPerChildResolved
config.doc: When true, union should only be resolved once there are no duplicate attributes in each branch.

config.name: spark.sql.analyzer.uniqueNecessaryMetadataColumns
config.doc: When this conf is enabled, AddMetadataColumns rule should only add necessary metadata columns and only if those columns are not already present in the project list.

config.name: spark.sql.legacy.blockCreateTempTableUsingProvider
config.doc: If enabled, we fail legacy CREATE TEMPORARY TABLE ... USING provider during parsing.

config.name: spark.sql.analyzer.singlePassResolver.enabledTentatively
config.doc: When true, use the single-pass Resolver instead of the fixed-point Analyzer only if a SQL query or a DataFrame program is fully supported by the single-pass Analyzer. This is an alternative Analyzer framework, which resolves the parsed logical plan in a single post-order traversal. It uses ExpressionResolver to resolve expressions and NameScope to control the visibility of names. In contrast to the current fixed-point framework, subsequent in-tree traversals are disallowed. Most of the fixed-point Analyzer code is reused in the form of specific node transformation functions (AliasResolution.resolve, FunctionResolution.resolveFunction, etc).This feature is currently under development.

config.name: spark.sql.analyzer.singlePassResolver.dualRunSampleRate
config.doc: Represents the rate of queries that will be run in both fixed-point and single-pass mode (dual run). It should be taken into account that the sample rate is not a strict percentage (in tests we don't sample). It is determined whether query should be run in dual run mode by comparing a random value with the value of this flag.

config.name: spark.sql.analyzer.singlePassResolver.exposeResolverGuardFailure
config.doc: When true, any failure thrown from ResolverGuard will be exposed as a query failure. Otherwise we just assume that the ResolverGuard returned false and the query is not supported by the single-pass Analyzer. This is important to make dual-runs unnoticeable in production.

config.name: spark.sql.analyzer.singlePassResolver.preventUsingAliasesFromNonDirectChildren
config.doc: When true, in Sort/Having/Filter expressions allow replacing of these expressions only with semantically equal aliased expressions from direct children. This is necessary in order to stay compatible with fixed-point, but the functionality and correctness remain the same. Because enabling this case would break some cases that are supported in single-pass but not in fixed-point, this flag should only be used to hide false positive logical plan mismatches during testing.

config.name: spark.sql.analyzer.singlePassResolver.throwFromResolverGuard
config.doc: When set to true, ResolverGuard will throw a descriptive error on unsupported features.

config.name: spark.sql.analyzer.singlePassResolver.runExtendedResolutionChecks
config.doc: When true, run `extendedResolutionChecks` after the main analysis.

config.name: spark.sql.analyzer.singlePassResolver.runHeavyExtendedResolutionChecks
config.doc: When true, run heavy `extendedResolutionChecks` after the main analysis. Otherwise skip them. Heavy check either involves a network call changing external persistent storage, or changes a global state. For example, `ViewSyncSchemaToMetaStore` calls alter table.

config.name: spark.sql.optimizer.preserveAliasMetadataWhenCollapsingProjects
config.doc: When true, make sure to explicitly copy the metadata of the aliases from lower project list.

config.name: spark.sql.nameResolutionLog.level
config.doc: Configures the log level for logging the name resolution in the single-pass bottom-up Resolver. The value can be ${VALID_LOG_LEVELS.mkString()}.

config.name: spark.sql.geospatial.enabled
config.doc: When true, enables geospatial types (GEOGRAPHY/GEOMETRY) and ST functions.

config.name: spark.sql.shuffle.orderIndependentChecksum.enabled
config.doc: Whether to calculate order independent checksum for the shuffle data or not. If enabled, Spark will calculate a checksum that is independent of the input row order for each mapper and returns the checksums from executors to driver. This is different from the checksum computed when spark.shuffle.checksum.enabled is enabled which is sensitive to shuffle data ordering to detect file corruption. While this checksum will be the same even if the shuffle row order changes and it is used to detect whether different task attempts of the same partition produce different output data or not (same set of keyValue pairs). In case the output data has changed across retries, Spark will need to retry all tasks of the consumer stages to avoid correctness issues.

config.name: spark.sql.shuffle.orderIndependentChecksum.enableFullRetryOnMismatch
config.doc: Whether to retry all tasks of a consumer stage when we detect checksum mismatches with its producer stages.

config.name: spark.sql.adaptive.streaming.stateless.enabled
config.doc: When true, enable adaptive query execution for stateless streaming query. To enable this config, `spark.sql.adaptive.enabled` needs to be also enabled.

config.name: spark.sql.collation.schemaLevel.enabled
config.doc: Schema level collations feature is under development and its use should be done under this feature flag. The feature allows setting default collation for all underlying objects within that schema, except the ones that were previously created.An object with an explicitly set collation will not inherit the collation from the schema.

config.name: spark.sql.legacy.collationAwareHashFunctions
config.doc: Enables collation aware hashing (legacy behavior) for collated strings in Murmur3Hash and XxHash64 user-facing expressions.

config.name: spark.sql.mapZipWithUsesJavaCollections
config.doc: When true, the `map_zip_with` function uses Java collections instead of Scala collections. This is useful for avoiding NaN equality issues.

config.name: spark.sql.parser.parserDfaCacheFlushRatio
config.doc: Like `spark.sql.parser.parserDfaCacheFlushThreshold`, but uses a threshold that is a |linear function of the memory allocated to the driver process. Represents the percentage |of the driver memory that the DFA cache can consume before it is flushed. | |Estimates the memory used by the DFA cache, assuming each state consumes |`AbstractParser.BYTES_PER_DFA_STATE` bytes. If this value exceeds the product of the |driver memory with the config value (interpreted as a percentage), the cache is flushed. | |Active values should be in the range 0-100, and a negative value disables the feature. |If both this config and `spark.sql.parser.parserDfaCacheFlushThreshold` are set, the |cache is flushed if either condition is met. |Requires `spark.sql.parser.manageParserCaches` to be true to take effect. |

config.name: spark.sql.parser.parserDfaCacheFlushThreshold
config.doc: When positive, release ANTLR caches after parsing a SQL query when the number of states |in the DFA cache exceeds the value of the config. DFA states empirically consume about |`AbstractParser.BYTES_PER_DFA_STATE` bytes of memory each. | |ANTLR parsers retain a DFA cache designed to speed up parsing future input. However, |there is no limit to how large this cache can become. Parsing large SQL statements can |lead to an accumulation of objects in the cache that are unlikely to be reused, causing |high GC overhead and eventually OOMs. | |If this config is set to a negative value, it is ignored. |If both this config and `spark.sql.parser.parserDfaCacheFlushRatio` are set, the |cache is flushed if either condition is met. |Requires `spark.sql.parser.manageParserCaches` to be true to take effect. | |Can significantly slow down parsing in exchange for better memory stability. |

config.name: spark.sql.parser.manageParserCaches
config.doc: When true, we install our own ANTLR caches to manage memory usage. When false, we use the |default ANTLR caches. Dependency for |`spark.sql.parser.parserDfaCacheFlushThreshold`.

config.name: spark.sql.legacy.parquet.returnNullStructIfAllFieldsMissing
config.doc: When true, if all requested fields of a struct are missing in a parquet file, assume the struct is always null, even if other fields are present. The default behavior is to fetch and read an arbitrary non-requested field present in the file to determine struct nullness. If enabled, schema pruning may cause non-null structs to be read as null.

config.name: spark.sql.parquet.enableNullTypeVectorizedReader
config.doc: Enables vectorized Parquet reader support for NullType columns.

config.name: spark.sql.parquet.variant.annotateLogicalType.enabled
config.doc: When enabled, Spark annotates the variant groups written to Parquet as the parquet variant logical type.

config.name: spark.sql.parquet.ignoreVariantAnnotation
config.doc: When true, ignore the variant logical type annotation and treat the Parquet column in the same way as the underlying struct type

config.name: spark.sql.maxBroadcastTableSize
config.doc: The maximum table size in bytes that can be broadcast in broadcast joins.

config.name: spark.sql.dataSource.alwaysCreateV2Predicate
config.doc: When true, the v2 push-down framework always wraps the expression that returns boolean type with a v2 Predicate so that it can be pushed down.

config.name: spark.sql.optimizer.datasourceV2JoinPushdown
config.doc: When this config is set to true, join is tried to be pushed downfor DSv2 data sources in V2ScanRelationPushdown optimization rule.

config.name: spark.sql.optimizer.datasourceV2ExprFolding
config.doc: When this config is set to true, do safe constant folding for the expressions before translation and pushdown.

config.name: spark.sql.analyzer.sqlFunctionResolution.applyConfOverrides
config.doc: When true, applies the conf overrides for certain feature flags during the resolution of user-defined sql table valued functions, consistent with view resolution.

config.name: spark.sql.codegen.logLevel
config.doc: Configures the log level for logging of codegen. The value can be ${VALID_LOG_LEVELS.mkString()}.

config.name: spark.sql.streaming.stateStore.maintenanceShutdownTimeout
config.doc: Timeout in seconds for maintenance pool operations to complete on shutdown

config.name: spark.sql.streaming.stateStore.maintenanceProcessingTimeout
config.doc: Timeout in seconds to wait for maintenance to process this partition.

config.name: spark.sql.streaming.stateStore.numStateStoreInstanceMetricsToReport
config.doc: Number of state store instance metrics included in streaming query progress messages per stateful operator. Instance metrics are selected based on metric-specific ordering to minimize noise in the progress report.

config.name: spark.sql.streaming.stateStore.multiplierForMinVersionDiffToLog
config.doc: Determines the version threshold for logging warnings when a state store falls behind. The coordinator logs a warning when the store's uploaded snapshot version trails the query's latest version by the configured number of deltas needed to create a snapshot, times this multiplier.

config.name: spark.sql.streaming.stateStore.multiplierForMinTimeDiffToLog
config.doc: Determines the time threshold for logging warnings when a state store falls behind. The coordinator logs a warning when the store's uploaded snapshot timestamp trails the current time by the configured maintenance interval, times this multiplier.

config.name: spark.sql.streaming.stateStore.coordinatorReportSnapshotUploadLag
config.doc: When enabled, the state store coordinator will report state stores whose snapshot have not been uploaded for some time. See the conf snapshotLagReportInterval for the minimum time between reports, and the conf multiplierForMinVersionDiffToLog and multiplierForMinTimeDiffToLog for the logging thresholds.

config.name: spark.sql.streaming.stateStore.snapshotLagReportInterval
config.doc: The minimum amount of time between the state store coordinator's reports on state store instances trailing behind in snapshot uploads.

config.name: spark.sql.streaming.stateStore.maxLaggingStoresToReport
config.doc: Maximum number of state stores the coordinator will report as trailing in snapshot uploads. Stores are selected based on the most lagging behind in snapshot version.

config.name: spark.sql.streaming.internal.stateStore.partitions
config.doc: WARN: This config is used internally and is not intended to be user-facing. This config can be removed without support of compatibility in any time. DO NOT USE THIS CONFIG DIRECTLY AND USE THE CONFIG `spark.sql.shuffle.partitions`. The default number of partitions to use when shuffling data for stateful operations. If not specified, this config picks up the value of `spark.sql.shuffle.partitions`. Note: For structured streaming, this configuration cannot be changed between query restarts from the same checkpoint location.

config.name: spark.sql.streaming.stateStore.maxVersionsToDeletePerMaintenance
config.doc: The maximum number of versions to delete per maintenance operation. By default, this value is set to -1, which means no limit. Note that, currently this is only supported for the RocksDB state store provider.

config.name: spark.sql.streaming.verifyCheckpointDirectoryEmptyOnStart
config.doc: When true, verifies that the checkpoint directory (offsets, state, commits) is empty when first starting a streaming query. This prevents prevents sharing checkpoint directories between different queries.

config.name: spark.sql.streaming.stateStore.unloadOnCommit
config.doc: When true, Spark will synchronously run maintenance and then close each StateStore instance on task completion. This removes the overhead of keeping every StateStore loaded indefinitely, at the cost of having to reload each StateStore every batch. Stateful applications that are failing due to resource exhaustion or that use dynamic allocation may benefit from enabling this.

config.name: spark.sql.streaming.stateStore.commitValidation.enabled
config.doc: When true, Spark will validate that all StateStore instances have committed for stateful streaming queries using foreachBatch. This helps detect cases where user-defined functions in foreachBatch (e.g., show(), limit()) don't process all partitions, which can lead to incorrect results. The validation only applies to foreachBatch sinks without global aggregates or limits.

config.name: spark.sql.streaming.realTimeMode.minBatchDuration
config.doc: The minimum long-running batch duration in milliseconds for real-time mode.

config.name: spark.sql.streaming.realTimeMode.allowlistCheck
config.doc: Whether to check all operators, sinks used in real-time mode are in the allowlist.

config.name: spark.sql.streaming.checkpoint.fileChecksum.enabled
config.doc: When true, checksum would be generated and verified for checkpoint files. This is used to detect file corruption. This is only enabled when STATE_STORE_CHECKPOINT_FORMAT_VERSION >= 2

config.name: spark.sql.streaming.checkpoint.fileChecksum.skipCreationIfFileMissingChecksum
config.doc: When true, if a microbatch is retried, if a file already exists but its checksum file does not exist, the file checksum will not be created. This is useful for compatibility with files created before file checksums were enabled.

config.name: spark.sql.windowExec.buffer.spill.size.threshold
config.doc: Threshold for size of rows to be spilled by window operator

config.name: spark.sql.sessionWindow.buffer.spill.size.threshold
config.doc: Threshold for size of rows to be spilled by window operator. Note that the buffer is used only for the query Spark cannot apply aggregations on determining session window.

config.name: spark.sql.classic.shuffleDependency.fileCleanup.enabled
config.doc: When enabled, shuffle files will be cleaned up at the end of classic SQL executions. Note that this cleanup may cause stage retries and regenerate shuffle files if the same dataframe reference is executed again.

config.name: spark.sql.connect.shuffleDependency.fileCleanup.enabled
config.doc: When enabled, shuffle files will be cleaned up at the end of Spark Connect SQL executions.

config.name: spark.sql.sortMergeJoinExec.buffer.spill.size.threshold
config.doc: Threshold for size of rows to be spilled by sort merge join operator

config.name: spark.sql.cartesianProductExec.buffer.spill.size.threshold
config.doc: Threshold for size of rows to be spilled by cartesian product operator

config.name: spark.sql.execution.pyspark.binaryAsBytes
config.doc: When true, BinaryType is consistently mapped to bytes in PySpark. When false, restores the PySpark behavior before 4.1.0. Before 4.1.0, BinaryType is mapped to bytearray for regular UDF and UDTF without Arrow optimization, DataFrame APIs (both Spark Classic and Spark Connect), and data sources; BinaryType is mapped to bytes for Arrow-optimized UDF and UDTF with legacy pandas conversion.

config.name: spark.sql.execution.pyspark.udf.killOnIdleTimeout
config.doc: Same as ${Python.PYTHON_WORKER_KILL_ON_IDLE_TIMEOUT.key} for Python execution with DataFrame and SQL. It can change during runtime.

config.name: spark.sql.execution.pyspark.udf.tracebackDumpIntervalSeconds
config.doc: Same as ${Python.PYTHON_WORKER_TRACEBACK_DUMP_INTERVAL_SECONDS.key} for Python execution with DataFrame and SQL. It can change during runtime.

config.name: spark.sql.execution.pyspark.udf.daemonKillWorkerOnFlushFailure
config.doc: Same as ${Python.PYTHON_DAEMON_KILL_WORKER_ON_FLUSH_FAILURE.key} for Python execution with DataFrame and SQL. It can change during runtime.

config.name: spark.sql.pyspark.worker.logging.enabled
config.doc: When set to true, this configuration enables comprehensive logging within Python worker processes that execute User-Defined Functions (UDFs), User-Defined Table Functions (UDTFs), and other Python-based operations in Spark SQL.

config.name: spark.sql.execution.arrow.maxRecordsPerOutputBatch
config.doc: When using Apache Arrow, limit the maximum number of records that can be output in a single ArrowRecordBatch to the downstream operator. If set to zero or negative there is no limit. Note that the complete ArrowRecordBatch is actually created but the number of records is limited when sending it to the downstream operator. This is used to avoid large batches being sent to the downstream operator including the columnar-based operator implemented by third-party libraries. applyInPandasWithState, Arrow Python UDTFs and Arrow Python UDFs that take columnar input directly ignore this config.

config.name: spark.sql.execution.arrow.maxBytesPerOutputBatch
config.doc: When using Apache Arrow, limit the maximum bytes that can be output in a single ArrowRecordBatch to the downstream operator. If set to zero or negative there is no limit. Note that the complete ArrowRecordBatch is actually created but the number of bytes is limited when sending it to the downstream operator. This is used to avoid large batches being sent to the downstream operator including the columnar-based operator implemented by third-party libraries. Spark will try to create batches with the size equal or less than this value. Normally it should not happen, but if in extreme case that even one record is still larger than this value, Spark will create a batch with one record. applyInPandasWithState, Arrow Python UDTFs and Arrow Python UDFs that take columnar input directly ignore this config.

config.name: spark.sql.execution.arrow.compression.codec
config.doc: Compression codec used to compress Arrow IPC data when transferring data between JVM and Python processes (e.g., toPandas, toArrow). This can significantly reduce memory usage and network bandwidth when transferring large datasets. Supported codecs: 'none' (no compression), 'zstd' (Zstandard), 'lz4' (LZ4). Note that compression may add CPU overhead but can provide substantial memory savings especially for datasets with high compression ratios.

config.name: spark.sql.execution.arrow.compression.zstd.level
config.doc: Compression level for Zstandard (zstd) codec when compressing Arrow IPC data. This config is only used when spark.sql.execution.arrow.compression.codec is set to 'zstd'. Negative values provide ultra-fast compression with lower compression ratios. Positive values provide normal to maximum compression, with higher values giving better compression but slower speed. The default value 3 provides a good balance between compression speed and compression ratio.

config.name: spark.sql.execution.arrow.transformWithStateInPySpark.maxStateRecordsPerBatch
config.doc: When using TransformWithState in PySpark (both Python Row and Pandas), limit the maximum number of state records that can be written to a single ArrowRecordBatch in memory.

config.name: spark.sql.execution.arrow.pyspark.validateSchema.enabled
config.doc: When true, validate the schema of Arrow batches returned by mapInArrow, mapInPandas and DataSource against the expected schema to ensure that they are compatible.

config.name: spark.sql.execution.pythonUDF.arrow.legacy.fallbackOnUDT
config.doc: When true, Arrow-optimized Python UDF will fallback to the regular UDF when its input or output is UDT.

config.name: spark.sql.execution.pythonUDF.pandas.intToDecimalCoercionEnabled
config.doc: When true, convert int to Decimal python objects before converting Pandas.Series to Arrow array during serialization.Disabled by default, impacts performance.

config.name: spark.sql.legacy.execution.pythonUDTF.pandas.conversion.enabled
config.doc: When true and ${PYTHON_TABLE_UDF_ARROW_ENABLED.key} is enabled, extra pandas conversion happens during (de)serialization between JVM and Python workers. This matters especially when the produced output has a schema different from specified schema, resulting in a different type coercion.

config.name: spark.sql.legacy.execution.pythonUDF.pandas.conversion.enabled
config.doc: When true and ${PYTHON_UDF_ARROW_ENABLED.key} is enabled, matches the default Arrow Python UDF behavior before 4.1.0. With this behavior, extrapandas conversion happens during (de)serialization between JVM and Python workers. This matters especially when the produced output has a schema different from specified schema, resulting in a different type coercion.

config.name: spark.sql.scripting.continueHandlerEnabled
config.doc: SQL Scripting CONTINUE HANDLER feature enables CONTINUE exception handlers which are essential for cursor iteration with NOT FOUND conditions.

config.name: spark.sql.legacy.consecutiveStringLiterals.enabled
config.doc: When true, consecutive string literals separated by double quotes (e.g. 'a''b') will be parsed as concatenated strings. This preserves pre-Spark 4.0 behavior where'a''b' would be parsed as 'ab' instead of 'a'b'.

config.name: spark.sql.legacy.identifierClause
config.doc: When set to false, IDENTIFIER('literal') is resolved to an identifier at parse time anywhere identifiers can occur. When set to true, only the legacy IDENTIFIER(constantExpr) clause is allowed, which evaluates the expression at analysis and is limited to a narrow subset of scenarios.

config.name: spark.sql.cteRecursionLevelLimit
config.doc: Maximum level of recursion that is allowed while executing a recursive CTE definition.If a query does not get exhausted before reaching this limit it fails. Use -1 for unlimited.

config.name: spark.sql.cteRecursionRowLimit
config.doc: Maximum number of rows that can be returned when executing a recursive CTE definition.If a query does not get exhausted before reaching this limit it fails. Use -1 for unlimited.

config.name: spark.sql.cteRecursionAnchorRowsLimitToConvertToLocalRelation
config.doc: Maximum number of rows that the anchor in a recursive CTE can return for it to beconverted to a localRelation.

config.name: spark.sql.legacy.parameterSubstitution.constantsOnly
config.doc: When true, limits parameter substitution to constants in DML/queries only, restoring the legacy behavior where parameter markers (? or :param) are only allowed in contexts where constant literals are expected. When false (default), parameter substitution is enabled everywhere a literal is supported, allowing parameter markers in any literal context throughout SQL parsing.

config.name: spark.sql.python.filterPushdown.enabled
config.doc: When true, enable filter pushdown to Python datasource, at the cost of running Python worker one additional time during planning.

config.name: spark.sql.variant.shredding.maxSchemaWidth
config.doc: Maximum number of shredded fields to create when inferring a schema for Variant

config.name: spark.sql.variant.shredding.maxSchemaDepth
config.doc: Maximum depth in Variant value to traverse when inferring a schema. Any array/object below this depth will be shredded as a single binary.

config.name: spark.sql.variant.inferShreddingSchema
config.doc: Infer shredding schema when writing Variant columns in Parquet tables.

config.name: spark.sql.session.localRelationChunkSizeRows
config.doc: The chunk size in number of rows when splitting ChunkedCachedLocalRelation.data into batches. A new chunk is created when either spark.sql.session.localRelationChunkSizeBytes or spark.sql.session.localRelationChunkSizeRows is reached.

config.name: spark.sql.session.localRelationChunkSizeBytes
config.doc: The chunk size in bytes when splitting ChunkedCachedLocalRelation.data into batches. A new chunk is created when either spark.sql.session.localRelationChunkSizeBytes or spark.sql.session.localRelationChunkSizeRows is reached. Limited by the spark.sql.session.localRelationBatchOfChunksSizeBytes, a minimum of the two confs is used to determine the chunk size.

config.name: spark.sql.session.localRelationChunkSizeLimit
config.doc: Limit on how large a single chunk of a ChunkedCachedLocalRelation.data can be in bytes. If the limit is exceeded, an exception is thrown.

config.name: spark.sql.session.localRelationSizeLimit
config.doc: Limit on how large ChunkedCachedLocalRelation.data can be in bytes.If the limit is exceeded, an exception is thrown.

config.name: spark.sql.session.localRelationBatchOfChunksSizeBytes
config.doc: Limit on how much memory the client can use when uploading a local relation to the server. The client collects multiple local relation chunks into a single batch in memory until the limit is reached, then uploads the batch to the server. This helps reduce memory pressure on the client when dealing with very large local relations because the client does not have to materialize all chunks in memory. Limits the spark.sql.session.localRelationChunkSizeBytes, a minimum of the two confs is used to determine the chunk size.

config.name: spark.sql.unionOutputPartitioning
config.doc: When set to true, the output partitioning of UnionExec will be the same as the input partitioning if its children have same partitioning. Otherwise, it will be a default partitioning. The value is read once per physical preparation, and the decision taken with it, so the exchanges planned around a UnionExec and the decision it executes under agree. One decided to concatenate keeps reporting the default partitioning if its children come to share one afterwards.

config.name: spark.sql.cteRelationDefMaxRows.enabled
